It was the first win in the competition by a Gallagher Prem team after seven failed attempts by fellow English sides.

Tries from James Pater and Toby Thame gave Northampton a 14-0 half-time lead. Harri Millard and Mason Grady scored for Cardiff to close within two points, before George Hendy and Fraser Dingwall tries secured victory. Dowson said everyone wants to go deep in both league and cup, so the squad's depth will be used. Northampton visit Leicester in the East Midlands derby next Saturday, while Cardiff face the Sharks next.
Rugby.copy:
Northampton director of rugby Phil Dowson praised his young players for stepping up after his much-changed team defeated Cardiff 28-12 in the Investec Champions Cup. Dowson rested Henry Pollock, Tommy Freeman and Alex Coles and named Fin Smith on the bench for their European opener, with one eye on next Saturday’s East Midlands derby at Leicester.

Despite the changes, Northampton were able to finally record a first victory for a Gallagher Prem team in the competition after seven failed attempts from their fellow English sides.

Rugby.title: Five things we learned from the opening round of the Champions Cup as English sides struggle
Rugby.summary: Only one of the eight Prem entrants was successful on the first weekend of the competition
bullets: English clubs struggled in the opening round of the Investec Champions Cup, with only Northampton winning, 28-12 against Cardiff, while Gloucester secured a draw against defending champions Bordeaux-Bègles. Saracens were well beaten at Connacht, Bath lost to Montpellier, and Sale and Leicester were beaten by Glasgow and Pau respectively. Exeter performed well in Toulouse despite Rodrigue Neti's first-half red card.

Glasgow and Connacht impressed, with Sione Tuipulotu making 19 passes for the Warriors and Connacht benefiting from recruits Ciaran Frawley and Sam Gilbert. The Bulls and Stormers beat Stade Français and Bristol, though both opponents fielded weakened sides. The weekend was overshadowed by the sudden death of Lions lock Hyron Andrews on Friday, and by the tenth anniversary of Anthony Foley's death, which Munster marked with a win over Racing 92.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. The Investec Champions Cup campaign is underway with an intriguing opening round of action whetting the appetite for the season ahead.

This one-off weekend of fixtures serves only as an hors d’ouevres with the competition not resuming until after the Nations Championship in November, and the eight English clubs will have plenty to do when it picks up again.

Rugby.title: All Blacks winger ruled out for rest of 2026 as injury woes mount
Rugby.summary: Carter picked up the high-ankle injury in the act of scoring in the second half of the first Bledisloe Cup Test at Eden Park against the Wallabies.
bullets: Chiefs and All Blacks winger Leroy Carter will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign after ankle surgery. He suffered a high-ankle injury while scoring in the first Bledisloe Cup Test against the Wallabies at Eden Park, when Rob Valetini fell on his lower leg. He joins Ardie Savea, Luke Jacobson and Ruben Love on the list of injured All Blacks ruled out for the rest of the year.

Ethan Blackadder, Patrick Tuipulotu, Richie Mo'unga, Shannon Frizell and Samisoni Taukei'aho are doubts for the end-of-year tour. Mo'unga is expected to be available for the final two Tests but is uncertain for the first two, against Scotland and Wales. The All Blacks are due to name a squad of 34 to 36 players on Tuesday NZT for a four-Test tour that also includes England in London and a finals weekend match at Allianz Stadium.
Rugby.copy:
Chiefs and All Blacks winger Leroy Carter will miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign after having ankle surgery following a nasty ankle injury at Eden Park. Carter picked up the high-ankle injury in the act of scoring in the second half of the first Bledisloe Cup Test at Eden Park against the Wallabies.

The winger charged towards the line after a Peter Lakai pop pass from the base of a ruck, before Wallabies loose-forward Rob Valetini fell on Carter’s lower leg in an attempt to stop the All Black from scoring.

Rugby.title: Perspective is needed on Wallabies thrashings, but RA must learn its lessons
Rugby.summary: Let’s not tiptoe around the lessons; they are black on white, and we have now seen them out in the open.
bullets: Back-to-back heavy defeats by the All Blacks have halted the momentum of the sixth-ranked Wallabies, who had gone six games unbeaten beforehand. The article argues the margins were probable because of factors known in advance and late injury and suspension issues, with the Wallabies unable to contend with a full-strength top-three side outside the World Rugby Regulation-9 window.

The piece calls on Rugby Australia to build better relationships with overseas clubs so coach Les Kiss can pick France-based Will Skelton, Taniela Tupou and Langi Gleeson, England-based Tom Hooper, and Japan-based Mark Nawaqanitawase, Jordan Petaia, Hunter Paisami and Samu Kerevi for the ANZAC weekend Bledisloe in 2027. It also says an experienced no.10 should be selected for November, noting the Wallabies kicked only 14 times in Sydney despite 56%-44% territory.
Rugby.copy:
The momentum behind the Wallabies has taken a couple of big hits with the back-to-back wallopings by the All Blacks. A previously six-game unbeaten streak had the Wallaby faithful and even some pundits wrongly proclaiming that ‘this was the best opportunity to win back the Bledisloe in years’.

The losses and the margins of those defeats were not only possible, but probable, because of factors known well in advance and late injury/suspension issues. Let’s not tiptoe around the lessons; they are black on white, and we have now seen them out in the open.

Rugby.title: The players who staked late claims for Wales spots
Rugby.summary: Dragons, Ospreys, Scarlets and Cardiff players give Wales boss Steve Tandy plenty to mull over before he names his Nations Championship squad on Tuesday.
bullets: Wales head coach Steve Tandy names his Nations Championship squad on Tuesday, 20 October, after Welsh clubs' European matches offered late evidence. Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets won their Challenge Cup openers, while Cardiff lost at Northampton on their return to the Champions Cup. Taulupe Faletau played almost an hour on his first outing since March, and Josh Adams came off the bench after injury.

Wales face Japan, New Zealand and Australia in Cardiff, with another fixture against a southern hemisphere side at Twickenham on finals weekend. Tomos Williams is set to start at scrum-half against Japan on 7 November, with the replacement role open. Ospreys' Reuben Morgan-Williams made his first start of the season in Tbilisi, while Dragons' Aneurin Owen, uncapped at 25, was man of the match against Perpignan. Fly-half Sam Costelow came off with a hamstring injury, described as a precaution.
Rugby.copy:
Wales head coach Steve Tandy names his Nations Championship squad on Tuesday, 20 October and was given some late food for thought by the Welsh clubs in European action. Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets made winning starts in the Challenge Cup while Cardiff competed hard but lost at Northampton on their return to the top-tier Champions Cup.

Wales will face Japan, New Zealand and Australia in Cardiff before another fixture at Twickenham against a southern hemisphere opponent on finals weekend. BBC Sport Wales looks at the players who grasped their last chance to make an impression on Tandy and his staff, as opportunities run out before the 2027 World Cup.

Rugby.title: Former Wallaroos captain calls time on eight-year international career
Rugby.summary: "Wallaroo #158 and the 19th Wallaroos captain, Emily’s work ethic and passion for the jersey means she has left it in a better place."
bullets: Former Wallaroos captain Emily Chancellor has announced her retirement from international rugby after eight years. The loose-forward, 35, will make her 41st and final appearance in the WXV Global Series Test against Scotland in Canberra this weekend. She debuted against the Black Ferns in Sydney in 2018, played at the 2021 and 2025 World Cups, and became the 19th Wallaroos captain in 2025.

Chancellor will remain available for the NSW Waratahs in the Swytx Super Rugby Women's competition. She said the time was right to leave the jersey open for the next generation and that she would cheer on the Wallaroos towards the 2029 home World Cup. Rugby Australia's Director of Women's High Performance, Tim Walsh, praised her work ethic and said she had left the jersey in a better place.
Rugby.copy:
The Wallaroos will be without their former captain after the Scotland Test in Canberra this weekend, with loose-forward Emily Chancellor calling time on her international career.

Wallaroos No.158 made her debut for Australia in 2018, three years after first being introduced to the national team environment. Chancellor captained the Wallaroos for the first time in 2025, becoming the 19th ever captain of the national side.

Rugby.title: Hurricanes secure 'ever improving' All Black prop until 2029
Rugby.summary: "I’m grateful to be with this club and to be part of the Hurricanes family,” Lauaki said.
bullets: The Hurricanes and New Zealand Rugby have signed new All Blacks prop Siale Lauaki until the end of the 2029 Super Rugby Pacific season, keeping him in New Zealand for the 2029 British and Irish Lions tour. The 23-year-old featured in three midweek matches on the All Blacks' tour of South Africa, making his tour debut against the Stormers in Cape Town.

Lauaki made his Hurricanes debut in 2024 against the Fijian Drua and has won two national titles with Wellington. Head coach Clark Laidlaw said the prop can play both sides of the scrum and adds consistency to a front row that includes Pasilio Tosi, Tyrel Lomax and Xavier Numia. Lauaki said he was grateful to a club that has given him many opportunities.
Rugby.copy:
The Hurricanes and New Zealand Rugby have secured the long-term services of new All Black prop Siale Lauaki. Lauaki has signed a deal until the end of the 2029 Super Rugby Pacific season, keeping him in New Zealand for the 2029 British and Irish Lions tour.

Lauaki was named in the All Blacks‘ 44-man squad to tour South Africa and featured on three occasions during the midweek matches. The prop made his All Blacks tour debut against the Stormers in Cape Town.

Rugby.title: Whitney Hansen: 'Six months ago we would have left 60 points out there'
Rugby.summary: Tuliau-Tua’a's four try-second half was proof of the system that Hansen is building, and how players out of the Farah Palmer Cup and Super Rugby Aupiki are being readied for the international game.
bullets: The Black Ferns beat France 81-12 in the first of three Tests at FMG Stadium Waikato in Hamilton, leading 43-0 at half-time. Maia Joseph scored the opening try and Shyrah Tuliau-Tua'a scored four in the second half, while France replied only in the 60th minute through left-winger Léa Murie.

Head coach Whitney Hansen said her side was clinical, adding that six months ago they would have left 50 to 60 points unscored. She warned that the team was too passive in some collisions and expects a strong French response in Whangarei next weekend. Hansen has now won seven of her eight Tests in charge, and she highlighted the growth of young leaders such as Amarante Sititi, Braxton Sorensen-McGee and Tuliau-Tua'a in Ruahei Demant's recent absence.
Rugby.copy:
Black Ferns head coach Whitney Hansen has given credit to her team for their clinical performance against France, where they piled on the points at FMG Stadium Waikato in Hamilton.

Hansen’s side claimed an 81-12 victory in the first Test of three against France, dominating from the first whistle. Black Ferns halfback Maia Joseph was the first to cross on a sunny afternoon in Hamilton, before backing it up six minutes later.

Rugby.title: Northampton beat Cardiff for first English win in Champions Cup
Rugby.summary: Northampton edge to a nervy Champions Cup pool win against tenacious Cardiff at Franklin's Gardens.
bullets: Northampton became the only English side to win in the opening round of the Champions Cup, beating Cardiff 28-12 in Pool Four at Franklin's Gardens. They led 14-0 at half-time through tries from James Pater and Toby Thame. Harri Millard and Mason Grady narrowed the gap to two points, before George Hendy and Fraser Dingwall scored, though without securing a bonus point.

It was a difficult opening weekend for Prem clubs, with Gloucester drawing against champions Bordeaux-Begles and six other English sides losing. Cardiff, back in the top tier after two seasons in the Challenge Cup, rested several players but gave Taulupe Faletau and Josh Adams their first appearances of the season. Northampton visit Stade Francais in December, then Montpellier in January, before hosting Bulls. Cardiff host Bath in December.
Rugby.copy:
Northampton became the only English side to win in the opening round of the Champions Cup by battling past Cardiff. Saints, quarter-finalists last season, scored four tries at Franklin's Gardens in a nervy Pool Four encounter.

The English champions led 14-0 at half-time thanks to efforts in tricky conditions by James Pater and Toby Thame. Tenacious Cardiff struck back through Harri Millard and Mason Grady to make it a two-point game in the final quarter.

Rugby.title: India Women records best-ever finish in Asian Rugby Sevens Series second leg
Rugby.summary: India Women records best-ever finish in Asian Rugby Sevens Series second leg Sportstar
bullets: The Indian women's rugby sevens team recorded its best performance at the Asian Rugby Sevens Series by finishing fifth in the second leg of the 2026 edition in Colombo, Sri Lanka, on Sunday 18 October. Captain Shikha Yadav and her side confirmed fifth place with a 19-12 victory over Thailand in the fifth-place classification match.

India finished second in its group behind Japan, ahead of UAE and Iran, then lost its quarter-final to Hong Kong-China before beating UAE and Thailand in classification matches. Shikha scored four tries, with Kalyani Patil and Mama Naik adding two each. Coach Paul Delport said the result, which included India's first-ever win over Thailand, showed the team can compete with established Asian sides. The men finished 11th, with one win in six matches.
Rugby.copy:
The Indian women’s rugby sevens team recorded its best performance at the Asian Rugby Sevens Series by finishing fifth in the second leg of the 2026 edition in Sri Lanka on Sunday, October 18.

Shikha Yadav and Co. confirmed its fifth place finish with a 19-12 victory over Thailand in the 5th-place classification match. It finished second in its group behind Japan, and ahead of UAE and Iran. It lost its quarterfinal Hong Kong-China, but recovered to defeat UAE and Thailand in its classification matches.

Rugby.title: Toulouse survive red card to outlast Exeter in epic as English woes continue in Champions Cup
Rugby.summary: Toulouse overcame Rodrigue Neti’s sending off, while Leicester were well beaten by Pau as only Northampton won of the Prem clubs on the opening weekend
bullets: Exeter Chiefs lost 43-40 to 14-man Toulouse in the Champions Cup despite a hat-trick from Zack Wimbush. Toulouse prop Rodrigue Neti was shown a red card for a high tackle, and Exeter led 26-24 at half-time, but Toulouse went ahead through Matias Remue's late try and Henry Slade sent a penalty wide in the final moments.

Elsewhere, Leicester lost 41-17 at Pau despite tries from Ollie Chessum on his return from injury and Archie van der Flier, with Pau securing a bonus point. Northampton became the first Gallagher Prem side to win in this season's competition, beating Cardiff 28-12 at Franklin's Gardens after seven failed attempts by English clubs, with George Hendy named man of the match.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Exeter Chiefs slipped to a 43-40 Champions Cup defeat against 14-man Toulouse rugby despite Zack Wimbush scoring a hat-trick.

A thrilling start saw Wimbush cross for the Chiefs only a minute into the match, with Henry Slade adding the extras. Ange Capuozzo soon struck for the hosts but Romain Ntamack was unable to convert before they went ahead through a penalty try.

Rugby.title: Toulouse deny Exeter famous win as Slade misses last-gasp kick for draw
Rugby.summary: Toulouse deny Exeter Chiefs a famous Champions Cup victory in France, fighting back to win a frenetic contest with 14 men following Rodrigue Neti's first-half red card.
bullets: Toulouse beat Exeter Chiefs in a Champions Cup pool game despite playing most of it with 14 men after prop Rodrigue Neti was sent off in the 16th minute for shoulder-to-head contact on Ross Vintcent. Exeter's Zack Wimbush scored a hat-trick, but Toulouse took the lead while Ben Hammersley was in the sin-bin. Henry Slade pulled a late penalty from about 40 metres wide, so Exeter took only a losing bonus point.

The first half finished 26-24 to Exeter, with eight tries and two yellow cards. Matias Remue scored twice for Toulouse, with further tries from Ange Capuozzo, Joshua Brennan, Teddy Thomas and Romain Ntamack. Wimbush started on the wing in place of the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso. Will Butt, Jack Yeandle and Stephen Varney also scored for Exeter.
Rugby.copy:
Toulouse denied Exeter Chiefs a famous Champions Cup victory in France, fighting back to win a frenetic pool game with 14 men following Rodrigue Neti's first-half red card. Exeter had the chance to force a draw but, with the clock in the red, Henry Slade missed a penalty from about 40 metres out.

Zack Wimbush, starting on the wing for Exeter in place of injured England international Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, scored a hat-trick of tries as the 2020 champions fell just short of winning a classic contest.

Rugby.title: He scored five tries but could only think of a sixth
Rugby.summary: Leicester Tigers wing Gabriel Hamer-Webb speaks to the Scrum V team about his ambitions for both club and country.
bullets: Wales wing Gabriel Hamer-Webb, 25, told the Scrum V podcast that even after scoring five tries in a game he would dwell on the one he missed. He represented England at under-20 level, began his professional career at Bath, spent time with Southland in New Zealand and scored 12 tries in 24 appearances for Cardiff without winning a Wales call-up before joining Leicester Tigers.

He made his Wales debut against Scotland in February, a defeat in Cardiff that he called "bittersweet", though the cap now hangs on his wall. Hamer-Webb was in Wales' summer squad but did not play, so he is still waiting for a second cap. He praised head coach Steve Tandy, said his confidence has returned at Leicester, and named a Premiership medal and a place at the World Cup in Australia as his goals.
Rugby.copy:
Gabriel Hamer-Webb could almost have a cigar in his hand. Reclined on a sofa at Leicester Tigers' training ground, dressed in casual sportswear, the Wales wing looks entirely at ease.

But there is an intensity to him. His large, friendly oval eyes are engaging, even as his gaze remains unwavering. He maintains eye contact, considers his answers carefully and speaks with striking precision.

Rugby.title: Struggling Quins pick up welcome Challenge Cup win
Rugby.summary: Harlequins shrug off poor form in the Prem to score a half-century of points against French side Vannes.
bullets: Harlequins opened their 2026-27 Challenge Cup campaign with a bonus-point win over French club Vannes, scoring nine tries to Vannes' three. Marcus Smith contributed 22 points from two tries and six conversions. Captain Cadan Murley and Will Evans each scored twice, with further tries from Will Hobson, Sam Riley and Jimmy Staples.

Quins are bottom of the Prem after losing all three league matches, while Vannes are bottom of the Top 14 with four defeats from four. It was Quins' first match at this stage of the competition since 2018. They have won the Challenge Cup a record-equalling three times, most recently in 2011. They host Saracens in a Prem derby next Sunday.
Rugby.copy:
Harlequins put aside their difficulties in the early weeks of the new Prem season to start their 2026-27 Challenge Cup campaign with a welcome bonus-point win over French club Vannes.

Quins are bottom of the Prem after losing all three of their matches, but they were far too strong for their visitors, clocking up nine tries. England back Marcus Smith contributed 22 points courtesy of two tries and six conversions, while there were two tries from captain Cadan Murley and Will Evans and further efforts from Will Hobson, Sam Riley and Jimmy Staples.

Rugby.title: Late tries give Pau bonus-point win over Leicester
Rugby.summary: Leicester Tigers begin their Champions Cup campaign with a 41-17 defeat by French club Pau.
bullets: Leicester Tigers began their Champions Cup campaign with a 41-17 Pool One defeat by Pau. Portugal international Rodrigo Marta scored two of the home side's five tries, and a late burst earned Pau a bonus point. Leicester's Ollie Chessum scored on his first appearance of the season after a foot injury, following a Billy Searle 50-22.

Pau scored three tries in a 20-minute spell either side of half-time, and Archie van der Flier's try cut the gap to seven points. Pau then scored 17 unanswered points, including a penalty from Axel Desperes and an interception try from Fabien Brau-Boirie. Marta is the Top 14's leading try-scorer this season with six in five appearances. Leicester's remaining pool matches are against Clermont Auvergne, Glasgow Warriors and Leinster.
Rugby.copy:
Leicester Tigers began their Champions Cup campaign with a 41-17 defeat by French club Pau. Portugal international Rodrigo Marta crossed for two of the home side's five tries, with a late burst helping them earn a bonus point from their Pool One opener.

Despite falling behind to an early Pau penalty, Leicester did well in the early exchanges, their tactical kicking game keeping them camped in their opponents' territory. Billy Searle's 50-22 put the Tigers in superb field position and they capitalised through captain Ollie Chessum, who was making his first appearance of the season after recovering from a foot injury.

Rugby.title: The Johann van Graan verdict on Bath's shock loss to Stuart Hogg's Montpellier
Rugby.summary: Bath boss Johann van Graan lamented a costly combination of inaccuracy and unforced errors after his side's Investec Champions Cup campaign began with a shock 32-14 home defeat to Montpellier Hérault Rugby.
bullets: Bath began their Investec Champions Cup campaign with a 32-14 home defeat to Montpellier at The Rec, despite leading 14-10 at half-time through tries from Ollie Lawrence and Arthur Green. Montpellier took control after the break, with Donovan Taofifenua scoring twice, including an interception of a Finn Russell pass. A Josh Bayliss try for Bath was ruled out after the TMO spotted a neck roll.

Bath boss Johann van Graan said his side created enough chances but were let down by unforced errors and a lack of accuracy, adding that they had not adapted quickly enough to the referee. He pointed to missed opportunities at 14-10, 15-14 and 25-14. Bath face Gloucester in the Gallagher PREM next weekend and meet Montpellier again in December.
Rugby.copy:
Bath boss Johann van Graan lamented a costly combination of inaccuracy and unforced errors after his side’s Investec Champions Cup campaign began with a shock 32-14 home defeat to Montpellier Hérault Rugby.

The Gallagher PREM side looked well placed after a strong first-half display at The Rec but it all went to hell in a handbasket in a second-half where Bath, at times, were their own worst enemies.

Rugby.title: South American underdogs claim victory in World Rugby U20 Challenger
Rugby.summary: Chile claimed the inaugural WR U20 Challenger title after beating Belgium 30-17 in a tense match that had everything. Portugal took a podium spot after beating Romania...
bullets: Chile won the inaugural World Rugby U20 Challenger title, beating Belgium 30-17 on finals day as hosts. Belgium scored inside the first minute through a charge-down by Oscar Shortall, but Santiago Wood's try and Jaime Soler's kicking put Chile ahead. Portugal took bronze with a 67-13 win over Romania, their biggest U20 victory over their rivals.

Canada finished fifth with a 61-24 win over Brazil, while Namibia beat Hong Kong China 53-5 to place above them. Namibia's William Beukes contributed a penalty and conversions throughout, and skipper Jano Erasmus scored twice. Brazil's Francisco da Ros scored three tries in defeat.
Rugby.copy:
Chile claimed the inaugural WR U20 Challenger title after beating Belgium 30-17 in a tense match that had everything. Portugal took a podium spot after beating Romania, while Canada finished fifth with a 61-24 win over Brazil. Namibia ended the campaign with a victory, placing themselves above Hong Kong China.

In the opening match of finals day at the World Rugby U20 Challenger, Namibia enjoyed their best performance of the tournament to claim a 53-5 win over Hong Kong China. The U20 Welwitschias headed into half-time with a commanding 17-0 advantage after tries from full-back Wesely Haukongo and winger Ethan Sinden, with William Beukes contributing a penalty and two successful conversions.

Rugby.title: 'It's not good enough': Wallabies digest loss as Suaalii and Jorgensen come under spotlight
Rugby.summary: Wallabies coach Les Kiss is unsure if he will find the answers in time after the All Blacks delivered an attacking masterclass to provide the blueprint for 2027 Rugby World Cup glory
bullets: Australia lost 43-21 to the All Blacks in Sydney, following a 50-19 defeat in Auckland, as New Zealand retained the Bledisloe Cup for a 23rd straight year. The Wallabies conceded seven tries, with wingers and centres under scrutiny: Max Jorgensen gave away the opening try and Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii missed five tackles at outside centre.

Wallabies coach Les Kiss said he remained optimistic but could not promise there was enough time before the 2027 World Cup, where Australia open against Hong Kong in Perth. Captain Harry Wilson called the performance not good enough. All Blacks coach Dave Rennie said his side would keep playing attacking rugby at the World Cup rather than adopt a risk-free approach.
Rugby.copy:
Wallabies coach Les Kiss is unsure if he will find the answers in time after the All Blacks delivered an attacking masterclass to provide the blueprint for 2027 Rugby World Cup glory with yet another Bledisloe Cup belting in Sydney.

While Kiss is remaining “optimistic”, Saturday’s 43-21 pounding after a 50-19 shellacking in Auckland had already secured the prized silverware for a 23rd straight year once again exposed the gulf in class between the two trans-Tasman “rivals”.

Rugby.title: '20 to go he might get me': Beauden Barrett on Bledisloe double as 150th cap looms
Rugby.summary: Beauden Barrett has extended his All Blacks try record to 48 after a Bledisloe double in Sydney inched him closer to the former spot held by Doug Howlett.
bullets: Beauden Barrett extended his All Blacks try record to 48 with two tries in the Bledisloe Cup win over Australia in Sydney, moving closer to Doug Howlett's mark. The second of his tries was a 70-metre intercept on half-time from a Max Jorgensen pass, with Wallabies fullback Tom Wright in pursuit. Barrett said he thought Wright might catch him in the final 20 metres.

Barrett, who has 147 Test caps, is three short of a 150th and could reach the milestone on the end-of-year tour. He said playing in Dave Rennie's system made him feel like himself again after a tough season with the Blues. He added that he does not take selection for granted given the squad's depth and injuries.
Rugby.copy:
Beauden Barrett has extended his All Blacks try record to 48 after a Bledisloe double in Sydney inched him closer to the former spot held by Doug Howlett. In that first half demolition fullback Barrett bagged a brace with power from close before a classic intercept right on half-time which proved critical.

The Wallabies had attempted to pick apart the All Blacks on the edges frequently, something they had a lot of success with but without polish as the final pass went astray. Looking to land a blow right on half-time, Barrett landed a big blow by reigning in a Max Jorgensen pop pass and taking back 70 metres the other way.

Rugby.title: Prima KottuMee backs Asia Rugby Sevens as sponsor
Rugby.summary: Prima KottuMee backs Asia Rugby Sevens as sponsor Island.lk
bullets: Prima KottuMee has become Silver Sponsor of the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series 2026. The series concludes in Colombo on 17 and 18 October, with Sri Lanka's national team facing the region's best. The 2026 edition features 24 national teams, with 12 sides each in the men's and women's competitions.

Prima KottuMee has long supported Sri Lankan rugby at school, club and national levels, backing players, teams and tournaments. With Colombo hosting the final leg of the series, the brand said it hopes to add momentum to the occasion and reaffirm its commitment to nurturing local sporting talent.
Rugby.copy:
Prima KottuMee has come on board as the Silver Sponsor of the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series 2026, throwing its weight behind Sri Lankan rugby as the national team prepares to take on the region’s best.

The prestigious tournament will reach its climax in Colombo on 17 and 18 October, giving local rugby enthusiasts an opportunity to witness some of Asia’s finest talent in action on home soil.

Rugby.title: 'Unbelievable': All Blacks coach heaps praise on in-form loose-forward
Rugby.summary: Lakai finished with a game-high 18 carries against the Wallabies, making sixteen tackles, missing only four.
bullets: All Blacks coach Dave Rennie praised loose-forward Peter Lakai after the 43-21 win over the Wallabies in Sydney, calling him an unbelievable athlete who runs like a back and hits hard. Lakai made a game-high 18 carries and 16 tackles, missing four, while Wallace Sititi scored a first-half try and added 15 carries and 11 tackles. Rennie named the same back-row trio as in Auckland despite the absence of Ardie Savea, Luke Jacobson, Anton Segner and Ethan Blackadder.

Lakai also played in midfield for a period while the All Blacks were reduced to 13 men. Rennie said he was proud of the team's character but disappointed they were not more clinical after dominating the first 40 minutes. Stand-in captain Codie Taylor said the group had reflected honestly after the tour of South Africa and had met the standards it wanted to set.
Rugby.copy:
Even with Ardie Savea, Luke Jacobson, Anton Segner, and Ethan Blackadder missing from the All Blacks‘ 23-man squad for the Wallabies in Sydney, Dave Rennie’s side were far from short of quality in the loose-forwards.

Rennie named the same trio to start the second Test at Sydney’s Accor Stadium against the Wallabies as he did the week before in Auckland, which included Tupou Vaa’i, Peter Lakai, and Wallace Sititi.

Rugby.title: Georgie Perris-Redding: 'We made it harder than we needed to'
Rugby.summary: USA captain Georgie Perris-Redding believes the Eagles made life harder for themselves in their 36-27 victory over Italy.
bullets: USA captain Georgie Perris-Redding said the Eagles made life harder than necessary in their 36-27 win over Italy at Texas Health Mansfield Stadium in the WXV Global Series. She scored a hat-trick, carried a team-high 18 times, made two line breaks and 15 tackles. The USA led 26-10 at half-time before Italy scored three second-half tries.

The win is the Eagles' fourth Test victory in a row, their first such run since 2006, and their third against a Guinness Women's Six Nations team this autumn. They remain due to face Italy again in Nashville, then the Red Roses. Perris-Redding said the team knew what to fix and credited the crowd and her teammates.
Rugby.copy:
USA captain Georgie Perris-Redding believes the Eagles made life harder for themselves in their 36-27 victory over Italy. The USA Women’s Eagles have now won four Test matches in a row for the first time since 2006, setting themselves up superbly for their remaining WXV Global Series fixtures against Italy and the Red Roses.

The Eagles have beaten three Guinness Women’s Six Nations teams this autumn, and established themselves as a team to watch in women’s Test rugby. Despite securing another victory, there was a sense at full-time that the hosts could have put Italy away sooner.

Rugby.title: Neil Barnes: 'That's who we are, that's what our people expect from us'
Rugby.summary: Barnes, who addressed media in Sydney post-match, admitted that no matter who the All Blacks play, the fundamentals of their game plan will remain the same.
bullets: All Blacks assistant Neil Barnes said the team's approach is "our DNA" and what supporters expect, after a 43-21 win over the Wallabies in Sydney. The visitors scored six tries to one in the first 40 minutes, but were reduced to 13 men at one point after debutant Chay Fihaki was yellow-carded and Timoci Tavatavanawai left the field with no substitutes remaining.

Barnes said the coaching staff emphasised physicality at the breakdown, particularly against Fraser McReight and Rob Valetini, with players expected to be first to the cleanout. He said the All Blacks have used more than 50 players in 2026 to build depth ahead of next year's World Cup in Australia, and praised Fabian Holland's performance.
Rugby.copy:
All Blacks assistant and former Taranaki head coach Neil Barnes is keeping his feet firmly on the floor despite back-to-back convincing victories over the Wallabies, conceding that it’s “what our people expect from us”.

In the end, Dave Rennie’s All Blacks battled their way to a 43-21 triumph over Les Kiss’ Wallabies in Sydney, even after a near-perfect first forty minutes where the visitors ran in six tries to one heading into the break.

Rugby.title: Talking points: Bella Vogel shines as USA overcome Italy in Texas
Rugby.summary: The USA Women's Eagles' extended their unbeaten WXV Global Series 2026 campaign with a 36-27 win over Italy in Texas.
bullets: The USA Women's Eagles beat Italy 36-27 in Texas to extend their unbeaten WXV Global Series 2026 campaign, having earlier beaten Ireland and Wales in September. Georgie Perris-Redding scored a hat-trick, Hope Rogers added two tries, and 19-year-old Bella Vogel kicked a penalty in the 76th minute to put the game out of reach. Italy scored through Francesca Granzotto (twice), Vittoria Vecchini, Aura Muzzo and Vittoria Zanette.

The USA face Italy again next week in Nashville before hosting the Red Roses in New Jersey. Italy turned the ball over 15 times, while the USA conceded eight penalties and lost the ball nine times. The Eagles recorded 207 post-contact metres, 10 line breaks and 172 carries, and Vogel has won eight caps.
Rugby.copy:
The USA Women’s Eagles’ extended their unbeaten WXV Global Series 2026 campaign with a 36-27 win over Italy in Texas. The result means the Americans have now beaten three Guinness Women’s Six Nations teams this autumn, having previously defeated Ireland and Wales in September.

Jack Hanratty’s team can call themselves the form team in women’s Test rugby, with four consecutive wins under their belts. They will have a second shot at Italy next week in Nashville before concluding 2026 by hosting the Red Roses in New Jersey.

Rugby.title: Montpellier down Bath through Taofifenua double, Munster honour Foley
Rugby.summary: Donovan Taofifenua crossed in the corner to hand Montpellier the lead before he then intercepted Finn Russell’s pass to deliver a quickfire double.
bullets: Munster beat Racing 92 33-25 at Supervalu Pairc ui Chaoimh, with Brian Gleeson scoring the opening try in the seventh minute after giving up the number eight jersey. Shay McCarthy added a second try to make it 14-6 at half-time, and Tadhg Beirne, Fineen Wychereley and Craig Casey scored in the second half. Charlie O'Shea converted three times on debut.

In Pool Four, Montpellier won 32-14 at Bath's The Rec, having trailed 14-10 at half-time. Donovan Taofifenua scored a quickfire double, the second try coming from intercepting Finn Russell's pass, and Alex Becognee made the result safe. Josh Bayliss's late try for Bath was ruled out. At Munster, the number eight jersey was retired in honour of Anthony Foley, who died aged 42 in 2016, and 'There is an Isle' was performed before kick-off.
Rugby.copy:
Brian Gleeson paid the perfect tribute to the late Anthony Foley, relinquishing the number eight jersey then scoring Munster’s opening try in a 33-25 win over Racing 92. The number eight jersey was retired for the night at Supervalu Pairc ui Chaoimh in honour of the club’s former captain and head coach, who died aged 42 on the eve of a clash between the same teams in 2016.

Gleeson instead wore number 24 and gave the Irish side a seventh-minute lead when he powered over the line. That helped his side take a 14-6 half-time lead, Shay McCarthy adding a second score. Both teams touched down three times in an expansive second half, Tadhg Beirne, Fineen Wychereley and Craig Casey for the hosts, who never surrendered the lead, while Wilfried Hulleu, Maxime Machenaud and Joey Manu responded for the French outfit.

Rugby.title: Two All Blacks fly home from Sydney to bolster NPC semi-finalists
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks confirmed on Sunday morning that the duo would turn out for their respective franchises.
bullets: All Blacks Josh Jacomb and Jamie Hannah have flown home from Sydney straight after the warm-up to play in Sunday afternoon's Hilux NPC semi-finals, for Taranaki and Canterbury respectively. Both missed selection for the two Bledisloe Cup Tests but were in the 34-man squad that travelled for the second Test against the Wallabies.

Assistant coach Neil Barnes said Northland's Simon Parker will also fly home on Sunday to play in the NPC final, adding that the All Blacks have tried to release as many players as possible to support the competition. Northland will host Taranaki in the final if Taranaki beat Canterbury, while a Canterbury win would see Northland travel to Christchurch.
Rugby.copy:
Both Taranaki and Canterbury have been handed a huge boost ahead of Sunday afternoon’s Hilux NPC semi-final, with Josh Jacomb and Jamie Hannah returning to New Zealand early. The duo missed out on All Blacks selection for both Bledisloe Cup Tests, but were in the 34-man squad that travelled to Sydney ahead of the second Test match against the Wallabies.

But the All Blacks confirmed on Sunday morning that the duo would turn out for their respective franchises, having flown home straight after the warm-up at Sydney’s Accor Stadium.

Rugby.title: Scarlets cruise past Newcastle as Walker double headlines Ulster win
Rugby.summary: Last season’s Challenge Cup finalists built up a 19-0 advantage by the halfway point, through Walker’s two tries, scored eight minutes before and after one by Jacob Stockdale.
bullets: Scarlets beat Newcastle 47-14 in the EPCR Challenge Cup at Parc y Scarlets, Llanelli, on 17 October, scoring seven tries and leading 26-0 at half-time. Macs Page scored twice, with further tries from Sam Costelow, Fletcher Anderson, Johnny Williams, Gareth Davies and Ellis Mee.

Newcastle replied with tries from Oli Spencer and Ollie Leatherbarrow, and were reduced to 14 men when Murray McCallum was sent to the sin bin. Elsewhere, Ulster won 40-21 against Zebre with six tries, including two from hooker Henry Walker, who was making his first competitive start for the province. Ulster led 19-0 at the interval, and Michael Lowry and Martin Moloney scored late tries.

Rugby.title: ‘Best in the world’: Dave Rennie on keeping Wallabies breakdown ace quiet
Rugby.summary: Despite the Wallabies flanker's class, the All Blacks suffocated McReight's opportunities over the ball, limiting him to very few genuine turnovers.
bullets: All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie said Wallabies openside Fraser McReight is probably the best in the world in his position, after his side limited him to very few genuine turnovers across the two 2026 Bledisloe Cup Tests. The All Blacks completed a clean sweep of the series with the win at Sydney's Accor Stadium, following the Eden Park Test just over a week earlier.

Rennie said the plan relied on the quality of New Zealand's carries and their ability to stay up longer and win races, adding that McReight came up with nothing in key moments. The All Blacks held firm despite Quinn Tupaea failing an HIA, injuries to Samisoni Taukei'aho and Shannon Frizell, and playing the last ten minutes with 13 players. Captain Codie Taylor praised the Wallabies' lineout and maul.
Rugby.copy:
It’s safe to say All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie was over the moon with how his side nullified Wallabies No. 7 Fraser McReight across the two Bledisloe Cup fixtures. Following the All Blacks’ disappointing 3-1 series defeat to South Africa, where Malcolm Marx enjoyed some pay at the breakdown, Rennie clearly challenged his players to respond against the Wallabies.

McReight is among the world’s best in his position, offering the Wallabies genuine breakdown presence across the two-Test series against the All Blacks. Despite McReight’s class, the All Blacks suffocated his opportunities over the ball, limiting him to very few genuine turnovers across the 2026 Bledisloe Cup series.

Rugby.title: Munster hold on to beat Racing after Foley tributes
Rugby.summary: Munster start their Champions Cup campaign with a 33-25 win over Racing 92 on an emotional night at Pairc Ui Chaoimh.
bullets: Munster beat Racing 92 33-25 at Pairc Ui Chaoimh in their opening Champions Cup match, played a decade and a day after the death of former captain Anthony Foley. Tries came from Brian Gleeson, Shay McCarthy, Tadhg Beirne, Fineen Wycherley and Craig Casey. Racing replied through Wilfried Hulleu, Maxime Machenaud and Joey Manu, cutting the lead to three points before Arthur Roche's late yellow card.

Before kick-off the Shannon RFC choir sang There is an Isle, and a minute's applause was held in the eighth minute. Neither side wore the number eight shirt. Munster had surrendered a 21-point lead against Ulster the previous week. Racing are 12th in the Top 14 after four losses in six games. Munster travel to Leinster in the United Rugby Championship next weekend.
Rugby.copy:
Munster started their Champions Cup campaign with a 33-25 win over Racing 92 on an emotional night at Pairc Ui Chaoimh. The game was played a decade and a day on from the passing of Munster legend Anthony Foley - the first Munster captain to lift the Heineken Cup - who died in his sleep before a scheduled fixture between these two sides in October 2016.

Before kick-off in Cork, the Shannon RFC choir gave a moving rendition of There is an Isle, the club song that formed such a memorable part of Foley's Limerick funeral. Neither side took to the field with a player wearing Foley's number eight, while there was also a minute's applause in the eighth minute of a game attended by members of the former Ireland back row's family.

Rugby.title: Bath loss rounds off disappointing day for Prem clubs in Champions Cup
Rugby.summary: Montpellier score 22 second-half points without reply to beat Bath on the opening weekend of the Champions Cup.
bullets: Montpellier won at Bath in their opening Champions Cup Pool Four fixture at The Rec, with Donovan Taofifenua scoring a second-half double and Alex Becognee adding a late try. Last season's Challenge Cup winners scored 22 points without reply after half-time. Bath had a try disallowed in each half, and Joe Cokanasiga failed to gather a pass with the line open when they led 14-10.

Bath had scored at least 33 points in each of their first three Prem games this season. They joined Sale, Bristol and Saracens in losing their opening pool match, after Gloucester drew with holders Bordeaux on Friday. Bath's remaining pool fixtures are against Cardiff, the Bulls and Stade Francais. The Bulls beat Stade Francais 56-20 earlier on Saturday, with Cheswill Jooste scoring a hat-trick.
Rugby.copy:
Montpellier earned an impressive victory at Bath, rounding off a disappointing Saturday for English clubs in the Champions Cup. After Gloucester's high-scoring draw against holders Bordeaux on Friday, Bath joined Sale, Bristol and Saracens in losing their opening pool fixture.

Leicester, Exeter and Northampton are all in action on Sunday. Bath had scored at least 33 points in each of their first three Prem games this season but failed to reach those heights in attack during their Pool Four opener at The Rec.

Rugby.title: Costelow injury worry as Scarlets thrash Newcastle in Challenge Cup
Rugby.summary: Scarlets hammer Newcastle but fly-half Sam Costelow gives Wales coach Steve Tandy an injury concern.
bullets: Scarlets beat Newcastle Red Bulls with a seven-try bonus-point win in the European Challenge Cup at Llanelli. Macs Page scored two tries on his 50th appearance, with Sam Costelow, Fletcher Anderson, Johnny Williams, Gareth Davies and Ellis Mee also crossing. Newcastle replied late through Oliver Spencer and Ollie Leatherbarrow, and have now lost four successive games. The hosts led 26-0 at half-time.

Costelow scored the opening try but limped off with a hamstring problem, three days before Wales coach Steve Tandy names his squad for next month's Autumn Nations Championship. Taine Plumtree made his first appearance of the season after shoulder surgery. Scarlets now face a United Rugby Championship double-header in South Africa against Stormers and Bulls. Newcastle host Sale in the Prem next Saturday.
Rugby.copy:
Scarlets cantered to a seven-try bonus-point European Challenge Cup win against Newcastle Red Bulls but fly-half Sam Costelow has given Wales coach Steve Tandy an injury concern.

Costelow scored the opening try only to limp off with a hamstring problem later in the first half, just three days before Tandy names his squad for next month's Autumn Nations Championship campaign.

Rugby.title: Tributes to Andrews before Champions Cup matches
Rugby.summary: Lions and Sale Sharks are among the clubs to pay tribute to Hyron Andrews at their matches on Saturday, following the South African's death aged 31.
bullets: Lions and Sale Sharks were among the clubs to pay tribute to Hyron Andrews, the former Sale lock who died aged 31 at the Lions' team hotel on Friday, a day before their Champions Cup game at La Rochelle. The Lions played the match in his honour and lost 31-14. Both sides wore black armbands, and Andrews' number five jersey was laid out on the pitch during a minute's silence.

Lions head coach Ivan van Rooyen said the team chose to play to celebrate Andrews and show respect to his wife and children. La Rochelle's Dillyn Leyds, David Kriel and Salmaan Moerat presented a commemorative jersey to the Lions. Pre-match tributes were held before all of this weekend's Champions Cup and Challenge Cup fixtures. Sale's Alex Sanderson, after a 47-27 loss to Glasgow Warriors, said the club would help Andrews' family through it.
Rugby.copy:
Lions and Sale Sharks were among the clubs to pay tribute to Hyron Andrews at their matches on Saturday, following the South African's death aged 31. Former Sale lock Andrews died at the Lions' team hotel on Friday, a day before their Champions Cup pool game against La Rochelle in France.

The Lions, who said they would fulfil the fixture in Andrews' honour, lost 31-14. Asked before the match why the Lions had chosen to play, head coach Ivan van Rooyen said: "It's been a tough 24 hours and we've decided to celebrate Hyron, show respect to his wife and his children, and celebrate life. It gets taken away so quickly.

Rugby.title: Seven-try Connacht beat Saracens in Champions Cup
Rugby.summary: Connacht produce a superb attacking performance to beat Saracens in their opening Champions Cup pool game.
bullets: Connacht beat Saracens in their opening Champions Cup pool game at Dexcom Stadium, scoring seven tries. Captain Cian Prendergast and fly-half Ciaran Frawley each scored two, with Caolin Blade adding another. Saracens led 12-0 early through Sione Vaenuku and Noah Caluori tries, but Connacht replied with 19 unanswered points and the sides were level at 19-19 at half-time.

Saracens had a chance of a losing bonus point, but Owen Farrell's conversion after Elliot Daly's late try went wide. Connacht are third from bottom in the United Rugby Championship after three games. They missed a bonus point because teams must score three or more tries than their opponents to earn one in the pool stage this season. Elsewhere in Pool Two, La Rochelle beat Lions 31-14.
Rugby.copy:
Connacht produced a superb attacking performance to beat Saracens in their opening Champions Cup pool game. Captain Cian Prendergast and fly-half Ciaran Frawley scored two tries apiece as Connacht, third from bottom in the United Rugby Championship table after three games, crossed seven times against the three-time Champions Cup winners at a raucous Dexcom Stadium.

Saracens had the chance to leave with a losing bonus point, but Owen Farrell's conversion attempt after Elliot Daly's late try went wide. The Prem club had led 12-0 early on with tries from Sione Vaenuku and Noah Caluori.

Rugby.title: Six-try Ulster secure bonus-point win over Zebre
Rugby.summary: Ulster run in six tries on their way to a 40-21 bonus-point win over Zebre in Parma to open their European Challenge Cup campaign.
bullets: Ulster ran in six tries to beat Zebre 40-21 in Parma, securing a bonus point in the opening match of their European Challenge Cup campaign. Recent academy graduate Henry Walker scored two tries on his first competitive start, with Jacob Stockdale, David McCann, Mike Lowry and Martin Moloney also crossing. Ulster led 19-0 in the first half before Zebre fought back after the break.

Zebre, bottom of the URC table, scored through Giovanni Licata, Alessandro Ortombina and Giovanni Montemauri, with the last briefly pushing Ulster out of bonus-point range before Moloney's try restored the buffer. McCann captained the side for the first time. With the Challenge Cup now parked until December, Ulster face three consecutive away URC fixtures, starting with a South African double-header against the Bulls and Stormers.
Rugby.copy:
Ulster ran in six tries on their way to a 40-21 bonus-point win over Zebre in Parma to open their European Challenge Cup campaign. Recent academy graduate Henry Walker shone on his first competitive start for Richie Murphy's side as he scored two tries for the province and showed great promise in the front row against a tenacious Zebre outfit.

Last season's beaten finalists took a 19-0 lead with Jacob Stockdale also crossing in between Walker's first-half double. Zebre clawed their way back into the contest in the second half but the visitors finished strongly to keep hold of their bonus point.

Rugby.title: Bristol beaten by Stormers in Champions Cup opener
Rugby.summary: Bristol Bears lose their Champions Cup pool-stage opener against Stormers, with Jonathan Roche and Leolin Zas both scoring twice for the South African side.
bullets: Stormers beat Bristol Bears by scoring seven tries in the Champions Cup pool opener. Seabelo Senatla, Leolin Zas, Jonathan Roche (twice), Warrick Gelant and Andre-Hugo Venter crossed, and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu converted all seven. Bristol replied through Joe Owen and Sol Moody. Stormers hooker JJ Kotze was shown a 20-minute red card for head-to-head contact with Bristol captain Kieran Marmion.

Stormers secured a bonus point. Bristol have won two of their first three Prem games. They host Munster in their next Champions Cup fixture on 12 December, then face French clubs Racing 92 and Bordeaux in January to complete the pool phase.
Rugby.copy:
Bristol Bears conceded seven tries as they lost to South African side Stormers in their first pool match of this season's Champions Cup. Seabelo Senatla raced clear for Stormers' opening score and then showed incredible footwork to control a pass with his boot before offloading to fellow winger Leolin Zas.

Joe Owen powered over in the corner to reply for Bristol but Stormers quickly restored their 14-point advantage with a Jonathan Roche try. Stormers hooker JJ Kotze was shown a 20-minute red card before the interval for making head-to-head contact in a tackle with Bristol skipper Kieran Marmion.

Rugby.title: Seven-try Leinster too strong for Clermont
Rugby.summary: Leinster launch their quest for an elusive fifth European title with an ultimately comprehensive bonus-point win over Clermont at Stade Marcel-Michelin.
bullets: Leinster beat Clermont with a seven-try bonus-point win at Stade Marcel-Michelin in their Pool One opener. Tadhg Furlong and Dan Sheehan, who scored twice, crossed along with Jack Conan, Tommy O'Brien and Sam Prendergast, who scored 16 points. A penalty try was also awarded. Clermont led by a point at half-time through Joris Jurand's try and 11 points from Harry Plummer, and Mathys Belaubre scored later.

A minute's silence was held beforehand for Lions lock Hyron Andrews, who died on Friday aged 31. Leinster were beaten finalists for the fifth time in eight seasons in May. Conan left the stadium with his arm in a sling, a concern for Ireland boss Andy Farrell, who names his squad for next month's Nations Championship fixtures on Wednesday. Clermont have lost four of six Top 14 games.
Rugby.copy:
Leinster launched their quest for an elusive fifth European title with an ultimately comprehensive bonus-point win over Clermont at Stade Marcel-Michelin. Beaten finalists for the fifth time in eight seasons in May, Leinster head coach Leo Cullen loaded his line-up with Ireland internationals and it paid dividends in a seven-try display in their pool one opener.

While Tadhg Furlong and Dan Sheehan scored first-half tries for Leinster, the hosts edged in front before half-time thanks to Joris Jurand's score and 11 points from the boot of fly-half Harry Plummer.

Rugby.title: Glasgow get bonus-point win at emotion-filled Sale
Rugby.summary: Glasgow Warriors pull away to record an impressive bonus-point victory over Sale Sharks in the Investec Champions Cup at an emotional CorpAcq Stadium.
bullets: Glasgow Warriors earned a bonus-point win over Sale Sharks at CorpAcq Stadium in the Champions Cup. Tries came from Kyle Steyn, Jamie Dobie, Alex Craig, Ollie Smith and Ottavio Tuipulotu, plus a penalty try that sent Gus Warr to the sin-bin. Sale scored through Ben Curry, Arron Reed twice and Rekeiti Ma'asi-White. A new rule this year awards an extra point to teams scoring three more tries than their opponents.

A minute's silence was held before kick-off for former Sale lock Hyron Andrews, who died on Friday aged 31. Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson said he did not want to use the emotion as motivation and praised how the squad had supported each other. Glasgow, who were beaten by Toulon in last season's quarter-finals, host Pau in December, while Sale travel to Leinster.
Rugby.copy:
Glasgow Warriors pulled away to record an impressive bonus-point victory over Sale Sharks in the Investec Champions Cup on an emotional day at CorpAcq Stadium. Pre-match tears were shed on the pitch and in the stands during a minute's silence in memory of former Sale lock Hyron Andrews, who died on Friday at the Johannesburg Lions' team hotel before their Champions Cup match at La Rochelle.

The 31-year-old played regularly for Sale last season, and his former side started positively as they sought a memorable performance. Ben Curry peeled off a maul and sprinted through, much to Glasgow's surprise, before Arron Reed crossed out wide after some sharp handling.

Rugby.title: Ospreys ease to Challenge Cup victory over Black Lion
Rugby.summary: Ospreys get off to a winning start in the 2026-27 Challenge Cup, running in seven tries against Black Lion in Georgia.
bullets: Ospreys secured a bonus-point win over Black Lion at Avchala Stadium in Tbilisi in the Challenge Cup, scoring seven tries to the hosts' two. They led 22-7 at half-time after tries from Gwilym Evans, Morgan Morse, Huw Sutton and Luke Morgan, with further scores from Morgan, hooker Lewis Lloyd and prop Kian Hire after the break. Fly-half Lawson Creighton struggled with the kicking tee.

Black Lion had previously beaten Scarlets, Vannes and Montauban, but never threatened the Welsh side. Ospreys return to Swansea for two fixtures after opening their 2026-27 season with away games in Durban, Johannesburg, Newport and Tbilisi. They open their revamped St Helen's home with URC derbies against Dragons and Cardiff before the November international break, then host Harlequins in December.
Rugby.copy:
Ospreys successfully avoided a Challenge Cup banana skin with a comfortable bonus-point win against Black Lion in Georgia. Mark Jones' men scored seven tries at Avchala Stadium in Tbilisi and limited their hosts to two efforts to secure a bonus point.

Ospreys led 22-7 at half-time after tries by all three members of their back row, Gwilym Evans, Morgan Morse and Huw Sutton, plus wing Luke Morgan. Further scores followed in perfect conditions for running rugby from Morgan, hooker Lewis Lloyd and prop Kian Hire.

Rugby.title: England vow to respond after Canada end historic unbeaten streak
Rugby.summary: Red Roses captain Megan Jones has sworn England will respond after their first defeat in 42 Tests matches.
bullets: Canada ended England's run of 42 Tests without defeat with a 24-21 win at Toronto's BMO Field in the WXV Global Series on Friday, England's first loss in almost four years. A second-half resurgence and a physical display from Kévin Rouet's side, backed by 18,621 supporters, beat their Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 final opponents.

The first Test of the three-match autumn series in Exeter finished 26-26, so England can now only draw the series. The teams meet again next Friday at Ottawa's TD Place, before England end their campaign against the USA at New Jersey's Sports Illustrated Stadium. Captain Megan Jones said the side would respond and that a team at the top always carries a target, while Mitchell said England had been asking someone to come and get them and must now reflect and respond.
Rugby.copy:
Red Roses captain Megan Jones has sworn England will respond after their first defeat in 42 Tests matches. On Friday night, a second-half resurgence saw Canada end England’s four-year unbeaten streak with a 24-21 win at Toronto’s BMO Field in WXV Global Series action.

A raucous home crowd set the scene in the second of three Tests the two teams are playing this autumn. The first game in Exeter ended 26-26, with England now only able to draw the series before ending their campaign at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium against the USA Women’s Eagles.

Rugby.title: ‘Awesome’ New Zealand humiliate Australia with 13th consecutive win over rivals
Rugby.summary: Australia 21-43 New Zealand: The All Blacks were rampant in the first half in Sydney
bullets: New Zealand beat Australia 43-21 at Stadium Australia, extending their winning run over the Wallabies to 13 matches. Having already retained the Bledisloe Cup for a 24th year after a 50-19 win in Auckland, they scored six first-half tries and led 36-7 at the break. Moorby, Beauden Barrett (twice), Peter Lakai, Rieko Ioane and Wallace Sititi crossed in the first half.

Jordie Barrett was lost to a calf injury before kick-off and Quinn Tupaea to concussion early on. Captain Codie Taylor praised the first 40 minutes. Tom Wright and Filipo Daugunu scored for Australia in front of 73,399. Chay Fihaki was yellow-carded on debut, and Wallabies captain Harry Wilson said the group must be a lot better.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. The All Blacks rode a first-half try blitz to a 43-21 victory over the Wallabies at Stadium Australia on Saturday, extending their win streak over their trans-Tasman-Sea rivals to 13 matches. With the Bledisloe Cup already safely in the cupboard for a 24th year after last week's 50-19 win in Auckland, New Zealand exploded out of the blocks and crushed all thoughts of an upset with six tries before the break.

Despite losing Jordie Barrett to a calf injury before kickoff and another centre in Quinn Tupaea early on with a concussion, the All Blacks overwhelmed the Wallabies with power, pace and precision in the opening 40 minutes. "I'm really proud of the boys, the way we came out on that in that first half," said New Zealand captain Codie Taylor.

Rugby.title: Canada end England’s 41-match unbeaten streak with first defeat in four years
Rugby.summary: England had not lost a match since the World Cup final in 2022 and will play emerging rivals Canada again in Ottawa next week
bullets: Canada beat England 24-21 in Toronto, ending the Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten run, which stretched back four years to the 2022 World Cup final loss to New Zealand. Replacement Shoshanah Seumanutafa scored the winning try in the 77th minute. The crowd of 18,621 was a record for a women's rugby union match in North America.

Canada drew 26-26 with England in Exeter last month, and this win avenged the defeat in last year's World Cup final at Twickenham. Head coach John Mitchell said the team would stick to its processes and that the loss would let him learn more about the group. Captain Meg Jones said England took huge pride in the unbeaten run. The sides meet again in Ottawa next Saturday.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. England were stunned by a late charge from Canada as the Red Roses lost their 41-match unbeaten run that stretched back four years.

Last month, Canada snapped England’s 39-game winning streak with a 26-26 draw against the World Cup champions in Exeter. And Canada finally earned revenge for their defeat to England in last year’s World Cup final at Twickenham as they won 24-21 in front of a record crowd in Toronto.

Rugby.title: The ‘really good positive’ for Wallabies despite All Blacks defeat
Rugby.summary: Les Kiss wasn’t surprised to see Declan Meredith produce an impressive performance in just his fourth Test start.
bullets: Wallabies coach Les Kiss praised fly-half Declan Meredith after the 43-21 defeat by the All Blacks at Sydney's Accor Stadium. Meredith, 26, who is four Tests old, made more than 100 running metres and came close to a second-half try, only for Cam Roigard to stop him. He played in the absence of the injured Ben Donaldson. Kiss said Meredith was the most dangerous player in putting the Wallabies into space.

Kiss said the Wallabies conceded 22 points in a short period early on, similar to the second half of the previous week's defeat. The All Blacks led 22-0 after 25 minutes and scored further tries through Wallace Sititi and Beauden Barrett after Jeremy Williams was yellow-carded. The Wallabies outscored the All Blacks 14-7 in the second half, with tries from Tom Wright and Filipo Daugunu.
Rugby.copy:
Les Kiss wasn’t surprised to see Declan Meredith produce an impressive performance against the All Blacks, with the international rookie fly-half standing out despite the Wallabies falling to a 43-21 defeat at Sydney’s Accor Stadium.

Meredith enjoyed a breakout Super Rugby Pacific campaign with the ACT Brumbies, which saw the 26-year-old skyrocket into the Wallabies selection frame. The playmaker debuted against Six Nations side France during the Nations Championship, and also suited up against Italy.

Rugby.title: Rennie explains why All Blacks are ‘fortunate’ to have Beauden Barrett
Rugby.summary: Dave Rennie has explained how fortunate the All Blacks are to have someone like Beauden Barrett in the mix.
bullets: All Blacks coach Dave Rennie said the team is fortunate to have 147-Test veteran Beauden Barrett, who stepped up during the Bledisloe Cup series after injuries to Richie Mo'unga and Ruben Love. The 35-year-old started at fullback, scored a first-half double in the 43-21 win over the Wallabies at Accor Stadium, and the All Blacks secured a series sweep.

Rennie praised Barrett's experience, communication and decision-making. He also singled out Rieko Ioane, who scored a first-half try and played at centre despite barely training there, after being named on the bench and coming on early when Quinn Tupaea went off. The All Blacks led 36-7 at half-time, with Josh Moorby, Peter Lakai and Wallace Sititi also scoring. Rennie said they were clinical in the first 43 minutes.
Rugby.copy:
Dave Rennie has explained how fortunate the All Blacks are to have someone like Beauden Barrett in the mix, with the now 147-Test veteran stepping up during the Bledisloe Cup series after injuries to other playmaking options.

Ruben Love emerged as the first-choice All Blacks first five-eighth after steering the Hurricanes to a drought-breaking Super Rugby Pacific title. Love started in all three Nations Championship fixtures and continued to hold that role during most of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry.

Rugby.title: All Blacks pile on the points to complete Bledisloe Cup series sweep
Rugby.summary: Les Kiss concedes the ruthless All Blacks delivered his side a brutal reality check after heaping more misery on the Wallabies.
bullets: The All Blacks beat the Wallabies 43-21 in Sydney to complete a Bledisloe Cup series sweep, after a 50-19 win in Auckland secured the trophy for a 23rd straight year. Beauden Barrett scored two first-half tries, his 47th and 48th against Australia, making him New Zealand's greatest-ever try-scorer against them. The All Blacks led 36-7 at half-time and extended their winning streak over the Wallabies to 13 Tests.

Les Kiss said the Wallabies' moments got away from them and noted they are ranked sixth in the world, while captain Harry Wilson called the series very disappointing ahead of a big spring tour. The All Blacks were without Jordie Barrett, who withdrew with a calf injury before kick-off, and Quinn Tupaea, who left with concussion. Consolation tries came from Tom Wright and Filipo Daugunu.
Rugby.copy:
Les Kiss concedes the ruthless All Blacks delivered his side a brutal reality check after heaping more misery on the Wallabies with a crushing 43-21 victory in the Bledisloe Cup return bout in Sydney.

As promised after securing the trans-Tasman silverware for a 23rd straight year with a 50-19 shellacking in Auckland, the All Blacks displayed no let-up in another seven-try rout on Saturday.

Rugby.title: Fissler Confidential: Ollie Lawrence rumours wide of mark
Rugby.summary: Leicester Tigers boss Geoff Parling admits he considered a move for former Gloucester hooker Jack Singleton before United Rugby Championship outfit Glasgow Warriors snapped him up on a three-month deal earlier this week.
bullets: Fissler Confidential reports that Leicester Tigers boss Geoff Parling considered signing former Gloucester hooker Jack Singleton before Glasgow Warriors signed him on a three-month deal. Leicester instead signed Samoan international Richie Asiata after Finn Theobald-Thomas' retirement. US Eagles tighthead David Ainu'u, 26, will leave Toulouse for Bordeaux at the end of the season on a four-year deal.

Reports linking England centre Ollie Lawrence, 27, with Bayonne are said to be wide of the mark, as he is under contract at Bath until the summer. Billy Vunipola, 33, is weighing up his future with his Montpellier contract expiring next summer. Toulon's Beka Gigashvili, 34, could leave this summer as the club considers changes to its pack, and Bayonne are negotiating to extend Ewan Johnson's contract.
Rugby.copy:
Leicester Tigers boss Geoff Parling admits he considered a move for former Gloucester hooker Jack Singleton before United Rugby Championship outfit Glasgow Warriors snapped him up on a three-month deal earlier this week.

Singleton has been out of the game since leaving Gloucester when his contract ran out at the end of last season, and the Tigers had their sights on him before landing Samoan international Richie Asiata after Finn Theobald-Thomas’ premature retirement.

Rugby.title: Eight-try Australia send Scotland to eighth straight defeat
Rugby.summary: Scotland suffer a chastening eight-try defeat by Australia in their WXV Global Series match in Sydney.
bullets: Scotland lost their WXV Global Series match against Australia in Sydney after the hosts ran in eight tries, extending the visitors' losing run to eight matches, four of them in the new competition. Scotland, under caretaker head coach Dave Butcher, led through Katie Buchanan's fifth-minute try on her first international start, but Australia scored five tries to lead 35-5 at half-time.

Scotland had lost Sarah Bonar to illness shortly before kick-off, with Bristol Bears' Hollie Cunningham replacing the Harlequins lock. Captain Rachel Malcolm scored a second-half try with Helen Nelson converting, but Amelia Whitaker added her second try and Eva Karpani scored in the closing seconds after Scotland's Eva Donaldson was shown a yellow card. Australia's earlier 30-10 win in Edinburgh lifted them above Scotland in the world rankings.
Rugby.copy:
Scotland suffered a chastening eight-try defeat by Australia in their WXV Global Series match in Sydney. It was the visitors' eighth straight defeat, four of them in the new competition, having lost to Canada, New Zealand and the Aussies in their home ties.

Australia have two victories, both against the Scots, after losing to England and France, their 30-10 win in Edinburgh having lifted them above their hosts in the world rankings.

Rugby.title: England's 41-match unbeaten run ended by Canada
Rugby.summary: England's 41-match unbeaten streak ends in dramatic fashion as Shoshanah Seumanutafa's late try hands Canada a thrilling 24-21 victory in Toronto.
bullets: Canada ended England's 41-match unbeaten run with a 24-21 win in Toronto, courtesy of a late try from replacement Shoshanah Seumanutafa three minutes from time. It is England's first defeat since the 2022 World Cup final loss to New Zealand and their first against Canada since 2016. The crowd of 18,621 was a record for a standalone women's fixture in North America. England led 14-5 at half-time through tries from Maddie Feaunati and Zoe Harrison, and Sarah Bern scored after the break.

Head coach John Mitchell, beaten for the first time since his appointment in late 2023, urged his side to "find something more". Captain Meg Jones said England are still world champions. The teams meet again in Ottawa on Friday 23 October, before England finish their 2026 WXV Global Series against the USA in New Jersey on Friday 30 October. Canada, ranked third, had earlier drawn 26-26 with England in Exeter in September, and the government has announced a 775m Canadian dollar (£401m) sport fund.
Rugby.copy:
England head coach John Mitchell challenged his Red Roses to "find something more" after their 41-match unbeaten streak - dating back almost four years - ended in dramatic fashion as Shoshanah Seumanutafa's late try handed Canada a thrilling 24-21 victory in Toronto.

Canada, who previously snapped England's 39-match winning run with a 26-26 draw in Exeter in September, are the first team to defeat them since November 2022, when they lost to New Zealand in the World Cup final.

Rugby.title: All Blacks player ratings vs Australia | Bledisloe Cup II 2026
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks have comprehensively beat the Wallabies for the second week in a row by 43-21 in Sydney. Here's how the All Blacks rated in Sydney.
bullets: The All Blacks beat the Wallabies 43-21 at Accor Stadium in Sydney in the second Bledisloe Cup Test of 2026, winning for the second week in a row. They led 36-7 at half-time, with Beauden Barrett scoring twice, including a 70-metre intercept try just before the break. Josh Moorby, Peter Lakai, Rieko Ioane and Wallace Sititi also crossed.

Lakai made 17 carries and 15 tackles and scored a try, while Barrett's second-half tackle on Declan Meredith denied Australia a try. Chay Fihaki was shown a yellow card for a tackle on Suaalii with five minutes remaining. Shannon Frizell went off injured, leaving the All Blacks a player short for the final period.
Rugby.copy:
The All Blacks have comprehensively beat the Wallabies for the second week in a row by 43-21 in Sydney. In a game that mirrored the 2024 contest at the same venue, the All Blacks put up a 36-7 half-time lead before Australia edged the second half.

First scrum wasn’t until the 31st minute for the All Blacks front row, but the engine room was busy in defence, all racking up double digit tackles in their 49 minutes. They were impressive controlling the gain line and nullifying the roll of the Wallabies.

Rugby.title: Wallabies player ratings vs New Zealand | Bledisloe Cup II 2026
Rugby.summary: The Wallabies have fallen to a record 13th straight defeat to the All Blacks, losing 43-21 at Sydney’s Accor Stadium.
bullets: The Wallabies lost 43-21 to the All Blacks at Sydney's Accor Stadium, their record 13th straight defeat to New Zealand. Beauden Barrett scored twice as the visitors led 36-7 at the break, and Josh Moorby was first on the scoresheet in the second half. The match closed a first-of-its-kind quadruple-header that began with a Wallaroos win over Scotland.

Declan Meredith, in his fourth start at fly-half, set up Jeremy Williams for a try but limped off with about 10 minutes left. Harry McLaughlin-Phillips became Wallaby number 1001 as his replacement. Williams was shown a yellow card shortly after his try, and Rob Valetini played only 43 minutes. Nick Salakaia-Loto won his 50th Test cap.
Rugby.copy:
The Wallabies have fallen to a record 13th straight defeat to the All Blacks, losing 43-21 at Sydney’s Accor Stadium on Saturday. It was the final match in a first-of-its-kind quadruple-header, which began with a dominant Wallaroos win against Scotland.

Beauden Barrett scored twice as the All Blacks took a 36-7 lead into the break. Josh Moorby was first on the scoresheet in the second term, but the Wallabies managed to stop the point-scoring avalanche from there.

Rugby.title: Talking points as Black Ferns run rampant against outgunned France
Rugby.summary: The Black Ferns have opened their three-Test series against France with a mammoth 81-12 win in Hamilton.
bullets: The Black Ferns beat France 81-12 in Hamilton in the first of a three-Test series, scoring 60 points before France replied. They made 23 linebreaks to France's two, and 20-year-old Shyrah Tuliau-Tua'a scored four second-half tries. Amy Du Plessis, Maia Joseph and Ayesha Leti-I'iga each scored two. New Zealand scored 43 points in the first half and 38 in the second.

The Black Ferns made 20 entries into France's 22m zone and converted at four points per entry, against a 2026 average of 2.9 points per entry. Head coach Whitney Hansen said the team had spoken about being clinical. France tackled at 72 per cent and were outcarried by 103 carries. The series moves to Whangarei next week before a finale in Christchurch.
Rugby.copy:
The Black Ferns have opened their three-Test series against France with a mammoth 81-12 win in Hamilton. The hosts had piled on 60 points before the visitors could fire their first shot, with France’s second try coming in the dying minutes.

New Zealand’s 23 linebreaks dwarfed France’s tally of two, and while Ayesha Leti-I’iga was responsible for four of them, there were 11 other Kiwis who broke the French line in a superb team performance. 20-year-old rookie Shyrah Tuliau-Tua’a bagged four second-half tries while Amy Du Plessis, Maia Joseph and Ayesha Leti-I’iga all scored doubles.

Rugby.title: Black Ferns player ratings vs France in Hamilton | WXV Global Series 2026
Rugby.summary: It took just 67 seconds for New Zealand to get their first five points on the board on a sunny afternoon in Hamilton, and those 67 seconds were as close as France would get in the opening Test of this three-game series.
bullets: New Zealand scored their first try after 67 seconds and led 43-0 at half-time before winning 81-12 against France in Hamilton in the opening Test of the series. Shyrah Tuliau-Tua'a scored four tries in her fourth Test and second start. Olsen-Baker led the Test in metres carried, and the Black Ferns made 14 first-half linebreaks.

Head coach Whitney Hansen said the challenge is now to repeat the effort against a France side desperate for a more respectable scoreline in the second Test. The Black Ferns' lineout operated at 91 per cent against France's 50 per cent, and they had 62 per cent possession. Tests in Whangarei and Christchurch remain.
Rugby.copy:
It took just 67 seconds for New Zealand to get their first five points on the board on a sunny afternoon in Hamilton, and those 67 seconds were as close as France would get in the opening Test of this three-game series.

It was 43-0 by halftime, and 81-12 by full-time. The Kiwis have set an impressive marker with Tests in Whangarei and Christchurch remaining in the series. Head coach Whitney Hansen says the challenge is now to repeat the effort against a France side who will be desperate to at least earn a more respectable scoreline in game 2.

Rugby.title: Maddison Levi stars as Australia claim pre-SVNS bragging rights against NZ
Rugby.summary: HSBC SVNS Series phenom Maddison Levi scored seven tries as Australia finished with a 2-1 record against arch-rivals New Zealand.
bullets: Maddison Levi scored seven tries in three games as Australia's women's sevens side won the series 2-1 against New Zealand in Sydney. Australia won both Kick On 7s matches on Friday, 24-19 and 36-26, before the Black Ferns Sevens won 21-12 on Saturday. Levi scored five tries on Friday, including a hat-trick in the second match.

Jorja Miller led New Zealand's response on Saturday, with Jazmin Felix-Hotham and Renee Holmes also scoring. Australia captain Isabella Nasser said the wins set up confidence for Dubai in a couple of months. In the men's matches, Australia and Fiji drew the series, with Australia winning 24-14, Fiji winning 10-0 and the final match ending 19-19.
Rugby.copy:
HSBC SVNS Series phenom Maddison Levi scored seven tries in three games as Australia finished with a 2-1 record against arch-rivals New Zealand. The Black Ferns Sevens avoided a series sweep with a 21-12 win on a picture-perfect Saturday afternoon in Sydney.

Australia prevailed in the two Kick On 7s matches on Friday evening, with the reigning HSBC SVNS World Championship winners making a bit of a statement in pre-season. But Jorja Miller led the way as the New Zealanders bounced back in style.

Rugby.title: Late charge from Canada ends England’s 41-match unbeaten run
Rugby.summary: .England were stunned by a late rally from Canada as the Red Roses fell 24-21 in their WXV Global Series clash in Toronto.
bullets: Canada beat England 24-21 in the WXV Global Series in Toronto, ending the Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten run. Replacement Shoshanah Seumanutafa scored the winning try in the 77th minute. England led 14-5 at half-time through tries from Maddie Feaunati and Zoe Harrison, after Savannah Bauder had opened the scoring for Canada in the 15th minute.

DaLeaka Menin's 63rd-minute try kept Canada in contention before Seumanutafa's score.
