Rugby.summary: Prima KottuMee boost for Asia Rugby Sevens Ceylon Daily News

Rugby.title: Darcy Graham makes shock early return as Edinburgh prepare for Toulon test
Rugby.summary: Scotland’s Darcy Graham will make a surprise return to action for Edinburgh in Friday night’s European Challenge Cup match against Toulon at Hive Stadium.
bullets: Scotland winger Darcy Graham will make a surprise return for Edinburgh in Friday night's European Challenge Cup match against Toulon at Hive Stadium. The British and Irish Lions player has recovered more quickly than expected from a torn bicep suffered in September, having initially been ruled out until Christmas.

The 29-year-old will hope to force his way into Gregor Townsend's Scotland plans for next month's Nations Championship fixtures against New Zealand, Australia and Japan. Head coach Sean Everitt has made one other change to the side that won 29-12 at Zebre in the United Rugby Championship, with flanker Tom Currie making his first start of the season. Second-row Grant Gilchrist, also back from injury, is on the bench and hopes to make his first appearance of the season.
Rugby.copy:
Scotland’s Darcy Graham will make a surprise return to action for Edinburgh in Friday night’s European Challenge Cup match against Toulon at Hive Stadium. The British and Irish Lions winger has made a quicker-than-expected recovery after tearing a bicep in September and initially being ruled out until Christmas.

It is a timely return for the 29-year-old, who will now be hoping to force his way into Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend’s plans for next month’s Nations Championship fixtures against New Zealand, Australia and Japan.

Rugby.title: Canada expect landmark victory over Red Roses
Rugby.summary: Scrum-half Olivia Apps believes the time is right for Canada to end England's four-year unbeaten run when the teams meet on Friday
bullets: Canada face England's Red Roses in Toronto on Friday and again seven days later in Ottawa, in the 'Rugby Rematch Tour'. The two Tests are Canada's first on home soil since a Rugby World Cup warm-up in August 2025, and more than 15,000 fans are expected at BMO Field. Last month Canada drew 26-26 with England at Sandy Park in Exeter, the first team to avoid defeat against them in nearly four years.

Scrum-half Olivia Apps said that playing alongside England players at Saracens has removed the mystique around them, and that Canada would be 'really, really disappointed' not to win this weekend. Canada's government announced a 755m Canadian dollar (£401m) sport funding package in May after their World Cup final defeat by England a year ago. Apps, named PWR player of the season, has just signed a three-year Saracens extension, and a documentary on Canada's World Cup campaign, All Heart, has been released.
Rugby.copy:
In Exeter last month, there were two expressions on Olivia Apps' face that bode ill for England. It came at the start of Canada's 26-26 draw with the Red Roses at Sandy Park. Apps, Canada's starting scrum-half, aimed it at, and shared it with, England trio Zoe Harrison, Jess Breach and Marlie Packer, who she has played alongside with Saracens in the PWR this season.

"Playing at Saracens has really helped to take the mystique away from all these names that you see on a teamsheet," Apps told BBC Sport. "You know them as people and it takes away that uncertainty, [the] mysterious part."

Rugby.title: Piper Simons: 'A year ago XVs wouldn't even be in the picture for me'
Rugby.summary: If you were to tell Piper Simons 12 months ago she’d be spending nearly all of 2026 diving into the world of XVs, it would have surprised the sevens star.
bullets: Piper Simons, a 21-year-old sevens player, has been named on the bench to win her third cap for the Wallaroos against Scotland at Accor Stadium in Sydney, the second of a three-match series. She made her XVs debut against Fijiana at the start of 2026 and travelled to Europe with the WXV Global Series tour, having not considered XVs a year ago.

Simons said she hopes to become a player able to move between both codes, and credited Samantha Wood for helping her learn. She has also been included in the inaugural Australia U21s squad to face New Zealand U21s at the end of the month. Director of women's high performance Tim Walsh is due to complete the Wallaroos' move to a full-time programme by the end of the year, before Sione Fukofuka takes over as head coach in 2027.
Rugby.copy:
If you were to tell Piper Simons 12 months ago she’d be spending nearly all of 2026 diving into the world of XVs, it would have surprised the sevens star. However, as the Wallaroos prepare for their final fortnight of action in 2026, when they take on Scotland in the second of their three match series, the 21-year-old is hungry to make her mark on both codes and was named to earn her third cap off the bench at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Coming straight into the Australian Women’s Sevens in 2024 after being part of the Australia’s U18s Girls Sevens side that won the Global Youth Sevens title and the Youth Commonwealth Games gold medal in 2023, the last two years saw Simons excel in the short format.

Rugby.title: Gilmore urges Harlequins to continue improvement
Rugby.summary: Harlequins head coach Jason Gilmore urges his team to continue their recent improvement as they look to recover from a woeful start to the season.
bullets: Harlequins head coach Jason Gilmore has urged his side to keep improving after they lost their first three Prem matches and sit bottom of the table. They were beaten 48-0 by Gloucester on 3 October, the club's heaviest league defeat for 26 years, then led Sale for most of Sunday's game before losing to a late penalty.

Quins open their European Challenge Cup campaign at home to Vannes this weekend. Gilmore described Vannes as a classic French team with a big forward pack, strong at the scrum and keen to play unstructured rugby, and said his side must bring physicality and be alert to counter-attack chances. Harlequins finished ninth in the Prem last season.
Rugby.copy:
Harlequins head coach Jason Gilmore has urged his team to continue their recent improvement as they look to recover from a woeful start to the season. Quins are bottom of the Prem table after losing their first three matches.

Gilmore's side were on the end of a 48-0 thrashing by Gloucester on 3 October, but were better against Sale on Sunday, leading for most of the match before being beaten by a late penalty.

Rugby.title: Laetitia Royer column: ‘We want to put England in an uncomfortable situation’
Rugby.summary: We’re so excited to finally have people in the crowd cheering for us. That is not something we have had regularly as a Canada team.
bullets: Canada's Laetitia Royer says the team want to use the support of almost 20,000 fans at BMO Field in Toronto to put England in an uncomfortable position on Friday, the first of two games against them. She said Canada have rarely played in front of regular home crowds and plan to shout over each other in training to prepare for the noise.

Royer said Canada won one, drew one and lost one of their September matches, drawing with England before losing to France after perhaps underestimating them and showing fatigue. She said the squad is maintaining standards rather than rebuilding, with several young players rising to the challenge. She also confirmed she will join Trailfinders Women next season, after playing in Premiership Women's Rugby for a year.
Rugby.copy:
We’re so excited to finally have people in the crowd cheering for us. That is not something we have had regularly as a Canada team. Three weeks ago in France, the crowd was so loud. French supporters are quite passionate. We want to feel that extra inch that home support can give us. It could give us some extra oomph and help build momentum on our side.

I hope that the almost 20,000 supporters at BMO Field can give us that and finally put England in an uncomfortable situation. They’ve had things relatively easy in terms of travel over the years.

Rugby.title: Spain puts Nou Camp and Bernabeu at heart of surprise Rugby World Cup bid
Rugby.summary: Sapin is keen to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup and has included a number of iconic football stadia in the bid but faces competition from Japan and a South American offer led by Argentina
bullets: Spain is bidding to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup, with the Spanish Rugby Federation (RFER) proposing the Nou Camp to host the final. The Bernabeu and Valencia's Mestalla Stadium would also stage matches. The bid has the support of the Spanish government and LaLiga, and the RFER promises the 'best World Cup in history'. It faces competition from Japan and a South American bid led by Argentina, including Brazil, Chile and Uruguay.

World Rugby will carry out site visits and feasibility assessments from December, with a preferred candidate expected by summer 2027 and an official announcement during next October's tournament in Australia. The USA hosts in 2031. Spain, who have qualified for the men's World Cup for the first time since 1999, will co-host the 2030 men's football World Cup with Morocco and Portugal. RFER president Juan Carlos Martin said hosting would be a turning point for the sport's global growth.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Spain is making a surprise bid to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup and will put some of the country’s most iconic football stadia, including Nou Camp and the Bernabeu, at the heart of the offer.

If Spain succeed in their bid, then the revamped Nou Camp – which holds more than 100,000 fans and is home to FC Barcelona – would host the final, with Real Madrid’s Bernabeu and Valencia’s Mestalla Stadium also being lined up to have matches.

Rugby.title: France include four debutants for Black Ferns clash in Hamilton
Rugby.summary: France head coach François Ratier has included four debutants in his matchday 23 to take on the Black Ferns in Hamilton.
bullets: France head coach François Ratier has named four debutants in his matchday 23 for the Black Ferns clash in Hamilton. Alexandra Chambon captains the side for the first time, with Manae Feleu and Pauline Bourdon Sansus unavailable. Ylona Avril earns her first cap in the starting XV, while Marion Latonnelle, Lylou Pedussaud and Charlie Gauyat are among the replacements.

France arrive in New Zealand after a 21-5 win over Canada to conclude the WXV Global Series. Gabrielle Vernier, Carla Arbez and Amber Mwayembe miss out. Ratier said the squad has an average age of 24 and few caps, and that this is the right time to introduce new players, with the World Cup three months away.
Rugby.copy:
France head coach François Ratier has included four debutants in his matchday 23 to take on the Black Ferns in Hamilton. It is the first time that Alexandra Chambon will captain the side, as both Manae Feleu and Pauline Bourdon Sansus are unavailable.

The fourth-ranked team in the world travelled to New Zealand hot on the heels of a 21-5 win against Canada to conclude their WXV Global Series. Ylona Avril gets her first cap in the starting XV, where she partners three-cap Julia Grosz. Toulon’s Marion Latonnelle, along with Toulouse teenagers Lylou Pedussaud and Charlie Gauyat will get their first taste of international rugby from the replacements.

Rugby.title: Tameifuna shifts outside of front-row as Bordeaux forced into bizarre calls
Rugby.summary: Back-to-back Investec Champions Cup winners Bordeaux-Bègles have been forced into an unconventional selection for the start of their title defence against Gloucester, with 148kg prop Ben Tameifuna named in the second-row at Kingsholm.
bullets: Champions Cup holders Bordeaux-Bègles have named 148kg prop Ben Tameifuna in the second row alongside Cameron Woki for their title defence at Gloucester on Friday night. Maxime Lucu moves to fly-half and Martin Page-Relo wears the nine jersey in the absence of Matthieu Jalibert.

Bordeaux have a six-two bench split, with no specialist half-back among the replacements. Gloucester, who pushed Leicester close at Welford Road last weekend, start new signings Dewi Lake, as captain, and Jac Morgan. Jean Kleyn and Arthur Clark are named in the second row.
Rugby.copy:
Back-to-back Investec Champions Cup winners Bordeaux-Bègles have been forced into an unconventional selection for the start of their title defence against Gloucester, with 148kg prop Ben Tameifuna named in the second-row at Kingsholm.

The 1.82m tighthead will make his first Bordeaux appearance of the season in the No.5 jersey alongside Cameron Woki on Friday night, while the visitors have also been forced into an unusual half-back combination in the absence of Matthieu Jalibert.

Rugby.title: Paul Williams: 'Cameron Hanekom is a back-row whose metres carried should be measured in kilometres, not metres'
Rugby.summary: Cameron Hanekom is gaining admirers in France while Sam Prendergast and Taine Basham have started the season with gusto
bullets: Paul Williams's column says Cameron Hanekom's line break and hand-off on Lions wing Richard Kriel show him moving to a different level. It notes tries per match are up by 0.9 in the Premiership, 0.8 in the Top 14 and 0.6 in the URC this season, citing Northampton's 71–48 win over Bath, a 19-try match.

Williams attributes the more open play to the removal of tackle escorts and lower tackle height. He says Sam Prendergast looks stronger on his return for Leinster against Cardiff and that Taine Basham is now Cardiff's premier ball carrier, with a Wales recall a matter of when. He also praises Freddie Steward's attacking threat from full-back.
Rugby.copy:
There are plenty of players in rugby who, over the course of a season, look to have mastered the game. But then there are players who rise above even that high bar and make the game look almost easy – Cameron Hanekom is one of them. He is a back-row forward whose metres carried should be measured in kilometres, not metres. Once he has broken the first line of defence with the power of a Test-level number eight, he accelerates with the speed of a Test-level centre. His line break against the Lions was impressive enough, but it was his nonchalant hand-off on Lions’ wing Richard Kriel that made you realise Hanekom is moving into a different level of play. Kriel is 6ft 4 ins tall and the best part of 100 kilograms – Hanekom flicked him away like an early Halloween cobweb.

Rugby is once again an attacking sport, and it is great news for attack coaches. Long gone are the days when attack coaches had to sit at the back of the team briefing, heads bowed, hands trembling and brows quivering, only to look up at the overly confident defence coaches with their chests puffed out. We’re witnessing an increase in tries across all the major northern hemisphere leagues this season: the Premiership is up by 0.9 tries per match, the Top 14 by 0.8 and the URC by 0.6. You’ll see no better example than Northampton Saints v Bath. It was all-out attack in a manner not seen since ‘Little Nicky’ Scarfo took over the Philadelphia mob in 1981. Northampton won 71–48 in a 19-try match that was as close to Super Rugby as the English Premiership has ever been. The result is a game that feels faster, looser and less predictable. Some old-school supporters are not fans of this new style, often referred to as ‘rugby basketball’.

Rugby.title: Former Scotland scrum-half Caity Mattinson lands development role
Rugby.summary: Former Scotland scrum-half Caity Mattinson has joined Scottish Rugby as a pathways skills coach.
bullets: Former Scotland scrum-half Caity Mattinson has joined Scottish Rugby as a pathways skills coach, focusing on the individual development of young players within the union's pathway system. The role is supported by sportscotland funding. The 37-cap international will lead the development and delivery of a specialist skills programme and support player identification and profiling.

Mattinson retired after the Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 and has since coached in Coventry Rugby's academy and worked as schools rugby manager at Banbury RFC. She also worked with Scotland Under-21 during the Six Nations Women's U21 Series and on the team's trip to Italy. Andy Rhys Jones, head of women's performance and pathways, said her experience would support players across the National Talent Pathway, National Academy Programme and wider pathway.
Rugby.copy:
Former Scotland scrum-half Caity Mattinson has joined Scottish Rugby as a pathways skills coach. The 37-cap Scotland international will focus on the individual development of young players within the union’s pathway system. The role is supported by sportscotland funding.

Mattinson retired following the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 and has since coached in Coventry Rugby’s academy and worked as schools rugby manager at Banbury RFC. “I’m delighted to be coming back to Scotland,” Mattinson said. “I coached across a big range of environments throughout my playing career and, since retiring, have thrown myself into every opportunity that’s come my way.

Rugby.title: Ben Loader: 'Gloucester want to be a team that fights for everything' as European champions loom
Rugby.summary: Rejuvenated and top of the Gallagher Prem, the Cherry and Whites take on the most daunting task in European rugby this Friday.
bullets: Gloucester wing Ben Loader says Friday's Champions Cup match at Kingsholm against holders Bordeaux-Bègles offers a chance to play what team-mate Lewis Ludlow described as a Test match. Loader has scored three tries in Gloucester's first three Premiership games, and the club lead the league after finishing eighth last season and only just qualifying for Europe.

Gloucester lost at Leicester last Friday but took two bonus points from the game. Loader said the signings of Wales pair Dewi Lake and Jac Morgan and South Africa second row Jean Kleyn have added experience, fight and hunger. He played mini rugby at Reading Abbey with Bordeaux back row Tom Willis and will face wing Louis Bielle-Biarrey, whom he ranks alongside Cheslin Kolbe as the world's best. London Irish's 2023 collapse took Loader's career to South Africa.
Rugby.copy:
The Champions Cup has its critics – and yes, Europe is not what it used to be – but it would take a stone-hearted soul not to feel the crackle when the holders Bordeaux-Begles take the field at a packed Kingsholm on Friday night.

A rejuvenated Gloucester in their atmospheric backyard will make for a memorable start to the kings of Europe’s hat-trick quest. Bordeaux, with their galaxy of stars, should have too much for the Cherry and Whites but it is the sort of occasion European club competition was created for.

Rugby.title: Jibulu caps great form with new Sharks deal but Sanderson expects more
Rugby.summary: Sale Sharks boss Alex Sanderson has confirmed that hooker Nathan Jibulu has signed a new deal to stay with the club until 2030, and he has backed the man they call Jibbernaut to secure his place in Steve Borthwick’s England squad for the Nations Championship.
bullets: Sale Sharks head coach Alex Sanderson has confirmed that hooker Nathan Jibulu, 23, has signed a new contract that keeps him at the club until 2030. Jibulu won man of the match awards in the Sharks' Gallagher PREM victories over Saracens and Harlequins in the last two weeks.

Sanderson backed Jibulu to secure a place in Steve Borthwick's England squad for the Nations Championship, noting that Jamie George is set to retire after the World Cup and nobody has challenged Luke Cowan-Dickie as first choice. Doubts remain over the set-piece throwing of Cowan-Dickie and Theo Dan, an area Jibulu improved this summer. Sanderson praised his throwing and scrummaging as well as his ball-carrying, and said forwards coach Mike Forshaw nicknamed him 'Jibbernaut' because he is hard to move in training.
Rugby.copy:
Sale Sharks boss Alex Sanderson has confirmed that hooker Nathan Jibulu has signed a new deal to stay with the club until 2030, and he has backed the man they call Jibbernaut to secure his place in Steve Borthwick’s England squad for the Nations Championship.

Croydon-born Jibulu, 23, has been in superb form for the Sharks this season and has secured man of the match awards in their Gallagher PREM wins over Saracens and Harlequins in the last two weeks.

Rugby.title: Scotland receive unexpected injury boost in time for Nations Championship
Rugby.summary: Darcy Graham will make a remarkably early return from injury after being named in Edinburgh’s starting XV to face Toulon in the Challenge Cup at Hive Stadium on Friday.
bullets: Edinburgh wing Darcy Graham has been named in the starting XV to face Toulon in the Challenge Cup at Hive Stadium on Friday, returning from injury far earlier than expected. The British & Irish Lion ruptured a bicep in the pre-season friendly against Harlequins and was expected to be out for at least 12 weeks, possibly until Christmas.

Graham, 29, is one of two changes from the side that beat Zebre to top the United Rugby Championship table. He replaces Malelili Satala on the right wing, with Satala moving to the left, and Tom Currie starts in the back row for the first time this season. Scotland lock Grant Gilchrist is among the replacements for his first appearance of the season. Head coach Sean Everitt said Toulon carry a huge European pedigree and that a big crowd is expected.
Rugby.copy:
Darcy Graham will make a remarkably early return from injury after being named in Edinburgh’s starting XV to face Toulon in the Challenge Cup at Hive Stadium on Friday. The British & Irish Lions wing was initially expected to miss at least 12 weeks after rupturing a bicep during Edinburgh’s pre-season friendly against Harlequins last month, an injury that appeared likely to keep him sidelined until Christmas.

Instead, Graham has recovered in time to make his first appearance of the season against the French giants, little more than three weeks after Edinburgh head coach Sean Everitt outlined the severity of the problem.

Rugby.title: Isabella Nasser eyes special Sydney occasion as attentions turn to LA28
Rugby.summary: The chance to play at Accor Stadium in Sydney this weekend will hold multiple meanings for Australian Women’s Sevens captain Isabella Nasser, who recently re-signed with the programme through to the 2028 Olympics.
bullets: Australian Women's Sevens captain Isabella Nasser, who recently re-signed with the programme through to the 2028 Olympics, will play New Zealand at the Kick On 7s event on Friday at Accor Stadium in Sydney. She will return on Saturday for the Sydney Quadruple Header, which also features the Wallaroos against Scotland, Australian Men's Sevens against Fiji and the Wallabies against New Zealand in the second Bledisloe Cup match.

Reg Tayler takes charge of the Australian Women's Sevens side for the first time, succeeding Tim Walsh, who is now Director of Women's High Performance. Sione Fukofuka has been named Wallaroos head coach and will lead them towards the 2029 Women's Rugby World Cup. Nasser said her brother, Wallaby Josh Nasser, could play on the same day, which they have never done before. She said the side's aim is Olympic qualification and success at LA28, building on their HSBC SVNS World Championship title earlier this year.
Rugby.copy:
The chance to play at Accor Stadium in Sydney this weekend will hold multiple meanings for Australian Women’s Sevens captain Isabella Nasser, who recently re-signed with the programme through to the 2028 Olympics.

Nasser is set to feature against New Zealand at the Kick On 7s event on Friday before returning to the field for Saturday’s Sydney Quadruple Header. The event will also see the Wallaroos face Scotland, the Australian Men’s Sevens take on Fiji and the Wallabies meet New Zealand in the second Bledisloe Cup clash.

Rugby.title: PREM giants target return of Kyle Sinckler to English shores
Rugby.summary: Saracens are being linked with a bid to bring former England and Lions tighthead Kyle Sinckler back to the Gallagher PREM as he looks to make a dramatic return to Steve Borthwick’s squad to play in a third World Cup.
bullets: Saracens are being linked with a bid to bring Kyle Sinckler, the former England and Lions tighthead, back to the Gallagher PREM from Toulon. The 33-year-old reportedly verbally agreed a new two-year deal with Toulon through 2029 in September but has not signed it, according to Midi Olympique, and the French club are said to be growing unhappy.

Saracens have tightheads Alec Cleary and Tietie Tuimauga in the final year of their contracts. French reports say Bristol Bears are also interested. Sinckler made over 130 appearances for Harlequins, has played 68 times for England and helped Toulon reach the semi-finals of the Champions Cup and Top 14. He was linked with Exeter Chiefs and Newcastle Red Bulls in the summer. He cannot be selected by Steve Borthwick while he plays in France, and Toulon are weighing up other targets.
Rugby.copy:
Saracens are being linked with a bid to bring former England and Lions tighthead Kyle Sinckler back to the Gallagher PREM as he looks to make a dramatic return to Steve Borthwick’s squad to play in a third World Cup.

Sinckler, 33, who entered the final year of his contract with Toulon in July, appeared set to close the door on a return to the PREM in September after verbally agreeing to a new two-year deal with Stade Mayol bosses through 2029.

Rugby.title: Newcastle boss 'relishing' Scarlets challenge
Rugby.summary: Newcastle Red Bulls boss Dan McFarland says he is "relishing" the challenge of facing Scarlets in the European Challenge Cup.
bullets: Newcastle Red Bulls begin their Challenge Cup campaign away at Scarlets on Saturday (20:00 BST), taking a break from the Prem. Head coach Dan McFarland said the Welsh side, coached by Dwayne Peel, play a counter-attacking brand of rugby, have dangerous backs and now have big, heavy forwards too.

Newcastle have lost all three Prem games this season, including a narrow defeat by Exeter Chiefs, but have collected four bonus points. They reached the Challenge Cup last 16 last season, and McFarland wants them to go further. He said there is still plenty of talent in Welsh rugby despite the regions shrinking from four to three.
Rugby.copy:
Newcastle Red Bulls may be escaping from the rigours of the new Prem season, but head coach Dan McFarland is not expecting there to be any let-up as they get set for European action.

Red Bulls take a break from Prem action to begin their Challenge Cup campaign with a trip to Welsh side Scarlets on Saturday (20:00 BST). But for someone like McFarland, vastly experienced within the United Rugby Championship and its previous incarnations from coaching spells with Connacht, Glasgow Warriors and Ulster, he is aware of what his team faces, especially after working alongside Scarlets' Dwayne Peel.

Rugby.title: Bristol sign English-qualified Kiwi with immediate effect as academy prop leaves
Rugby.summary: Bristol Bears have added English-qualified hooker Bryn Gordon to their squad with immediate effect as injury cover for Harry Thacker.
bullets: Bristol Bears have signed English-qualified hooker Bryn Gordon with immediate effect as injury cover for Harry Thacker. The 25-year-old arrives from North Harbour after their National Provincial Championship quarter-final defeat to Taranaki. It is his second stint in the Gallagher PREM, having joined Newcastle Red Bulls in January until the end of last season.

The signing is part of a wider reshuffle in Bristol's front row. Andrew Turner, who first joined the club aged 13 and returned ahead of the current campaign, has agreed fresh terms to extend his second spell at Ashton Gate. Academy loosehead Louie Trevett, the Wales U20 prop, has joined the Ospreys on loan to gain United Rugby Championship minutes while remaining under contract with Bristol. Director of rugby Pat Lam said Gordon would add competition and depth to the squad.
Rugby.copy:
Bristol Bears have added English-qualified hooker Bryn Gordon to their squad with immediate effect as injury cover for Harry Thacker. The 25-year-old has arrived from North Harbour following the conclusion of his National Provincial Championship campaign in New Zealand, where his side lost to Taranaki in the quarter-finals, and gives Pat Lam another option at No.2 as Bristol prepare to balance domestic and European commitments.

This will be the Kiwi’s second stint in the Gallagher PREM having joined Newcastle Red Bulls in January until the end of last season. His arrival is part of a wider reshuffle in the Bears’ front-row, with Andrew Turner committing his future to the club while academy loosehead Louie Trevett has been allowed to leave temporarily in search of senior rugby.

Rugby.title: Spain bids for Rugby World Cup with Nou Camp final
Rugby.summary: Barcelona's Nou Camp, Madrid's Bernabeu and the Mestalla in Valencia are all on a list of possible venues as Spain bids to host the Rugby World Cup in 2035.
bullets: Spain is bidding to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup, with Barcelona's Nou Camp, Real Madrid's Bernabeu and Valencia's Mestalla among the possible stadiums. The revamped Nou Camp is in line to stage the final, which would be the first Rugby World Cup final played before more than 100,000 fans. The bid has the backing of the Spanish government and La Liga, and the Spanish Rugby Federation says it aims to deliver the "best World Cup in history".

Argentina, leading a South American group that would include Brazil, Chile and Uruguay, and Japan are also bidding. World Rugby is expected to name its preferred bidder in spring or summer 2027, with site visits and feasibility assessments starting in December. Spain has submitted 14 stadiums, to be cut to nine or ten if it succeeds, and says 2035 would build on the 2030 Fifa World Cup, which it co-hosts with Morocco and Portugal. The federation aims to triple participation by 2035.
Rugby.copy:
Barcelona's Nou Camp, Real Madrid's Bernabeu and the Mestalla in Valencia are all on a list of possible stadiums as Spain bids to host the Rugby World Cup in 2035. The Spanish Rugby Federation says it aims to deliver the "best World Cup in history", connecting the tournament to 700 million Spanish speakers worldwide.

If Spain's bid is successful, the revamped Nou Camp is in line to host the final, which would be the first time the World Cup showpiece has been held in front of more than 100,000 fans.

Rugby.title: Bristol bring in hooker Gordon as injury cover
Rugby.summary: Bristol sign former Newcastle hooker Bryn Gordon as injury cover for their upcoming games.
bullets: Bristol have signed former Newcastle hooker Bryn Gordon, 25, as injury cover. Harry Thacker is out with a neck injury sustained in the Prem Rugby Cup last month, and Gabriel Oghre has a calf strain suffered in Saturday's defeat by Saracens and is expected to miss a few weeks.

Director of rugby Pat Lam said Gordon would add competition and depth. Gordon made two Prem Rugby Cup appearances for Newcastle and has played for North Harbour in New Zealand. Prop Andrew Turner, 24, has also agreed a new deal after joining from Doncaster, though Bristol have not disclosed contract lengths.
Rugby.copy:
Bristol have signed former Newcastle hooker Bryn Gordon as injury cover for their upcoming games. Gordon comes into the squad with Harry Thacker still out because of a neck injury he sustained while playing in the Prem Rugby Cup last month, with his return date still to be confirmed.

Gabriel Oghre is also unavailable with a calf strain that forced him off at half-time of Bristol's defeat by Saracens on Saturday, and is expected to be out for a few weeks. "With Harry Thacker currently sidelined, it was important for us to strengthen our options at hooker, and Bryn is a talented and hungry player who will add competition and depth to the squad," director of rugby Pat Lam said.

Rugby.title: Seb Stephen: Scotland's newest debutant, an 'absolute monster' raised in a medieval castle
Rugby.summary: The 21-year-old hooker won his first cap in July and is tipped for big things after leaving the family farm and its renovated castle for Glasgow.
bullets: Seb Stephen, a 21-year-old hooker, is Scotland's newest debutant, capped in the July win over Fiji. Head coach Gregor Townsend and forwards coach John Dalziel are admirers, and Townsend believes he has what it takes to make the World Cup squad next autumn.

Stephen grew up at Barra Castle in Aberdeenshire, where his family has farmed for more than 120 years. His father David is a fourth-generation farmer and his mother Sarah is a TV presenter and journalist. After leaving school he was not offered an academy contract and travelled to New Zealand, working as a teacher's aide and playing for the University of Waikato team. He said the relaxed approach there rekindled his love of rugby. A call from then Scotland U20s coach Kenny Murray, who needed hooker cover, brought him home.
Rugby.copy:
Along the B-roads which snake northwest from Aberdeen’s granite hub, where grey turns to green and severe old rock makes way for rolling pasture, sits Barra Castle. This place is steeped in history; a seat from which lairds and nobles once presided over the land; and during a fraught and vengeful time of civil war, much blood was shed. Six years before the Battle of Bannockburn in 1308, King Robert the Bruce rose from his sickbed and bested his rival John Comyn, Earl of Buchan in the shadow of Barra Hill. The king’s triumphant army tore through the countryside, razing to the ground homes and farms belonging to those loyal to the vanquished earl, wiping out any lingering dissention.

These days, the battlefield sits dormant but Barra is a site of thriving enterprise. The Stephen family has farmed here for more than 120 years, and owned the land, the grounds and buildings for over half a century. The castle has been renovated and become their home base.

Rugby.title: How are the Irish provinces shaping up for Europe?
Rugby.summary: BBC Sport NI assesses how the four Irish provinces are tracking before their European campaigns begin on Saturday.
bullets: The Investec Champions Cup begins in October for the first time since 2018, with the final to be held in Lyon. The Irish provinces have played only three United Rugby Championship games beforehand and have started slowly. Leinster, beaten 41-19 by Bordeaux-Begles in last May's final, have lost James Lowe, Rieko Ioane, Rabah Slimani and Ciaran Frawley. Joey Carbery has returned but is yet to play because of injury, and Leinster have won 31 consecutive Champions Cup pool games.

Munster dropped into the Challenge Cup last season after losing at home to Castres in the final pool round, and will be without Jack Crowley for at least the first pool fixtures. Connacht face Saracens, Exeter, La Rochelle and Toulouse, and have won one of their first three league games. Ulster, beaten by Montpellier in last season's Challenge Cup final in Bilbao, are in the Challenge Cup again, alongside Zebre, Dragons, Bayonne and Perpignan.
Rugby.copy:
For the first time since 2018, the Investec Champions Cup begins in October with the road to the final in Lyon starting this weekend. While autumnal fixtures used to be the norm in Europe's top competition, 2026-27 brings an earlier start date than in recent seasons with Irish provinces having just three league games under their collective belts before continental competition kicks off.

After a slow start to their United Rugby Championship (URC) campaigns, how are the sides shaping up to take on the best of the Prem and Top 14? BBC Sport NI takes a look. Leinster remain Ireland's leading light and will be among the biggest threats to Bordeaux-Begles' ambitions of a third title in a row.

Rugby.title: ‘Feared and respected’: Australia captain’s vision before SVNS Series
Rugby.summary: Australian men’s sevens captain Henry Hutchison is approaching his next two years in gold with an increased hunger.
bullets: Australian men's sevens captain Henry Hutchison has signed a new contract that keeps him in sevens until the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The 29-year-old is the most-capped men's player in Australia Sevens history, with 68 events and over 350 games. He will play at the Kick On 7s event on Friday and against Fiji in the Sydney quadruple-header on Saturday.

Hutchison wants Australia to be feared and respected on the circuit, after the team lost the 2024 Paris Olympics bronze medal match 26-19 to South Africa. He played in India's Rugby Premier League and the Ultimate Sevens in Europe in the off-season. The squad will then play the All Blacks Sevens and Samoa in New Zealand ahead of the 2026-27 SVNS Series, where the top four earn Olympic qualification. New faces include Dane Mitchell and Tylan Berryman, with Josh Coward returning.
Rugby.copy:
One of the most decorated players in the HSBC SVNS competition, Australian men’s sevens captain Henry Hutchison is approaching his next two years in gold with an increased hunger, fresh off signing a new contract that will keep him in sevens until the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

The 29-year-old Hutchison is the most-capped men’s player in Australia Sevens history, with 68 events and over 350 games under his belt, and is set to take the field for the Kick On 7s event on Friday and the Sydney quadruple-header on Saturday against Fiji.

Rugby.summary: ‘Feared and respected’: Australia captain’s vision before SVNS Series Rugbypass.com
bullets: Australian men's sevens captain Henry Hutchison, 29, has signed a new contract that will keep him in sevens until the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Hutchison named gold in LA as the goal and said he wants the team to be respected on the circuit. The 29-year-old Hutchison is the most-capped men’s player in Australia Sevens history, with 68 events and over 350 games under his belt, and is set to take the field for the Kick On 7s event on Friday and the Sydney quadruple-header on Saturday against Fiji.

Rugby.title: Wales players in Prem can help Welsh game
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs' Dafydd Jenkins says the influx of Wales players into the English Prem can help improve the game in his homeland.
bullets: Exeter lock Dafydd Jenkins, 23, said the influx of Wales players into the English Prem can help Welsh rugby. Wales captain Jac Morgan and Dewi Lake moved from Ospreys to Gloucester in the summer and featured in the win at Jenkins' Chiefs on the opening day.

Jenkins said their departures open space for young Welsh hookers and back-rowers in the United Rugby Championship. He missed Wales' July Nations Championship games against South Africa, Argentina and Fiji after a shoulder operation following Exeter's Prem final defeat by Northampton Saints in June. He has started all three of Exeter's league games this season.
Rugby.copy:
Dafydd Jenkins says the influx of Wales players into the English Prem can help improve the game in his homeland. Exeter lock Jenkins, 23, has spent all his senior career at Sandy Park, and is one of a growing list of Wales' top players to ply their trade across the border.

Wales captain Jac Morgan and compatriot Dewi Lake were the highest-profile summer additions after they moved from Ospreys to Gloucester, and featured in the Cherry and Whites' opening day win at Jenkins' Chiefs.

Rugby.title: The Welsh back-row trio starring for Leicester
Rugby.summary: How Wales forwards Aaron Wainwright, Olly Cracknell and Tommy Reffell have been key to Leicester Tigers' good start to the season.
bullets: Welsh back-rowers Aaron Wainwright, Olly Cracknell and Tommy Reffell have started all three of Leicester's Prem games together, with wins over Newcastle and Gloucester and a narrow defeat to Saracens. Wainwright and Reffell have played as flankers with Cracknell at number eight, and Wainwright set up Gabriel Hamer-Webb's try against Saracens on his debut.

Wainwright, 29, joined from Dragons after 138 matches and 70 Wales caps, and has yet to play in the Champions Cup, which Leicester begin away at Pau on Sunday. He and Jac Morgan are certainties for Steve Tandy's Nations Championship squad, due next week, while Reffell and Cracknell face stiff competition for places.
Rugby.copy:
Wainwright, Cracknell and Reffell. Not an accountancy firm, even if it sounds like one, but the trio of Welsh back-rowers whose numbers are stacking up at Leicester this season.

To give them their full names, Aaron Wainwright, Olly Cracknell and Tommy Reffell have starred in Leicester's encouraging start to the season. The trio had never played together before but have started all Leicester's three league games together, with victories coming against Newcastle and Gloucester and a narrow defeat to Saracens.

Rugby.title: The Champions Cup Is Back: Conan, Big Will Skelton & More
Rugby.summary: Ashy & Sara chat to Will Skelton, Jack Conan & Nathan Hughes at the Champions Cup launch.
Rugby.copy: Ashy and Sara are at the Champions Cup launch speaking to a host of big names ahead of the opening round. Jack Conan reflects on the heartbreak of losing another final and the criticism Leinster receive over their Champions Cup record. Can they finally adda fifth star or will the French dominance continue? Ashy is reunited with his old team-mate 'big' Will Skelton, who gives us a the lowdown on why Ronan O'Gara is loved in La Rochelle and what has changed following last year's surprise exit. Nathan Hughes talks about life in Paris at Racing 92 and how a routine pre-season eye check-up saved his sight. Plus, former Wasps back row Nizaam Carr explains just how tough it is playing rugby during Ramadan and why the Champions Cup has struggled to capture the imagination in South Africa.

Rugby.title: UAE rugby teams head to Colombo for Asia Rugby Sevens
Rugby.summary: UAE rugby teams head to Colombo for Asia Rugby Sevens برق الإمارات
Rugby.copy:
The UAE men’s and women’s national rugby teams will compete in the second leg of the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series 2026, scheduled for Saturday and Sunday in Colombo, Sri Lanka.

The UAE Rugby Federation announced in a statement that the delegation will depart for Colombo tomorrow, led by Secretary-General Mohamed Sultan Al Zaabi, ahead of the competition.

Rugby.title: Cokayne back as England face Canada threat in Toronto
Rugby.summary: England welcome back the experience of Amy Cokayne at hooker as their 41-match unbeaten run comes under serious threat away to Canada.
bullets: England's Red Roses bring back hooker Amy Cokayne, who has 94 caps, as their 41-match unbeaten run faces Rugby World Cup runners-up Canada in Toronto on Friday. Cokayne has not played Test rugby since scoring in the Grand Slam-sealing win over France in Bordeaux in May, and Bryony Field drops to the bench.

Canada ended England's near four-year winning streak with a 26-26 draw at Sandy Park in Exeter last month. The Toronto attendance is expected to exceed 14,000, which would beat the North American record of 11,453 for a standalone women's rugby match. The sides meet again in Ottawa on Friday, 23 October.
Rugby.copy:
England welcome back the experienced Amy Cokayne at hooker as their 41-match unbeaten run goes on the line against Rugby World Cup runners-up Canada in Toronto on Friday. Cokayne has not played Test rugby since scoring the Red Roses' final try in a Grand Slam-sealing win over France in Bordeaux in May.

Saracens' Bryony Field, who has three caps to Cokayne's 94, drops to the bench after deputising impressively in the first half of the WXV Global Series last month. During that part of the campaign, Canada ended England's near four-year winning streak with a nail-biting 26-26 draw at Sandy Park in Exeter.

Rugby.title: Amy Cokayne returns as Red Roses plot revenge on Canada
Rugby.summary: England had their 39-match winning run ended by Canada in Exeter last month
bullets: England hooker Amy Cokayne returns to the starting XV for the first of two Tests against Canada in Toronto, kicking off at midnight BST on Saturday 17 October at BMO Field. The Red Roses had their 39-match winning run ended by the World Cup runners-up in a 26-all draw at Sandy Park in Exeter last month. Cokayne missed England's September home fixtures through injury but has been passed fit.

Tatyana Heard also returns at inside centre, while Hannah Botterman and Abi Burton feature in the other changes. Alex Matthews plays openside with Marlie Packer at home ahead of the birth of a child, and Sadia Kabeya is on the bench. Head coach John Mitchell said the team is focused on raising its level as it builds towards 2029. The games in Toronto and Ottawa form part of the WXV Global Series.
Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. England have been boosted by the return of hooker Amy Cokayne as they plot revenge on Canada in the first of back-to-back Test meetings.

The Red Roses had their 39-match winning run ended by the World Cup runners-up in Exeter last month, with John Mitchell’s side held to a 26-all draw at Sandy Park. The two teams now meet in games in Toronto and Ottawa that form part of the WXV Global Series, and have been regarded internally within England camp as a three-Test series.

Rugby.title: Wales centre Thomas to miss Nations Championship restart
Rugby.summary: Centre Ben Thomas is set to miss the opening games of the Nations Championship but Taulupe Faletau is expected to play before November.
bullets: Wales centre Ben Thomas is set to miss the start of the Nations Championship with a calf injury, according to Cardiff head coach Corniel van Zyl. Wales open against Japan on 7 November at the Principality Stadium, followed by home games against New Zealand and Australia, with Steve Tandy naming his squad next week.

Taulupe Faletau, 35, was withdrawn just before kick-off in Cardiff's 29-5 URC defeat by Leinster, with Taine Basham stepping in. Van Zyl said Faletau is 100% expected to play within the next couple of weeks, starting with Sunday's Champions Cup opener at Northampton. Basham, 26, has 17 caps and is in strong form at number eight.
Rugby.copy:
Wales centre Ben Thomas is set to miss the start of the Nations Championship but Cardiff team-mate Taulupe Faletau is expected to feature before the tournament returns in November.

Wales head coach Steve Tandy names his autumn squad next week, with the opening match against Japan on 7 November at the Principality Stadium followed by further home matches against New Zealand and Australia.

Rugby.title: Black Ferns' Mererangi Paul reflects on 'big year' ahead of WXV Global Series
Rugby.summary: Clinical. The word that can be heard on repeat as the Black Ferns prepare to face France in Hamilton on Saturday in the first of three WXV Global Series Tests this October.
bullets: The Black Ferns face France in Hamilton on Saturday in the first of three WXV Global Series Tests this October. Winger Mererangi Paul, who has scored 20 tries in 21 Tests, said the squad has had the word "clinical" drilled into them after narrowly losing to England at Twickenham in September, where the scores were level at 19-19 before an intercepted pass late on.

The Black Ferns beat France 28-14 in Lyon in their WXV opener, with Paul scoring from a line-out drive. The two sides have met 14 times since 1996, with New Zealand leading 9-5. Paul was recalled in April under new coach Whitney Hansen, scoring three tries against the USA. She has since moved from Chiefs Manawa to the Blues and said the lack of a break this year has helped her focus on her game.
Rugby.copy:
Clinical. The word that can be heard on repeat as the Black Ferns prepare to face France in Hamilton on Saturday in the first of three WXV Global Series Tests this October. While the Black Ferns pushed the 2025 Rugby World Cup Champions England to the brink at Twickenham in September, there’s a sense they threw it away.

Amy du Plessis literally did with the clock in the red when her pass was intercepted by Zoe Harrison with the score level at 19-19. Earlier, England had made 188 more tackles than the visitors, with Mererangi Paul scoring a try in the 70th minute to tie the scores.

Rugby.title: Capital gains: Have Edinburgh finally found the elusive winning formula?
Rugby.summary: The season is still in its infancy but the signs are the early URC leaders appear to be finally heading in the right direction.
bullets: Edinburgh top the United Rugby Championship with a 100 per cent record after three rounds, following wins over Ulster, Stormers and Zebre. It is their best start since 2015-16, when they won their first four Pro12 games before finishing ninth. They have done so despite starting the campaign with 16 players on the injured list, including Darcy Graham, Duhan van der Merwe, Wes Goosen and Grant Gilchrist.

Last season, Edinburgh lost three of their opening four league games and finished 12th, 16 points off the top eight. Head coach Sean Everitt was handed a two-year contract extension in January. Edinburgh host Toulon in the Challenge Cup on Friday, then face the Johannesburg Lions at home and Benetton away. New assistant coaches Tim Sampson and Brad Davis have bedded in new systems, and Ewan Ashman and Marshall Sykes have returned from injury.
Rugby.copy:
Casual observers of the United Rugby Championship may not be overly surprised to see a Scottish team heading up the table after the opening three rounds of the new campaign. Glasgow, after all, have been a familiar presence among the top four under Franco Smith, winning the title in 2024, leading the league for large chunks of last term and finishing top of the pile after the regular season.

But Edinburgh? The maddeningly inconsistent, perennial under-achievers across the other end of the M8? Even to those who follow the competition assiduously, the presence of the Scottish capital outfit out front, with a 100 per cent record from three games, elicits a double take.

Rugby.title: Tom Roebuck outlines 'big part' of career plans after new Sale deal
Rugby.summary: Tom Roebuck has committed his future to Sale Sharks after signing a new two-year contract with his boyhood club.
bullets: Tom Roebuck has signed a new two-year contract with Sale Sharks that runs until at least the end of the 2028/29 season. The 25-year-old England wing has made 114 appearances and scored 54 tries since his senior debut in a PREM Rugby Cup defeat to Worcester in 2018. He has missed the opening three rounds of the Gallagher PREM with a calf strain.

Roebuck was left out after England's disappointing Six Nations and omitted from Steve Borthwick's original Nations Championship squad. He was added when George Furbank underwent appendix surgery but did not feature. He said playing for England is a big part of his career plans and that Sale is the best place to pursue them. Director of rugby Alex Sanderson said Roebuck has an X-factor that very few other players have.
Rugby.copy:
Tom Roebuck has committed his future to Sale Sharks after signing a new two-year contract with his boyhood club. The new deal will keep the England wing at Sale until at least the end of the 2028/29 season, extending an association that began in the club’s academy.

Roebuck has made 114 appearances and scored 54 tries since making his senior debut in a PREM Rugby Cup defeat to Worcester in 2018, having previously played his junior rugby at Chester Rugby Club.

Rugby.title: Sale winger Roebuck signs deal to end of 2028-29
Rugby.summary: Sale Sharks winger Tom Roebuck signs a new deal to remain with the Prem club for a further two years.
bullets: Sale Sharks winger Tom Roebuck has signed a new two-year deal that keeps him at the Prem club until the end of 2028-29. The 25-year-old England international came through the academy and has made 114 appearances and scored 54 tries since his 2018 debut. He has missed the first three league games of 2026-27 with a calf strain.

Roebuck, who has won 12 England caps since making his debut against Japan in 2024, said Sale is home and the club he supported as a child. He said he wants to be part of a Sale team that goes one better after reaching a semi-final and a final in recent years. Director of rugby Alex Sanderson said Roebuck has developed into one of the best wingers in the Prem and is a big part of how the club want to play going forward.
Rugby.copy:
Sale Sharks winger Tom Roebuck has signed a new deal to remain with the Prem club for a further two years. The 25-year-old England international progressed through the club's academy and has made a total of 114 appearances for Sale.

Since making his debut in 2018 he has scored 54 tries for the club but has so far missed the first three league games of 2026-27 due to a calf strain. "For me, Sale Sharks is home. It's the club I supported as a child, it's where I've grown up and it's all I know. I love it here and I couldn't see myself playing anywhere else," he said., external

bullets: Premier Sports face a battle to retain UK and Ireland rights to the Champions Cup and Challenge Cup, with their deal entering its third and final year. Coverage begins on Friday at Kingsholm, where Gloucester host defending champions Bordeaux-Begles. All 63 Champions Cup matches will be shown live, along with two Challenge Cup pool matches per round, two Round of 16 ties and all knockout matches from the quarter-finals.

Premier Sports replaced TNT Sports in 2024 in a deal reportedly worth £6m, after a £14m TNT offer was reportedly rejected. TNT's new owner Paramount Skydance, whose takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery is complete, appears to have cash to boost a diminishing portfolio. Premier Sports saw a 27% uplift in audience reach at the end of last season's pool stages, but only 23,000 watched the final between Bordeaux-Begles and Leinster on linear or connected TV, according to Barb.
Rugby.copy:

Rugby.title: 'Revamped' France ready for WXV Global Series tour of New Zealand
Rugby.summary: It was just one win. But it meant something more.
bullets: France head to New Zealand for the southern hemisphere leg of the WXV Global Series with a 2-1 record from their opening three games. They beat Canada 21-5 at La Rochelle in September, their first win over a top-three side since beating New Zealand 18-17 in October 2023. That followed a comeback victory over Australia in Provence a week earlier.

Head coach Francois Ratier said the squad will be slightly revamped and rejuvenated, with the focus on progress towards the 2029 Women's Rugby World Cup in Australia. Alexandra Chambon will captain the side. Scrum-half Pauline Bourdon Sansus has stayed in France for family reasons, while Cloé Correa and Ambre Mwayembe miss the opening Test through suspension. Usual captain Manae Feleu is studying for medical exams, and Madoussou Fall Raclot is pregnant.
Rugby.copy:
It was just one win. But it meant something more. France head to the southern hemisphere leg of their WXV Global Series campaign with something of a collective spring in their steps after their 21-5 victory over Canada at La Rochelle in September.

It was just one win, but it was a win over last year’s Women’s Rugby World Cup finalists, and it was Les Bleues’ first against a top three side since October 2023, when they beat New Zealand 18-17.

Rugby.title: Cornish Pirates seek to understand away day woes
Rugby.summary: Cornish Pirates coach Joe Walsh says the club is trying to understand their poor away form.
bullets: Cornish Pirates coach Joe Walsh says the club is trying to understand their poor away form after a 38-14 defeat at Bedford on Saturday. That followed a 73-40 loss at Coventry two weeks earlier, in which they conceded 11 tries. Pirates are eighth in the 14-team Champ, having won half of their games so far this season.

At the Mennaye Field, Pirates inflicted Ealing's first league defeat in 18 months and opened the season with a seven-try 45-19 win over Doncaster. Walsh told BBC Radio Cornwall that the team are chasing consistency, particularly away from home, and looked flat in both away warm-ups. He said the players were energised in warm-ups for the two home games. He added that many factors are at play, making it hard to pinpoint an exact cause.
Rugby.copy:
Cornish Pirates coach Joe Walsh says the club is trying to understand their poor away form. Pirates were beaten 38-14 at Bedford on Saturday, having conceded 11 tries in a 73-40 loss at Coventry two weeks before.

The results are in stark contrast to their form at the Mennaye Field where Pirates inflicted a first league loss on high-flying Ealing in 18 months having opened the season with a seven-try 45-19 win over Doncaster.

Rugby.title: How humble Pau are slowly turning into Top 14 powerhouse
Rugby.summary: Pau head coach Sébastien Piqueronies is slowly building a serious Top 14 outfit, not through superstars, but great coaching
bullets: Pau, who host Leicester in the Champions Cup on Sunday, are second in the Top 14 behind Toulouse with five wins from six matches. Their budget is 33.9m euros, compared with Toulouse's 60.8m euros. Last season they finished fourth and reached the play-offs for the first time in 26 years.

The turnaround followed the appointment of Sébastien Piqueronies as manager in the summer of 2021, after he led France U20s to world titles in 2018 and 2019. Pau were relegated to the ProD2 in 2005-06, took a decade to return and last won the Top 14 in 1964. Piqueronies signed Dan Robson, Joe Simmonds and Sam Whitelock, and has blended them with young players such as Fabien Brau-Boirie and Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang.
Rugby.copy:
When the draw for the Champions Cup pools was made the likes of Leinster and Leicester in Pool One must have breathed a sigh of relief. They’d avoided the big boys of the Top 14: no Bordeaux, no Toulouse, no La Rochelle and no Racing.

This quartet has appeared in at least one of the last seven Champions Cup finals. And, of course, there is also Montpellier, who thrashed Ulster 59-26 in the final of last season’s Challenge Cup.

He limped out early in the second half of Sunday's win over Newcastle Red Bulls and could be absent for only a week.

Baxter hopes Feyi-Waboso can return for the trip to Bristol Bears a week on Saturday, leaving a fortnight's rest before England face Australia at Twickenham on 8 November. He is the fourth Chiefs winger out injured, alongside Campbell Ridl, Olly Woodburn and Paul Brown-Bampoe. Baxter said the player reports little discomfort and tests well, and that an England physio assessed the scan and the player.
Rugby.copy:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter has ruled England flyer Immanuel Feyi-Waboso out of Sunday’s Champions Cup trip to Toulouse, but a scan cleared him of serious hamstring damage, so he could be out for only a week.

Feyi-Waboso, who scored two tries in the Gallagher PREM defeat at Bath, limped out of Sunday’s win over Newcastle Red Bulls early in the second half, but any fears he could face another lengthy lay-off have now been dispelled.

Rugby.title: Winger Feyi-Waboso should be fit for England
Rugby.summary: England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso should be fit to feature in next month's Nations Championship matches.
bullets: England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso should be fit for next month's Nations Championship after a scan on a hamstring injury showed a positive prognosis. The 23-year-old came off 15 minutes into the second half of Exeter's 34-28 Prem win over Newcastle on Sunday, and will miss Exeter's European Champions Cup trip to Toulouse.

Exeter director of rugby Rob Baxter said the club's physios did not expect a long-term issue, with the scan showing little and testing going well. As a centrally contracted player, the final say on his treatment rests with England, whose first of their last three Nations Championship games is against Australia at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium on 8 November. Exeter are also without wingers Campbell Ridl, Olly Woodburn and Paul Brown-Bampoe for the Toulouse trip.
Rugby.copy:
England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso should be fit to feature in next month's Nations Championship after a scan on a hamstring injury revealed a positive prognosis. The 23-year-old came off 15 minutes into the second half of Exeter's 34-28 Prem win over Newcastle on Sunday.

Feyi-Waboso missed this year's Six Nations after hurting his hamstring in January but has started every league game for Exeter this season - although he will be absent for Sunday's European Champions Cup trip to French champions Toulouse.

Rugby.summary: The British and Irish Lions are to take on France at Cardiff's Principality Stadium before their historic three-Test 2027 tour to New Zealand.
bullets: The British and Irish Lions women will play their first-ever fixture against France at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on Friday, 27 August (19:30 BST), ahead of their 2027 tour to New Zealand. Jo Yapp's side then face a Black Ferns XV in Whangarei the following weekend, before the first of three Tests with New Zealand on 11 September.

The five-match tour includes Tests in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch. Lions women's committee chair Carol Isherwood said the Welsh Rugby Union had argued it could stage the occasion well, and that the match is a chance to grow the game and leave a legacy. France, ranked fourth in the world, were 2025 World Cup semi-finalists and have been runners-up to England in the last seven Six Nations; a record 21,186 watched Wales women lose to England at the Principality Stadium in 2025.
Rugby.copy:
The British and Irish Lions will play a historic first women's fixture when they face France at Cardiff's Principality Stadium before their 2027 tour to New Zealand. Jo Yapp's side will face the French, ranked fourth in the world, in the Welsh capital on Friday, 27 August (19:30 BST).

The Lions face a Black Ferns XV the following weekend in Whangarei before the first of three Tests with New Zealand on 11 September. "There are moments in sport that only come around once - and this is one of them," said head coach Yapp.

Rugby.title: Courtney Lawes and Ellis Genge call for change to England’s overseas player policy: ‘I don’t think it’s fair’
Rugby.summary: Currently, only players based in England are eligible for international selection
bullets: Former England captains Ellis Genge and Courtney Lawes have called for the RFU to lift its restriction on picking overseas-based players, saying internationals with a certain number of caps should stay eligible while playing in France. It is the first time senior England players have spoken out against the rule, which is designed to protect the Gallagher Prem and give head coach Steve Borthwick greater control over his players.

Lawes, who has 105 caps and recently returned from two years in the Top 14, pointed to Wales' 25-cap threshold as a possible compromise on The Good, The Bad and The Rugby podcast. Genge, who has 83 caps, suggested 50 or 60 caps and said he had spoken to RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney but was yet to be convinced the rule is necessary. He cited Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane as examples of overseas moves helping players.

Racket.copy:
Former top-30 player Giovanni Mpetschi Perricard has opened up on his “depression and burnout” after sliding down the rankings. The big Frenchman enjoyed a breakthrough year in 2024, rising to 31st in the world and picking up his first ATP Tour titles in Lyon and Basel.

The 6ft 7in player beat the likes of Felix Auger-Aliassime, Holger Rune, and Ben Shelton at the Swiss Indoors, as his booming serve proved too hot to handle. Just when it seemed like the then 21-year-old, who holds the record for the fastest serve at Wimbledon at 153mph, would become the next big thing in French tennis, Mpetschi Perricard‘s progress has come to a grinding halt.

Racket.title: Inside British number one Kartal's remarkable comeback
Racket.summary: Six months ago, Sonay Kartal could not brush her teeth without "being in agony" - now she's the British number one after three events back from a long-term back injury.
bullets: Sonay Kartal, 24, became British number one on Monday after reaching the Wuhan Open final in only her third tournament back from a stress fracture in her back. Using a protected ranking, she rose from 170th to 49th by earning 650 points, and became the first British player to reach a WTA 1000 final since Johanna Konta in 2019. She lost the final to French Open runner-up Maja Chwalinska.

Kartal said she was unable to walk without pain for about the first month of her injury and credited coach Ben Reeves, fitness coach Ian Aylward and physio Dani Gillanders. Regaining her ranking means she will no longer need a protected ranking for events including the 2027 Australian Open. She withdrew from the Japan Open in Osaka, saying the goals of her Asian swing had been achieved.
Racket.copy:
Six months ago, Sonay Kartal could not stand up and brush her teeth without "being in agony". The pain caused by a stress fracture in her back eventually subsided, but the 24-year-old Briton still had a long road to full recovery, which needed to be navigated with patience and hard work.

Kartal did not make her return to competitive action until little under a month ago. But on Monday, she became the new British number one after an extraordinary week at the Wuhan Open, where she reached the biggest final of her career in just her third tournament back.

Racket.title: Sonay Kartal: What next for new British No 1 after 'unbelievable week' in run to the final at Wuhan Open
Racket.summary: Sonay Kartal: What next for new British No 1 after 'unbelievable week' in run to the final at Wuhan Open Sky Sports
bullets: Sonay Kartal became the new British No 1 after reaching the Wuhan Open final, where she lost 2-6 6-4 6-2 to Poland's Maja Chwalinska. She became only the second Briton after Johanna Konta to play a WTA 1000 final, beating Belinda Bencic, Jasmine Paolini, Elina Svitolina and Jelena Ostapenko along the way.

The 24-year-old had returned only last month after six months out with a stress fracture in her back, which forced her to retire from the fourth round at Indian Wells in March. She can use her protected ranking for 12 months, and may withdraw from the Japan Open in Osaka before ending her season at WTA 500 or 250 events in China, Hong Kong and India.
Racket.copy:
Britain's Sonay Kartal enjoyed the best week of her career so far as she surprisingly made the final at the Wuhan Open; Kartal only recently returned from injury, so what is her potential and can she kick on? Watch the Japan Open all this week, live on Sky Sports Tennis

Sonay Kartal is the new British No 1 after her remarkable run to the Wuhan Open final where she was narrowly beaten by Poland's Maja Chwalinska in three sets. Kartal became just the second Briton, after Johanna Konta, to play in a WTA 1000 final with superb wins over Tokyo Olympic champion Belinda Bencic, two-time Grand Slam finalist Jasmine Paolini, world No 6 Elina Svitolina and former French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko.

Racket.title: Denmark Says Thank You to Axelsen
Racket.summary: Denmark Says Thank You to Axelsen BWF
bullets: Danish badminton paid tribute to Viktor Axelsen in his home city of Odense on Sunday at the SJF Bank Arena, where he was presented with flowers. Odense Mayor Peter Rahbaek Juel and Badminton Denmark Chief Executive Kristian Pihl delivered tributes, with Pihl thanking Axelsen for the journey, the memories and everything he had given Danish badminton.

Axelsen's achievements include two Olympic gold medals, two world titles, four European crowns and a place in the Danish team that won the country's first Thomas Cup in 2016. He also spent years at the top of the world rankings in men's singles. Thanking fans, sponsors, family and friends, he said he started playing in Odense and almost hit his last shuttlecock there as well.
Racket.copy:
Danish badminton paid tribute to its greatest modern player Viktor Axelsen in his home city of Odense on Sunday. At the SJF Bank Arena, Axelsen was presented with flowers before receiving heartfelt tributes from the Mayor of Odense Peter Rahbaek Juel and Badminton Denmark Chief Executive Kristian Pihl. Their message was simple.

“We have come together to say thank you,” said Pihl. “Thank you, Viktor for the journey, the memories and everything you have given Danish badminton.” For nearly two decades, Axelsen carried Danish hopes on the biggest stages in world sports. He became a global ambassador for badminton, inspired a new generation of players and built a legacy few can match.

Racket.title: Denmark Open: An-Stoppable Force
Racket.summary: Denmark Open: An-Stoppable Force BWF World Tour
bullets: An Se Young won her 47th international title at the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026, beating Akane Yamaguchi 21-23 21-14 21-18 in the final. The world No.1 trailed 11-5 at the interval of the deciding game before taking 11 of the next 12 points. The win made her the most decorated women's singles player in international badminton, one title clear of Indonesia's Susi Susanti.

An, 24, slipped during the second game and said she would check her condition and speak to her trainer before deciding what to do next. She said the slower side of the court in the decider helped her confidence. She has now faced Yamaguchi 39 times and described her as her best rival, also naming Wang Zhi Yi and Chen Yu Fei as rivals.
Racket.copy:
Down 11-5 at the decider’s interval, An Se Young looked destined to wait another week for her landmark victory. Then, in that moment of doubt, the champion fans know best emerged.

Eleven of the next 12 points fell her way and suddenly there was no stopping the world No.1 from claiming her 47th title. The triumph, a hard-fought 21-23 21-14 21-18 victory over Akane Yamaguchi in the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026 final, made her the most decorated women’s singles player in international badminton, moving one title clear of Indonesian great Susi Susanti.

Racket.title: Inspiring story of the day: “My parents were very hard to please, but it shaped my resilience” - How Emma
Racket.summary: Inspiring story of the day: “My parents were very hard to please, but it shaped my resilience” - How Emma The Times of India
bullets: Emma Raducanu won the 2021 US Open at the age of 18 without dropping a set in 10 matches, becoming the first qualifier in the Open Era to win a Grand Slam singles title. She won three qualifying matches and seven main-draw rounds, beating Greece's Maria Sakkari in the semi-finals and Canada's Leylah Fernandez 6-4, 6-3 in the final.

Raducanu has said her strict upbringing in Bromley, south London, built her resilience. Her Romanian father Ian and Chinese mother Renee Zhai, both of whom worked in finance, set high expectations, and she earned an A* in mathematics and an A in economics at A-level in 2021. She said her parents' limits on her social life left her comfortable in her own company, and credits her mother's 'step by step' advice for her calmness.
Racket.copy:
Emma Raducanu made tennis history at 18 when she won the 2021 US Open without dropping a set in 10 matches, becoming the first qualifier in the Open Era to win a Grand Slam singles title. Her success came after years of balancing tennis training with schoolwork and living under her parents’ high expectations. Born in Toronto to Romanian father Ian Raducanu and Chinese mother Renee Zhai, she moved to England as a young child. Raducanu has often spoken about how her strict upbringing helped her become more independent, focused and resilient.

How did Ian Raducanu and Renee Zhai shape Emma Raducanu’s childhood? Emma Raducanu grew up in Bromley, south London, in a family that placed a strong focus on education and hard work. Her father, Ian, is Romanian, while her mother, Renee, is Chinese. Both worked in finance and encouraged their daughter to take her responsibilities seriously, both in the classroom and on the tennis court.

Racket.title: Alex Lanier wins Denmark Open 2026
Racket.summary: Alex Lanier wins Denmark Open 2026 Badminton Europe
bullets: Alex Lanier won the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026 in his first tournament since becoming World Champion, beating home favourite Anders Antonsen 21-15, 13-21, 21-13 in an all-European final. The Frenchman took the opening game, Antonsen levelled in the second, and Lanier then raised his intensity in the decider.

Lanier said the third game required more physicality, aggressiveness and pace, and admitted the title was a surprise. Antonsen, who had won the Arctic Open the previous Sunday before reaching his third Denmark Open final, said he was proud but also sad and disappointed. The BWF World Tour continues with the French Open 2026, a Super 750 event in Paris starting on Tuesday, 20 October.
Racket.copy:
Alex Lanier claimed the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026 title in his first tournament since becoming World Champion, defeating home favourite Anders Antonsen 21-15, 13-21, 21-13 in an all-European final.

The Frenchman took the opening game, but Antonsen responded strongly in the second to force a decider. With the title at stake, Lanier raised his intensity and eventually secured another major triumph.

Racket.title: How Rafael Jodar’s Shanghai Masters run has affected the ATP Finals qualification battle
Racket.summary: Jodar lost his maiden Masters 1000 final, but he has boosted his ATP Finals hopes. The post How Rafael Jodar’s Shanghai Masters run has affected the ATP Finals qualification battle appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Rafael Jodar lost the Shanghai Masters final 1-6, 7-6(5), 6-4 to fellow Spaniard Alejandro Davidovich Fokina on Sunday, having come within two points of victory in the second-set tiebreak. The 20-year-old world No 13 earned 650 ranking points as runner-up, lifting him from 11th to ninth in the Race to Turin on 3,159 points. He now leads De Minaur in 10th by 279 points and Novak Djokovic in 11th by 319.

The top eight in the Race qualify for the ATP Finals in Turin, but Jannik Sinner, second in the Race, will not play again in 2026, so ninth place is now the final qualifying spot. Jodar is 166 points behind Arthur Fils in eighth, 221 behind Frances Tiafoe in seventh and 261 behind Daniil Medvedev in sixth. The Paris Masters, from 2-8 November, is the last tournament where points count towards qualification.
Racket.copy:
Rafael Jodar was denied a maiden Masters 1000 title as he lost to Alejandro Davidovich Fokina in the Shanghai final, but how has the result affected the ATP Race to Turin? The 20-year-old was beaten 1-6, 7-6(5), 6-4 by his Spanish compatriot Davidovich Fokina on Sunday after coming within two points of victory in the second set tiebreak.

World No 13 Jodar was playing the biggest final of his career to date, and he was vying for his second ATP Tour title, having triumphed in Marrakech at the start of the clay-court season.

Racket.title: Annabel Croft explains why she thinks Emma Raducanu ending her 2026 season now would be a smart decision
Racket.summary: Annabel Croft explains why she thinks Emma Raducanu ending her 2026 season now would be a smart decision Tennishead
bullets: Annabel Croft has said that Emma Raducanu ending her 2026 season now would be a sensible decision, speaking on Sky Sports Tennis. Raducanu has not competed since June, when she suffered a stress fracture in her lower right leg after reaching the Queen's final, which she lost to Donna Vekic. Croft said a break would let Raducanu heal fully, rest and start next year fit, adding that health is the most important factor.

The 23-year-old is ranked 107th, having dropped out of the top 100, and has played 21 matches in 2026, winning 11. She lost in the second round of the Australian Open to Anastasia Potapova and in the first round of the French Open to Solana Sierra. Croft noted the ranking-points concern but said Raducanu might benefit from a protected ranking. Jannik Sinner, Joao Fonseca and Amanda Anisimova have also ended their seasons early.
Racket.copy:
Emma Raducanu ending her 2026 WTA season now could be a wise move, according to Annabel Croft. The former professional has analysed the current struggles of the WTA superstar, who has not competed since June after suffering a stress fracture in her lower right leg. Raducanu reached the final of Queen’s back then, which she lost to Donna Vekic.

But after that fantastic run on home soil, she has been forced out of a long list of WTA tournaments, including Wimbledon and the US Open. Her absence has now continued into the Asian Swing, with Croft suggesting that the 2021 US Open champion ending her difficult season now would not be the worst decision at all.

Racket.title: Sonay Kartal misses out on maiden WTA 1000 title in Wuhan Open final defeat to Maja Chwalinska
Racket.summary: Sonay Kartal misses out on maiden WTA 1000 title in Wuhan Open final defeat to Maja Chwalinska Sky Sports
bullets: Britain's Sonay Kartal lost the Wuhan Open final 2-6 6-4 6-2 to Poland's Maja Chwalinska after leading by a set and a break. She would have become the second Briton after Johanna Konta to win a WTA 1000 title, and had been ranked 170th before the event after a six-month lay-off with a back injury.

Kartal's run, which included wins over Belinda Bencic, Jasmine Paolini, Elina Svitolina and Jelena Ostapenko, returns her to the top 50 and makes her British number one on Monday. In the Shanghai Masters final, Spain's Alejandro Davidovich Fokina won his first ATP 1000 title, beating compatriot Rafael Jodar 1-6 7-6 (7-5) 6-4, and will rise to 13th in the rankings.
Racket.copy:
Britain's Sonay Kartal was beaten in a deciding set by Poland's Maja Chwalinska in a pulsating Wuhan Open final. Kartal led by a set and a break as she looked to become just the second Briton, after Johanna Konta, to win a WTA 1000 title but French Open finalist Chwalinska produced a superb display to fight back and win 2-6 6-4 6-2.

Nevertheless, it has still been a remarkable week for Kartal, the best in her career so far, after only returning to the tour earlier this month following a six-month lay-off due to a back injury.
