bullets: Maja Chwalinska won her first WTA 1000 title, and her first on the WTA Tour at any level, beating Sonay Kartal 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 in the Wuhan Open final after coming back from a set and a break down. The 25-year-old, a French Open finalist as a qualifier earlier this season, will now move towards the top 10.

Ranked 170th, Kartal was the lowest-ranked player to reach a final at this level since the format began in 2009, and the second British woman after Johanna Konta to do so. She rises to 50th, becoming British No 1 for the first time, and said she was happy with her performance only a fortnight after returning from six months out with a back injury.
Racket.copy:
Sonay Kartal missed out on winning the biggest title of her career as her brilliant run at the Wuhan Open ended in a final defeat by Maja Chwalinska. Kartal has enjoyed her best tournament only a fortnight after returning from six months out with a back injury, but her efforts appeared to catch up with her as she faded in a 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 loss.

Instead it was Chwalinska who lifted her first WTA 1000 trophy – the first of her career at any level on the WTA Tour – after fighting back from a set and a break down. The 25‑year‑old made a stunning breakthrough earlier this season when she reached the French Open final as a qualifier, and she will now move towards the top 10.

Racket.title: Britain's Kartal misses out on biggest title of her career
Racket.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal fades from a strong position in a gripping Wuhan Open final against Grand Slam runner-up Maja Chwalinska.
bullets: Britain's Sonay Kartal lost the Wuhan Open final 2-6 6-4 6-2 to Poland's Maja Chwalinska, having dominated the first set and led by a break in the second. Kartal, 24, was playing only her 10th match since a six-month absence with a back injury and was seeking to become the first Briton to win a WTA 1000 title since Johanna Konta in 2017.

Kartal beat Belinda Bencic, Jasmine Paolini, Elina Svitolina and Jelena Ostapenko on the way to the final, and she will return to the top 50 and become British number one for the first time. She earned prize money of about £290,000. Chwalinska, 25, won her first WTA Tour title and will rise to 11th in the rankings from a season start of 146th.
Racket.copy:
Britain's Sonay Kartal missed out on what would have been the biggest title of her career as she faded in a gripping Wuhan Open final against French Open runner-up Maja Chwalinska.

Kartal, 24, was bidding to lift the trophy in only her third event since returning from a six-month absence caused by a back injury. But an extraordinary week in China seemed to catch up with Kartal as she ran out of steam - physically and mentally - in a 2-6 6-4 6-2 defeat.

Racket.title: Maja Chwalinska and Sonay Kartal ranking points and prize money after Wuhan Open final
Racket.summary: Chwalinska secured her maiden title at the WTA 1000 event! The post Maja Chwalinska and Sonay Kartal ranking points and prize money after Wuhan Open final appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Maja Chwalinska won the 2026 Wuhan Open, beating Britain's Sonay Kartal 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 on Sunday in a first WTA 1000 final for both players. World No 22 Chwalinska, 25, claimed her first WTA Tour title and became the fourth player to win a maiden career title at WTA 1000 level, after Naomi Osaka, Bianca Andreescu and Victoria Mboko. She converted her third championship point serving at 5-2 in the decider.

Chwalinska earned 1,000 ranking points, taking her total to 2,681 and a projected career-high of world No 11, plus $665,000 (£503,338) in prize money. Kartal, 24 and ranked 170th, had led 6-2, 2-0 but earned 650 points and $385,001 (£291,407), rising 120 places to No 50. On the way to the final, Chwalinska beat Iga Swiatek and Maria Sakkari, while Kartal beat Elina Svitolina and Jasmine Paolini.
Racket.copy:
Maja Chwalinska overcame Sonay Kartal in the final at the 2026 Wuhan Open, but how many ranking points and how much prize money did the duo collect? In a final matchup no one would have predicted, world No 22 Chwalinska prevailed 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 against 170th-ranked Kartal on Sunday.

Both players were competing in their maiden WTA 1000 final, and Chwalinska’s victory saw her claim her first-ever WTA Tour title. Chwalinska is just the fourth player to win their maiden career title at WTA 1000 level after Naomi Osaka, Bianca Andreescu and Victoria Mboko.

Racket.title: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina says how Arthur Fils helped him win the Shanghai Masters
Racket.summary: What a win for Foki! The post Alejandro Davidovich Fokina says how Arthur Fils helped him win the Shanghai Masters appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina beat Rafael Jodar in the Shanghai Masters final to win his first Masters title. It was his third ATP Tour title in a row this year, following victories at the Mallorca Open and the Chengdu Open. He had previously lost five straight ATP Tour finals and was considered the best player in men's tennis without a trophy.

Davidovich Fokina told Sky Sports Tennis that his friend Arthur Fils, who returned stronger after missing many tournaments, gave him motivation after a back injury kept him out for two months. He also thanked his team for their support. He now sits at a career-high world No 13 and will play the Swiss Indoors and the Paris Masters, with an outside chance of qualifying for the ATP Finals.
Racket.copy:
Alejandro Davidovich Fokina’s incredible run in ATP finals continued as he beat Rafael Jodar in the Shanghai Masters final to win his first Masters tournament. The Spaniard has now won three ATP Tour finals in a row, following victories this year at the Mallorca Open, the Chengdu Open, and now the Shanghai Masters.

Prior to his incredible 2026 record, Davidovich Fokina has lost five straight ATP Tour titles without claiming one, and he was considered the best player in men’s tennis not to have a trophy.

Racket.title: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina ranking points and prize money after Shanghai Masters victory against Rafael Jodar
Racket.summary: A HUGE win! The post Alejandro Davidovich Fokina ranking points and prize money after Shanghai Masters victory against Rafael Jodar appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina won the first Masters title of his career at the Shanghai Masters, beating Rafael Jodar after losing the opening set 6-1. He took the second set in a tie-break and won a tense decider. The Spaniard collected 1000 ranking points and $1,151,380 in prize money, rising to a career-high world number 13.

He beat Jenson Brooksby, Frances Tiafoe, Hubert Hurkacz, Arthur Gea, Alexander Zverev and Jodar on the way to the title. Davidovich Fokina had no ATP titles before 2026 but now has three, after the Mallorca Open and Chengdu Open. He plays the Swiss Indoors from 26 October, then the Paris Masters, and still has an outside chance of qualifying for the ATP Finals in Turin from 15 to 22 November.
Racket.copy:
Alejandro Davidovich Fokina stunned Rafael Jodar to win the first Masters title of his career at the Shanghai Masters. Davidovich Fokina was blwon away 6-1 in the opening set and many expected the 20-year-old to romp to victory to claim his maiden Masters title.

However, Davidovich Fokina fought back into the match, taking a second set tie-break to pile on the pressure against Jodar. A tense deciding set ensued and Davidovich Fokina was able to use his experience to topple Jodar to win the title.

Racket.title: What Iga Swiatek told Maja Chwalinska at the net after losing the Wuhan Open semifinal
Racket.summary: They shared a moment at the net. The post What Iga Swiatek told Maja Chwalinska at the net after losing the Wuhan Open semifinal appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Iga Swiatek lost 7-5, 6-1 to fellow Pole Maja Chwalinska in the Wuhan Open semi-final after a left thigh problem hampered her. Swiatek had missed match points in the first set. Chwalinska reached her first WTA 1000 final, and said Swiatek congratulated her at the net, joking that she would "kill" her if she failed to qualify for the WTA Finals.

Swiatek is ninth in the race for the WTA Finals with one place left, and is competing with Karolina Muchova and Marta Kostyuk. Muchova has withdrawn from the Ningbo Open, leaving Swiatek and Kostyuk, who both have first-round byes. Swiatek is likely to face Marie Bouzkova, who has lost all four of their meetings, while Kostyuk could meet Ekaterina Alexandrova.
Racket.copy:
Iga Swiatek endured an unfortunate injury against Maja Chwalinska in the semifinals of the Wuhan Open. The Pole was in control in the first set, before a left thigh problem significantly hampered her against her long-time friend and compatriot.

Swiatek missed match points in the first set before losing in straight sets 7-5 6-1 against Chwalinska, whose dream season continued with a first Masters final appearance. For Swiatek, however, the Pole is now in a dangerous position when it comes to qualifying for the WTA Finals at the end of the season.

Racket.title: Novak Djokovic receives major ATP Finals qualification boost without even playing
Racket.summary: Another boost for Djokovic! The post Novak Djokovic receives major ATP Finals qualification boost without even playing appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Novak Djokovic has entered the Swiss Indoors in Basel for the first time in 15 years, hoping to qualify for the ATP Finals. He sits 11th in the race and has not won the Basel event since 2009. Felix Auger-Aliassime has withdrawn from Brussels and Basel after injuring his knee in Shanghai, which rules the Canadian out of qualifying for Turin.

With Jannik Sinner confirmed not to play the ATP Finals, the top nine in the race will qualify, leaving Djokovic two places away. Only Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton have confirmed places, so five spots remain open. Djokovic will likely need deep runs in Basel and at the Paris Masters, and he has not played the ATP Finals since winning a record seventh title in 2023.
Racket.copy:
Novak Djokovic is doing all he can to qualify for the ATP Finals. The Serbian star has signed up to play the Swiss Indoors for the first time in 15 years in an attempt to become one of the eight players to qualify for the ATP Finals.

Djokovic currently sits at 11 in the race for the ATP Finals so he will need a good performance in Basel, a tournament he has not lifted since the 2009 season. Ahead of his appearance at the ATP 500 tournament, Djokovic has received a little boost in his attempt to qualify for the Turin tournament at the end of the year.

Racket.title: Alex Eala given another tough draw as she looks to bounce back from worrying Asian swing form
Racket.summary: Her poor form could continue... The post Alex Eala given another tough draw as she looks to bounce back from worrying Asian swing form appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alexandra Eala has been drawn against Diane Parry in the first round of the Ningbo Open, a WTA 500 event running from 19 to 25 October. The pair have never met on the WTA Tour. Parry has been ranked as high as world No 30 and reached the fourth round of Roland Garros for the first time this year.

Eala's Asian swing has been difficult. She lost in the first round in Singapore to qualifier Tatiana Prozorova and took bronze at the Asian Games after a semi-final defeat to China's Wang Xiyu. She then lost in the first round at the Wuhan Open to qualifier Shi Han. If she beats Parry, she is likely to face Diana Shnaider in the second round and could meet Iva Jovic in the quarter-finals, having lost all three previous meetings with her. Ningbo is likely to be her penultimate event of the season, before the Hong Kong Open in November.
Racket.copy:
It’s fair to say Alexandra Eala has endured a difficult time on the WTA Tour’s Asian swing so far. The star was knocked out of the first round of the Singapore Open by qualifier Tatiana Prozorova before heading off to represent the Philippines at the 2026 Asian Games.

The Filipina star was the overwhelming favourite to win gold for the Philippines, but she ended up with just a bronze after losing to China’s Wang Xiyu in the semifinals. Back on WTA Tour action, Eala suffered another first round exit at the hands of another qualifier, Shi Han, at the final Masters tournament of the year at the Wuhan Open.

Racket.title: Alexander Zverev on track to create unwanted ATP history after Shanghai Masters exit
Racket.summary: He doesn't have long to change it either... The post Alexander Zverev on track to create unwanted ATP history after Shanghai Masters exit appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alexander Zverev was beaten in the Shanghai Masters semi-finals by Alejandro Davidovich Fokina, who came from a set down to win 6-4, 6-3 and set up an all-Spanish final against Rafael Jodar. Zverev has won Roland Garros and the US Open this year, his first Grand Slam titles, and has been confirmed as year-end world No 1. Those are his only titles of the season.

Zverev is on course to be the year-end world No 1 with the fewest titles in history. The current low is four, shared by Pete Sampras, Roger Federer, Novak Djokovic and Rafael Nadal. He would need to win at least two of the Vienna Open, the Paris Masters and the ATP Finals to avoid that. After the defeat he said he was tired, having had one day off after the US Open, and had felt flat since his match against Bublik.
Racket.copy:
Alexander Zverev’s time in the Shanghai Masters came to an end as he was beaten in the semifinals by Alejandro Davidovich Fokina. The German took the first set against the Spaniard, but Davidovich Fokina fought back to win the next two sets 6-4, 6-3 to set up an all-Spanish final with Rafael Jodar in Shanghai.

Zverev has finally come of age at the very top of men’s tennis this year by winning Roland Garros and the US Open; the first Grand Slam titles of his career. However, they are the only titles Zverev has managed to claim, in a very strange turn of events for the player who has already been confirmed to finish at the year-end world No 1.

Racket.title: Denmark Open: ‘I’m Hunting Everyone’
Racket.summary: Denmark Open: ‘I’m Hunting Everyone’ BWF World Tour
bullets: Frances's Alex Lanier, the world champion, became the first French men's singles player to reach the Denmark Open final in the tournament's 90-year history. The 21-year-old beat Victor Lai 21-19 21-10 in Odense on Saturday, after losing in the semi-finals in the previous two years. He will face home player Anders Antonsen, who beat Christo Popov 9-21 21-16 21-13 to reach his third Denmark Open final.

In the women's singles, An Se Young beat Nozomi Okuhara 21-16 21-8 and is one win from her 47th title, which would pass Susi Susanti's tally of 46, excluding Regional Games. She faces Akane Yamaguchi, who beat second seed Wang Zhi Yi 21-10 21-19, and leads their head-to-head 23-15. Lanier said that, as world champion, he has embraced being the player everyone wants to beat.
Racket.copy:
Alex Lanier has made history for France yet again. On Saturday in Odense, the world champ became the first men’s singles player from his country to reach the Denmark Open final in the tournament’s 90-year history.

bullets: Former British No 1 Greg Rusedski said on his podcast that there is no set formula for paying a tennis coach, with the arrangement negotiated between agent, player and coach. Most coaches receive a retainer plus bonuses and a guaranteed annual amount. Weekly fees range from $2,000 to as much as $25,000 including bonuses. Some coaches take a percentage of prize money, typically 5–10% from the second round, or only from the quarter-finals, semi-finals, finals or title wins if the base is higher.

Rusedski cited Brad Gilbert, who he said took only a percentage of prize money, with expenses paid and a higher percentage at the Grand Slams. He noted that prize money has risen sharply, with players on 15–23 records at the Shanghai Masters earning $1.3m. The piece notes Ivan Ljubicic's tie-up with Felix Auger-Aliassime and that Juan Carlos Ferrero will return in 2027 after splitting with Carlos Alcaraz last December.
Racket.copy:

Rusedski, a former world No 4 who reached the US Open final in 1997, worked with French player Giovanni Mpetshi Perricard on a brief trial that came to an end after Wimbledon in June and he has also worked with former world No 1 Victoria Azarenka.

bullets: ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi has unveiled OneVision proposals, intended for the 2028 season subject to consultation and approval, to alter prize money distribution, reduce pressure to overplay and give players more choice over where and when to compete. The Masters 1000 Bonus Pool would rise from $21.5m to $50m, with payments tied to rankings at each mandatory Masters 1000, and players would need to compete in at least four to qualify.

The ATP plans to invest $105m annually in central player compensation from 2028, including $25m for career support for year-end top 250 players and $30m for pension contributions. Total player compensation, excluding Grand Slams, is estimated to reach $350m from 2028. The proposals also seek dedicated calendar weeks for each tournament level, including the tenth Masters 1000 in Saudi Arabia from 2028, and a rankings reform giving more weight to the biggest events.
Racket.copy:

The tennis body has unveiled plans for OneVision, which is mooted to be in place for the 2028 season, subject to further consultation and approval. 2026 has been a year dominated by injuries, most notably to world No 1 Jannik Sinner and the youngest-ever player to complete the career Grand Slam, Carlos Alcaraz. Racket.title: Sonay Kartal: Brit breaks new ground by upsetting Elina Svitolina to reach Wuhan Open semi-finals
Racket.summary: Sonay Kartal: Brit breaks new ground by upsetting Elina Svitolina to reach Wuhan Open semi-finals Sky Sports
bullets: Britain's Sonay Kartal reached the Wuhan Open semi-finals, a WTA 1000 event, by beating fifth seed Elina Svitolina 6-2 2-6 6-4 in just her third tournament back from injury. She faces former French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko on Saturday for a place in Sunday's final. Kartal had beaten Anhelina Kalinina, Belinda Bencic and Jasmine Paolini earlier in the week.

The 24-year-old missed six months with a back stress fracture after reaching the fourth round at Indian Wells in March, returning at the Billie Jean King Cup Finals. Ranked 170th, she will return to the top 100, rising to 87, as the lowest-ranked player to reach the Wuhan semi-finals. Ostapenko beat 11th seed Diana Shnaider 7-6 (8-6) 6-1, and Iga Swiatek plays Ann Li in the other quarter-final.
Racket.copy:
Britain's Sonay Kartal has stormed into the semi-finals of the Wuhan Open - a WTA 1000 event - in just her third tournament back from injury. Kartal continued her incredible form by defeating fifth seed Elina Svitolina 6-2 2-6 6-4.

She will take on former French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko on Saturday for a spot in Sunday's final. Speaking on-court, Kartal said: "Despite winning the first set pretty comfortably, I knew what a great fighter she [Svitolina] is, so I knew that until the very last point was played, I was never safe.

Racket.title: Sonay Kartal +83 in Live WTA Rankings as she surges past Emma Raducanu with third big win in Wuhan
Racket.summary: What a week in Wuhan for Sonay Kartal! The post Sonay Kartal +83 in Live WTA Rankings as she surges past Emma Raducanu with third big win in Wuhan appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Sonay Kartal beat fifth seed Elina Svitolina 6-2, 2-6, 6-4 in the Wuhan Open quarter-finals to reach her first WTA 1000 semi-final. She had already beaten ninth seed Belinda Bencic 6-0, 7-5 and 15th seed Jasmine Paolini 6-2, 6-0, after opening with a 7-5, 6-3 win over Anhelina Kalinina. The 24-year-old used a protected ranking to enter after missing nearly seven months with a back injury.

Kartal started the tournament at No 170 and has moved up 83 places to No 87 in the Live WTA Rankings, making her British No 2 behind Katie Boulter (No 58) and ahead of Emma Raducanu (No 109). She faces Jelena Ostapenko in the semi-finals, and victory could lift her to No 50.
Racket.copy:
Sonay Kartal will return to the top 100 of the WTA Rankings after she continued her brilliant run at the Wuhan Open with an upset win over Elina Svitolina in the quarter-finals.

Following an injury-ravaged 2026 season that saw her miss nearly seven months of action due to a back injury, Kartal has bounced back in style as she has reached her maiden WTA 1000 semi-final with three consecutive wins over seeded players.

Racket.title: Rafael Jodar criticism ‘too harsh’, says former world No 8
Racket.summary: "He does need to get better but I also think people need to just chill out online." The post Rafael Jodar criticism ‘too harsh’, says former world No 8 appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: John Isner has urged social media users to "just chill out" over criticism of Rafael Jodar, calling it "too harsh" because the Spaniard is young. Jodar was given a code violation for unsportsmanlike conduct after swearing while asking a ball kid for a towel in his fourth-round match against Botic van de Zandschulp at the Shanghai Masters, and argued with chair umpire Jimmy Pinoargote.

The incident came a few months after Jodar was accused of pushing a ball girl at the French Open, which he denied, saying she tripped. Speaking on the Nothing Major podcast, the former world No 8 said players should always respect ball kids but cited frustration and the heat in Shanghai as mitigating factors. He said Jodar needs to improve and will get better.
Racket.copy:
Social media users have been told to “just chill out” with their attacks on Rafael Jodar with John Isner urging the tennis community to give him a break as “he’s young”. Not for the first time this season, Jodar has found himself at the centre of a controversial incident involving ball kids as he was overheard swearing during his fourth-round match against Botic van de Zandschulp at the Shanghai Masters.

Unhappy after a passing shot down the line was called long, the Spaniard told the ball kid, “Give me the f***** towel, damn it!” which prompted the chair umpire to give him a code violation for unsportsmanlike conduct.

Racket.title: Denmark Open: Gemke’s Purple Patch Rolls On
Racket.summary: Denmark Open: Gemke’s Purple Patch Rolls On BWF World Tour
bullets: Rasmus Gemke beat Ng Ka Long Angus 21-12 21-18 on Thursday to reach the quarter-finals of the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026 in Odense. Earlier in the week he had beaten top seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn. Backed by a home crowd, the Dane said it was a good feeling and that he had enjoyed the match.

Gemke lost in the opening round of last week's Arctic Open, but said the confidence from reaching the quarter-finals at the World Championships is driving his form. He said he has no injuries and his body feels good. He next plays Victor Lai, who has yet to drop a game this week and beat him in New Delhi. Anders Antonsen and Mathias Christiansen/Alexandra Boje also advanced for the home side.
Racket.copy:
Rasmus Gemke continued his rich form this week on Thursday, defeating Ng Ka Long Angus 21-12 21-18 to reach the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026 quarterfinals. Backed by a vocal home crowd in Odense, the Dane produced another assured display and admitted relishing every moment of his recent resurgence.

“I don’t know what’s going on but it’s a good feeling,” Gemke said. “It was a really great match for me. I enjoyed it a lot and felt very comfortable. It’s amazing to step on court in front of our fans.”

Racket.title: Denmark Open: Koga/Saito Trip World Champs
Racket.summary: Denmark Open: Koga/Saito Trip World Champs BWF World Tour
bullets: Akira Koga/Natsu Saito beat France's Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue 22-20 21-19 at the VICTOR Denmark Open 2026 in Odense. The world number 18 pair saved six game points in the opener and led throughout the second from 16-15. They next face Malaysia's Hoo Pang Ron/Lai Peijing, who beat fifth seeds Dechapol Puavaranukroh/Supissara Paewsampran 21-7 21-11, in their second Super 750 quarter-final.

Gicquel and Delrue, France's first world champions as of August, have now had two early exits after the World Championships. They lost in the first round of the China Masters. Their home YONEX French Open starts in Tremblay-en-France next Tuesday. Anders Antonsen beat Jason Gunawan 21-10 21-12 in 38 minutes to reach his sixth home quarter-final, and meets Alwi Farhan, who beat defending champion Jonatan Christie 21-14 21-9.
Racket.copy:
Thom Gicquel and Delphine Delrue’s post-World Championships dip continued at VICTOR Denmark Open 2026 with a second consecutive early exit. Akira Koga/Natsu Saito proved their conquerors in Odense, winning their first meeting 22-20 21-19. The world No.18s remarkably saved six game points in the opener before finishing strongly again in the second, never relinquishing the lead after moving ahead at 16-15.

The Japanese now advance to the quarterfinals – their second at Super 750 level – against Malaysians Hoo Pang Ron/Lai Peijing, who ousted fifth seeds Dechapol Puavaranukroh/Supissara Paewsampran 21-7 21-11.

Racket.title: World Juniors: Crafty Khangurra, Tenacious Ip into Semis
Racket.summary: World Juniors: Crafty Khangurra, Tenacious Ip into Semis BWF
bullets: Jagsher Singh Khangurra of India and Hong Kong China's Ip Sum Yau reached the semi-finals at the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026 on Thursday, securing medals. Khangurra beat Jhuang Yuan-Syue 6-15 17-15 15-12 in 48 minutes and next faces Indonesia's Radithya Bayu Wardhana. Ip came from 3-8 down in the third game to beat Su Xiao-Ting 8-15 15-6 15-11 and will play China's Zhang Yi Xin.

In the other men's singles quarter-finals, top seed Mady Sow of France beat Park Jung Bin 15-12 13-15 15-2 and meets 18th seed Fardhan Rainanda Joe. Ip said Hong Kong China's women's singles had not won a medal for many years. China's men's singles challenge ended in the last 16, but China still have a chance in four titles. Two Indonesian pairs reached the mixed doubles semi-finals, and Malaysia's Genevie Lim/Low Zi Yu are in the last four in women's doubles.
Racket.copy:
More than the archetypal badminton player, Jagsher Singh Khangurra has the bearing of a mild-mannered chess talent: studious, understated. In the men’s singles quarterfinals of the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026 on Thursday, facing an explosive opponent in Jhuang Yuan-Syue, Khangurra produced a performance as finely crafted and cerebral as befits an accomplished chess player. In 48 minutes he had secured a medal, beating Jhuang 6-15 17-15 15-12.

He had to win it the hard way. Having struggled in the opening game, Khangurra found his rhythm, correctly anticipating his opponent’s explosive smashes and showing great finesse at the net. The sense of calm control even while under attack prevailed, and once he had edged through the second game, he coasted in the third.

Racket.title: Stefan Milicevic given 24-year ban for match-fixing: Serbian player, 29, banned from tennis until 2050
Racket.summary: Stefan Milicevic given 24-year ban for match-fixing: Serbian player, 29, banned from tennis until 2050 Sky Sports
bullets: Serbian player Stefan Milicevic has been banned for 24 years for match-fixing after the International Tennis Integrity Agency found he led a "corrupt network" between 2022 and 2024. The 29-year-old, whose highest ranking was 1338, fixed six matches, five of which he played in, and attempted to fix six more. He was also fined $70,000 (£52,800).

The ITIA said Milicevic did not engage or co-operate with the investigation. His suspension ends on 8 October 2050, when he will be 53. While suspended he cannot play in, coach at or attend events organised or sanctioned by World Tennis, the WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams or any national association.
Racket.copy:
A Serbian tennis player has been handed a massive 24-year ban for match-fixing. Stefan Milicevic led a "corrupt network" of match-fixing between 2022 and 2024, according to the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA), with the 29-year-old shown to have fixed six matches - five of which he played in - and attempted to with six more.

Milicevic, whose highest ATP ranking was 1338, did not engage or co-operate with the investigation, according to the ITIA, and was also fined 70,000 US dollars (£52,800). The ITIA's statement on Thursday said: "Milicevic was also charged with recruiting or attempting to recruit multiple professional players as part of a corrupt network during the same period, resulting in a number of other players fixing matches."

Racket.title: Greg Rusedski praises Emma Raducanu for 'smart play' as he predicts where she could be ranked next year
Racket.summary: Greg Rusedski praises Emma Raducanu for 'smart play' as he predicts where she could be ranked next year Tennishead
bullets: Greg Rusedski has described Emma Raducanu's decision not to play again this year as a 'smart play'. Raducanu, now world number 107, last competed at the Queen's Club Championships in June, where she lost the final to Donna Vekic. She then suffered a stress fracture in her lower right leg, which forced her to miss Wimbledon and the US Open and took her outside the top 100.

Rusedski said on his podcast that an extended off-season would let her get physically stronger and technically better for 2027. Sitting out for at least six months would give her a protected ranking, allowing entry to the 2027 Australian Open. He said she could reach the top 30 or top 20 if she stays healthy, and could challenge the top 10. She has played just 10 tournaments this year, including her first two WTA Tour finals, at the Transylvania Open and Queen's.
Racket.copy:
Emma Raducanu has faced a very disrupted season once again, as a result of both injury and illness. Raducanu last competed at the Queen’s Club Championships back in June, where she reached the final before losing to Donna Vekic.

Despite her efforts to reach the biggest final of her career since winning the US Open in 2021, Raducanu suffered a stress fracture in her lower right leg. This injury has forced Raducanu to miss both Wimbledon and the US Open this year, and means she has now dropped outside the top 100.

Racket.title: ‘It’s mind-blowing’ – Carlos Alcaraz’s late Vienna wildcard sparks appearance fee debate
Racket.summary: Alcaraz reportedly wanted €750,000 in 2023 - how much will he get in 2026? The post ‘It’s mind-blowing’ – Carlos Alcaraz’s late Vienna wildcard sparks appearance fee debate appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Carlos Alcaraz has accepted a late wildcard for the Vienna Open, which runs from 26 October to 1 November, a day after the Six Kings Slam was postponed. The Riyadh exhibition, scheduled for 21-24 October, was moved to 27-30 December after Riyadh airport was bombed again. Players in it can earn £1.2m for competing, with the winner receiving an extra £3.5m.

It will be Alcaraz's first appearance in Vienna since 2021. Der Standard reported that he asked for a €750,000 (£633,858) appearance fee in 2023, which tournament director Herwig Straka declined, and he later withdrew from Basel injured. His fee this time is unknown, and fans on social media have debated what he will be paid.
Racket.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz has accepted a late wildcard for the Vienna Open later this month, a day after the Six Kings Slam was postponed. Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz, Alex de Minaur and Learner Tien were scheduled to take part in the Saudi Arabian exhibition between 21 and 24 October.

But after Riyadh airport was bombed again this week, the money-spinning event – where players can pocket £1.2million for competing, and the winner gets an extra £3.5m – has been postponed to 27-30 December.

Racket.title: Serb player banned until 2050 for tennis match-fixing
Racket.summary: Stefan Milicevic is given a 24-year suspension from tennis - one of the most severe punishments outside of a lifetime ban - for match-fixing.
bullets: Serbian player Stefan Milicevic has been given a 24-year suspension from tennis for match-fixing, one of the most severe punishments outside a lifetime ban. The 29-year-old, whose career-high ranking was 1,338th in 2014, was charged with fixing six matches, five of which he played in, and attempting to fix six more between 2022 and 2024. He also received a £53,000 fine.

The International Tennis Integrity Authority said he was also charged with recruiting, or attempting to recruit, multiple professional players as part of a corrupt network. The severity of the sanction is partly due to his lack of co-operation, as he did not engage despite seven attempts to contact him. His ban runs until October 2050, and in December French player Quentin Folliot was banned for 20 years in a separate case.
Racket.copy:
A player from Serbia has been given a 24-year suspension from tennis - one of the most severe punishments imposed by anti-corruption investigators outside of a lifetime ban - for match-fixing.

Stefan Milicevic, who reached a career-high world ranking of 1,338th in 2014, was charged with fixing six matches, including five in which he was competing. The 29-year-old, who played on the lower rungs of the professional ladder, was also charged with attempting to fix a further six matches between 2022 and 2024.

Racket.title: Novak Djokovic’s final dream may fall through unless he makes a big change
Racket.summary: Djokovic wants to play at the ATP Finals - but that target may be out of reach. The post Novak Djokovic’s final dream may fall through unless he makes a big change appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Novak Djokovic has said he would like to play the ATP Finals in Turin next month, after winning his 102nd career title at the ATP 500 event in Beijing. He has skipped the event in recent years despite qualifying. After an early exit in Shanghai, the 39-year-old said he plans to play only in Paris, and Alex de Minaur's run to the quarter-finals there took the final qualifying place from him.

With Jannik Sinner out for the season with a knee injury, ninth place in the ATP Race would be enough to qualify. Daniil Medvedev is currently eighth and will play in Almaty next week, while Frances Tiafoe is also ahead of Djokovic and plays in Lyon. De Minaur will play in Vienna, so Djokovic may need a semi-final or title run at the Paris Masters unless he adds tournaments.
Racket.copy:
Novak Djokovic has stated his intention to push for qualification to this season’s ATP Finals in Turin, but that ambition may fall short unless he makes a big change to his plans in what is left of the season.

Djokovic has skipped the ATP Finals in recent years, even though he has qualified for the eight-man end-of-season event that is the marquee tournament for the ATP Tour. So it was somewhat of a surprise when the 39-year-old declared he was keen to play in Turin next month after he won a remarkable 102nd career title in the ATP 500 event in Beijing earlier this month.

Racket.title: Alexander Zverev curbing ‘extreme’ behaviour and issues ankle injury update after Shanghai win
Racket.summary: "I feel like it is a bit unnecessary from my end." The post Alexander Zverev curbing ‘extreme’ behaviour and issues ankle injury update after Shanghai win appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alexander Zverev beat Alex de Minaur 6-4, 6-4 in 78 minutes on Thursday to reach the semi-finals of the Shanghai Masters 1000 event. He said he is trying to cut down on bouncing the ball between serves, which was heavily criticised during his US Open win, where he reportedly bounced it 12,000 times, adding nearly 2.5 hours to his time on court.

Zverev said the habit had gone to an "extreme" in New York and that he now considers it unnecessary. He is also managing an ankle problem sustained in his third-round win over Quentin Halys, which he said worsens the longer a match goes. He said playing quickly and avoiding long rallies eased the strain as he pursues a first Shanghai title.
Racket.copy:
Alexander Zverev says he is actively trying to curb his “unnecessary” behaviour between points following his Shanghai Open win over Alex De Minaur. The US Open champion marched into the semi-finals of the Masters 1000 event on Thursday after beating the Australian 6-4, 6-4 in just 78 minutes.

Following his victory, the soon-to-be world No 1 admitted he is making a conscious effort to reduce the amount of ball bouncing he does between serves, something that was heavily criticised during his Flushing Meadows triumph.

Racket.title: Wuhan Open: Sonay Kartal stuns Jasmine Paolini to set up quarter-final against Elina Svitolina while Alexander Zverev continues winning form
Racket.summary: Wuhan Open: Sonay Kartal stuns Jasmine Paolini to set up quarter-final against Elina Svitolina while Alexander Zverev continues winning form Sky Sports
bullets: Britain's Sonay Kartal beat 15th seed Jasmine Paolini 6-2 6-0 to reach the Wuhan Open quarter-finals, winning the final 11 games of the match. The 24-year-old, back after six months out with a back injury, equals her best WTA 1000 result, having also reached the last eight in Beijing last year. She next faces fifth seed Elina Svitolina, who beat Chinese wild card Guo Hanyu 6-1 6-4.

Maja Chwalinska, the surprise French Open runner-up, also advanced with a 6-4 6-1 win over American Iva Jovic, and Diana Shnaider beat sixth seed Karolina Muchova 7-5 6-3. At the Shanghai Masters, top-ranked Alexander Zverev beat Alex de Minaur 6-4 6-4, saving all five break points he faced, to set up a semi-final against Alejandro Davidovich Fokina. Zverev, who has been carrying an ankle injury, secured the year-end world No 1 ranking earlier this week.
Racket.copy:
Britain's Sonay Kartal thumped two-time Grand Slam finalist Jasmine Paolini to reach the quarter-finals of the Wuhan Open. Kartal has made a brilliant return from six months out with a back injury and dropped only two games in a 6-2 6-0 victory against 15th seed Paolini.

It was an error-strewn performance from former French Open and Wimbledon runner-up Paolini and Kartal took full advantage, winning the final 11 games. The result equals the 24-year-old's best performance at a WTA 1000 tournament - the top level of the women's tour - with Kartal also having reached the last eight in Beijing last year.

Racket.title: Kartal wins again as impressive comeback continues
Racket.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal beats former Wimbledon finalist Jasmine Paolini in straight sets to reach the Wuhan Open quarter-finals.
bullets: Britain's Sonay Kartal beat 15th seed Jasmine Paolini 6-2 6-0 to reach the Wuhan Open quarter-finals, where she will face Ukraine's Elina Svitolina. The 24-year-old, playing on a protected ranking, has not dropped a set in the tournament, having also beaten Anhelina Kalinina and ninth seed Belinda Bencic.

Kartal missed more than six months with a stress fracture in her back after retiring against Elena Rybakina in the fourth round at Indian Wells, and has won five of her seven matches since returning. She missed Wimbledon, where she reached the fourth round in 2025, and returned about three weeks ago at the BJK Cup before reaching the Beijing third round. Kartal said her display against Paolini was pretty flawless.
Racket.copy:
Britain's Sonay Kartal continued her impressive comeback from long-term injury with a comfortable win over former Wimbledon finalist Jasmine Paolini to reach the Wuhan Open quarter-finals.

Kartal, 24, missed more than six months with a stress fracture in her back, but has won five of her seven matches since returning to action. The former world number 44 ruthlessly brushed aside Italian 15th seed Paolini in a 6-2 6-0 victory, further validating Kartal's patient approach to recovering from the first serious injury of her career.

Racket.title: Former world No 1 calls for tennis star to be ‘suspended for months’ after ‘dangerous’ incident
Racket.summary: "This could be the worst thing I have ever seen on a tennis court." The post Former world No 1 calls for tennis star to be ‘suspended for months’ after ‘dangerous’ incident appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Former doubles world number one Rennae Stubbs says Terence Atmane should have been defaulted after he hurled his racket towards the crowd in his Shanghai Masters qualifying first round against Bernard Tomic. A railing stopped anyone being hit, and the 24-year-old Frenchman received a point penalty for unsportsmanlike conduct before later apologising.

On her podcast, Stubbs called it possibly the worst thing she had seen on a tennis court and said Atmane should be suspended for months. He had received only a warning for kicking his racket into the crowd at the Hamburg Open earlier this year. Co-host Caitlin Thompson also criticised Daniil Medvedev, defaulted at the China Open, and Arthur Fils. Stubbs favours a blanket ban for sending objects into the crowd, but no rule change has been made.
Racket.copy:
Rennae Stubbs says Terence Atmane’s “dangerous” actions at the Shanghai Open might have been the worst thing she’s ever seen on a tennis court. In Atmane‘s first-round qualifier for the Masters 1000 event, the Frenchman hurled his racket at the crowd, but fortunately for them, a railing stopped anyone from getting hit.

The 24-year-old was given a point penalty for unsportsmanlike conduct by the chair umpire, but former world No 1 women’s doubles player Stubbs was incredulous that he wasn’t defaulted.

Racket.title: Carlos Alcaraz makes last-minute schedule change after Shanghai shock and Six Kings Slam move
Racket.summary: Will we get a Carlos Alcaraz against Alexander Zverev match-up? The post Carlos Alcaraz makes last-minute schedule change after Shanghai shock and Six Kings Slam move appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Carlos Alcaraz has added the ATP 500 Vienna Open, running from 26 October to 1 November, to his schedule after his early exit from the Shanghai Masters, where Zizou Bergs beat him in the second round. He had previously said he would play only the Paris Masters, ATP Finals and Davis Cup Finals. Organisers said he will begin his tournament on Tuesday 27 October.

The change follows the postponement of the Six Kings Slam in Saudi Arabia, which he was due to play from 21-24 October, after attacks on Riyadh airport. Without it, he faced three weeks between Shanghai and the Paris Masters on 2 November. Alexander Zverev is top seed in Vienna, with Jannik Sinner withdrawn through a knee injury. Alcaraz reached the semi-finals on his 2021 debut.
Racket.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz has made a late change to his 2026 calendar as he has added an ATP 500 tournament to his schedule with the move coming on the back of his early exit from the Shanghai Masters.

The world No 3 has signed up for the Vienna Open, which runs from 26 October until 1 November, after previously stating he only planned to play three more ATP events, namely the Paris Masters, ATP Finals and Davis Cup Finals.

Racket.title: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina reveals he knew ‘something was wrong’ before Arthur Gea’s Shanghai retirement
Racket.summary: "I feel sorry for him." The post Alejandro Davidovich Fokina reveals he knew ‘something was wrong’ before Arthur Gea’s Shanghai retirement appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina reached the Shanghai Masters semi-finals on Thursday when Arthur Gea retired trailing 4-1 and 40-0 in the first set, after just 22 minutes. Gea, 21, had taken a medical timeout at 4-1 for an apparent right quad and hip problem. The 25th seed, now 18th in the rankings, will face either top seed Alexander Zverev or ninth seed Alex De Minaur.

Davidovich Fokina said he felt sorry for Gea, who has risen to a career-high ranking of 44. He said he knew something was wrong when he saw Gea ask for the physio and then hit an aggressive forehand into the net. He had come through three-setters against Frances Tiafoe and Hubert Hurkacz in the previous rounds, and planned to take a day off. He won the Chengdu Open in September, after the Mallorca Open in June.
Racket.copy:
Alejandro Davidovich Fokina said he knew “something was wrong” with Arthur Gea shortly before his retirement at the Shanghai Masters. The 25th seed swept into the semi-finals of the Chinese tournament on Thursday after Gea retired at 4-1 and 40-0 down in the first set, with just 22 minutes played.

The Frenchman took a medical timeout at 4-1 for what appeared to be an issue with his right quad and around his hip. And the 21-year-old lasted just a few more points before calling it quits.

Racket.title: ‘Wash it for me’ – Iga Swiatek under fire as ex-world No 5 reveals surprise Madrid Open requests
Racket.summary: "I actually went and dealt with it." The post ‘Wash it for me’ – Iga Swiatek under fire as ex-world No 5 reveals surprise Madrid Open requests appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Former world number five Daniela Hantuchova, part of the Madrid Open's management team since 2024 and responsible for player and media relations, has alleged Iga Swiatek showed a lack of consideration at the tournament. She said Swiatek personally brought her clothes after winning the 2024 event and asked what to do with them, and that she dealt with the request.

Hantuchova said that during the 2025 nationwide power outage, with organisers handing out bread rolls for dinner, Swiatek's sports psychologist Daria Abramowicz requested warm chicken at 11am before a match. Swiatek has faced criticism before, including after smashing a ball into the ground in frustration during a loss to Mirra Andreeva at Indian Wells last year, when she apologised but said her emotional expression was judged unfairly.
Racket.copy:
Former world No 5 Daniel Hantuchova has seemingly called out Iga Swiatek’s spoilt behaviour after two separate alleged incidents at the Madrid Open. The former Australian Open semi-finalist has been part of the Madrid Open’s management team since 2024, where she deals with player and media relations.

When Swiatek won the WTA 1000 event in 2024, the Slovakian alleged that the Pole showed a lack of consideration for people at the tournament. Hantuchova claims the six-time major winner personally approached her with clothes and asked if they could be washed, with the former player taken aback by the request.

Racket.title: Czech Open 2026: European Circuit action heads to Prague
Racket.summary: Czech Open 2026: European Circuit action heads to Prague Badminton Europe
bullets: The YONEX BYD Czech Open 2026 takes place from 15th to 18th October in Prague, Czechia, as the Badminton Europe Elite Circuit continues. The tournament features all five disciplines, with qualification and the main draw starting on Thursday and Friday, followed by the quarter-finals and semi-finals on Saturday and the finals on Sunday, 18th October.

Home players Jiří Král/Ondřej Král lead the Czech challenge in men's doubles, while Tereza Švábíková and Petra Maixnerová are among the names to watch in women's singles and doubles. Recent European Circuit winners Natan Begga/Elsa Jacob and William Kryger Boe/Rasmus Espersen will look to continue their strong form in Prague. The action is shown live on badmintoneurope.tv.

bullets: The University of Maryland has indefinitely suspended its club tennis team after a graphic featuring Ku Klux Klan imagery, in an altered Maryland state flag, was circulated to other universities in a shared Google document before a regional tournament. Toni Rachal, president of Howard University's club tennis team, spotted it, and Howard's club questioned how it reached official tournament materials.

The suspension is pending an administrative investigation by the office of student conduct, and the university police and civil rights office have also opened investigations. Maryland withdrew from the tournament and forfeited its matches, while Howard reached the semi-finals, its best result in the event since the club was established in 2021. University president Darryll J Pines said only a few members may have been directly involved, while Black student union leaders said the incident was not isolated.

Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Alex de Minaur, Taylor Fritz and Learner Tien were due to play. Yemen's Houthi movement launched attacks at the weekend, including a missile strike on Riyadh's airport on Saturday that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300.

Organisers cited organisational and logistical challenges and their potential impact on the audience experience. Three Saudi Pro League fixtures were also postponed, including Al-Nassr's trip to Al-Ahli, which moved to March. The Asian Tour said it is monitoring the situation ahead of the PIF Saudi International at Riyadh Golf Club from 18-21 November, and Formula 1 races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi could also be affected.

For Cruz, the sixth seed at the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026, her emotional side takes a toll, particularly in team events, for she takes on the concerns of her teammates. At the Suhandinata Cup last week, for instance: “I was so insecure because during the team event I just felt so much pressure that I took on myself, it was like I forgot how to play badminton, it was like my feeling was locked, my wrist would be cold, so coming into this (the individual championships), I was so insecure and scared that I wouldn’t perform. Iga Swiatek confirmed her place in the round of 16 at the Wuhan Open by beating compatriot Magdalena Frech. Swiatek produced a spellbinding display to win 6-2, 6-1 and she will now await the winner of Ashlyn Krueger or Lanlana Tararudee in the round of 16.

The Pole is looking to claim her second Masters title of the year in Wuhan as she continues her quest to try and qualify for the WTA Finals at the end of the year. Swiatek is currently tenth in the live race, but there is just one spot left for the Pole to qualify, so she is locked in a battle with Karolina Muchova, Marta Kostyuk, and Iva Jovic.

Racket.title: Finding Renée Richards: the complicated past and present of a trans sports pioneer
Racket.summary: In 1977, Richards sued to play in the US Open after transitioning. Now she supports bans on trans athletes in women’s sports. A new biography explores a complex legacy It was a story that dominated tennis headlines back in 1977: Dr Renée Richards, an ophthalmologist who excelled as a male amateur player before a sex-change operation, was suing for the right to play in the women’s draw of the US Open. Where did Richards go for legal assistance? None other than Roy Cohn. Better known for prosecuting suspected communists during the red scare and mentoring Donald Trump, Cohn turned his attention to fighting for Richards’s inclusion. His firm successfully argued the case – part of the narrative of a new biography, Finding Renée Richards: The Groundbreaking Story of Tennis’s Trans Pioneer by Julie Kliegman. Continue reading...
bullets: A new biography, Finding Renée Richards: The Groundbreaking Story of Tennis's Trans Pioneer by Julie Kliegman, revisits the 1977 lawsuit in which Richards, an ophthalmologist who had played as a male amateur before a sex-change operation, sued for the right to play in the women's US Open draw. Roy Cohn's firm successfully argued the case, though the decision was limited to Richards and set no precedent for other trans people.

Kliegman, a trans and non-binary sports journalist, drew on Richards' autobiographies, interview transcripts from an unpublished memoir and several in-person interviews with Richards, now 92. Kliegman said Richards now believes trans women and girls should not play women's sports unless they have not undergone male puberty, a reversal of her 1977 position that created tension between them. At Richards' wish, the book uses her former name and he/him pronouns for her early life.
Racket.copy:

Better known for prosecuting suspected communists during the red scare and mentoring Donald Trump, Cohn turned his attention to fighting for Richards’s inclusion. His firm successfully argued the case – part of the narrative of a new biography, Finding Renée Richards: The Groundbreaking Story of Tennis’s Trans Pioneer by Julie Kliegman.

Bencic is the highest-ranked player Kartal has beaten since world number five Mirra Andreeva in Beijing last year.

Kartal, 24, returned last month at the Billie Jean King Cup Finals in Shenzhen after six months out with a back stress fracture. Ranked 170th, she is guaranteed to rise around 40 places and plays Jasmine Paolini next. Elsewhere, seventh seed Iga Swiatek beat Magdalena Frech 6-2 6-1, while Jelena Ostapenko came from a set down to beat second seed Jessica Pegula, who squandered three match points.

Kartal missed six months of the season with a stress fracture in her back, returning last month at the Billie Jean King Cup Finals in Shenzhen before reaching the third round in Beijing last week.

bullets: Gael Monfils is now officially retired, with his status changed on the International Tennis Integrity Agency website and confirmed by its head of communication to L'Equipe. He is no longer authorised to take part in tournaments. He had said he would retire at the end of 2026 and was expected to finish at the Paris Masters, from 2 to 8 November, which would have been his 12th appearance there.

The ITIA said he would need six months of out-of-competition testing to return, as Serena Williams did. Monfils won 13 ATP Tour titles, including three at ATP 500 level, and reached three Masters finals: Paris in 2009 and 2010, losing to Novak Djokovic and Robin Soderling, and Monte Carlo in 2016, losing to Rafael Nadal. He also reached the semi-finals of Roland Garros and the US Open.
Racket.copy:

Fans began to speculate when the star’s status was changed to ‘retired’ on the International Tennis Integrity Agency’s official website, but many were surprised by the timing.

Monfils was expected to bring his career to a close on home soil, at the Paris Masters, the final Masters tournament on the ATP Tour. The French tournament is due to take place between the 2nd and 8th November, and it would have marked Monfils’ 12th appearance at his home event.

This past year, I had perhaps my best competitive season since high school, and a big reason was the new trust I had in my equipment. This season, I shot 71 twice, made an albatross, got my handicap index back below 1.0, and qualified for my first state amateur or mid-amateur in five years. The journey started, though, when we embarked on Fully Fit, a fitting bonanza that gave me the chance to get fit by six OEMs and decide what clubs would make it into my bag for the upcoming year. While I had been GOLF’s gear editor for about a year, I still had yet to take that kind of holistic look at my entire golf bag with each OEM. In fact, at that point, I had had a full bag fitting with just two of them.

It’s not so much that I had any gaping holes in my bag, but there was so much I hadn’t tried. While many of my fittings ended up in product that I would have expected, other spots I tried something new.

Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy backs a possible PGA Tour return for select LIV Golf players Yahoo Sports
bullets: Rory McIlroy said at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi on 13 October that he would vote to welcome former LIV Golf players back to the PGA Tour and DP World Tour. He argued their return could improve the tours' business prospects and strengthen their fields, while criticising how LIV used its financial resources. He acknowledged that not all players would share his view.

LIV's future is uncertain after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund said it would end its funding after the 2026 season and the league entered Chapter 11 proceedings. BC Partners received court approval for up to $300 million in financing, and a decision on LIV 2.0 is expected by the end of October. DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings has said players in LIV 2.0 in 2027 cannot compete on the European circuit. The PGA Tour's Returning Member Program, introduced in January 2026, carries a $5 million charitable contribution, and CEO Brian Rolapp said in August there were no plans to revive it.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy has signaled a willingness to welcome former LIV Golf players back to the PGA Tour, adding a significant twist to professional golf's ongoing divide. The Northern Irish star, once among the breakaway league's most outspoken critics, now believes bringing certain players back could strengthen the tour commercially and competitively.

His latest comments arrive as LIV Golf confronts serious financial uncertainty and several prominent players reassess their futures. However, McIlroy's support doesn't amount to an unrestricted invitation for every former rival. Questions about eligibility, financial consequences, and the views of current PGA Tour members remain central to any potential reintegration.

Golf.title: How shared stewardship helps drive the game forward
Golf.summary: There's more golf around us than ever. Here's why we need to embrace these additional forms while also creating pathways into more traditional golf. The post How shared stewardship helps drive the game forward appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
This piece was first published on the USGA’s website. In 2009, World Golf Hall of Famer Tom Watson, then 59, was on the verge of becoming the oldest major champion in history. After a nearly perfect iron shot into the 18th green landed firmly and rolled over the putting surface, Tom made bogey and lost in a playoff. Even so, it was an incredible runner-up finish.

Over the years, Tom and my dad, the longtime head golf professional at Delray Dunes Golf & Country Club, forged a strong friendship. Dad wanted to congratulate him on his inspiring performance. Knowing Tom had likely received hundreds of messages, I thought it unlikely we would ever hear back from him following his legendary near-miss.

Golf.copy:
TGL, the simulator golf league co-founded by Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy, returns this winter for its third season after a successful inaugural campaign that proved the concept and a second season that added new holes, tweaked gameplay and built momentum.

TGL’s third season will see a new team enter the mix, too, as Motor City GC will be the league’s seventh franchise. On Tuesday, TGL announced the complete rosters for its third season, and there have been some changes along with the introduction of Motor City GC. Before, teams had four players on a roster, with three participating each week. Now, teams will have five players, but still only three players will tee it up for each match at the SoFi Center in Florida.

Golf.title: Hero World Challenge field announced, but will Tiger Woods play?
Golf.summary: The field for the 2026 Hero World Challenge is mostly set, although there are still spots available if the host, Tiger Woods, wants to play. The post Hero World Challenge field announced, but will Tiger Woods play? appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Seven of the world's top 10 players will compete at the Hero World Challenge, hosted by Tiger Woods, at Albany in the Bahamas on 3-6 December. Scottie Scheffler, Matt Fitzpatrick and Cameron Young headline the field. Only 17 of the 20 players were announced on Monday, with three places left as "TBA tournament exemption" spots.

Woods is not yet in the field, but he could take one of the exemptions, as he has done in some previous years. He has not played competitively since missing the cut at the 2024 Open Championship, and he last played the Hero in 2023. He ruptured his Achilles in March 2025 and had a back disc replacement in October 2025. He has also been named on the TGL season three roster, as captain of Jupiter Links.
Golf.copy:
The field for this year’s Hero World Challenge is mostly set, with few surprises, although now the big storyline is if the tournament host will tee it up as well. Seven of the top 10 players in the world will compete at the Tiger Woods-hosted Hero World Challenge Dec. 3-6 at Albany in the Bahamas, and no, Woods is not in the 20-player field. At least not yet.

While it wouldn’t be surprising if Woods sat this one out, only 17 players were announced Monday, with three spots remaining for a “TBA tournament exemption.” Leaving a few spots available for last-minute exemptions is typical for the Hero, and it also makes it convenient for Woods to snag one himself — without kicking a player out — if he’s satisfied with his health and game. In past years Woods has used one of these exemptions on himself, but other times he’s passed on it.

Golf.title: You can now (finally) play this once off-limits Wyoming stunner
Golf.summary: New accommodations at Snake River Sporting Club offer guests a way on to a spectacular Tom Weiskopf design. The post You can now (finally) play this once off-limits Wyoming stunner appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Early in your round at Snake River Sporting Club, you pass a wooden cabin about the size of a turnstand. No snacks are on sale here. It’s only the 3rd hole, you don’t need them yet. The cabin is a relic: evidence that homesteaders were here before Tom Weiskopf, before the club, before any of this was given over to golf.

In the early 1800s, this swath of land alongside the Snake River, south of what is now Jackson Hole, Wyo., was fertile ground for the fur trade. Prospectors of other stripes came later, settling down and building infrastructure of all kinds, including that modest wooden cabin. Another century passed before Weiskopf arrived. The former major champion-turned-course architect drew up a routing that became the centerpiece of an exclusive golf club. The course opened in 2006, making it much younger than the cabin. Like the cabin, though, it fits the landscape. It looks as if it’s been there all along.

It hauls 14 clubs (15 if nobody’s looking), dozens of balls, a rangefinder, a rain jacket and whatever snack and drink stash you opt to carry. And it does it every round. If we’re being honest, most of us probably don’t think about our bag until something goes wrong: a zipper that sticks, a strap that digs in, a divider that lets your irons clang together.

Then there’s the summer. Months of heat and direct sun fade fabric, wear down zippers, and weaken stitching. Sweaty hands and wet-weather rounds leave their mark too. Your bag that felt fine in May can be pretty tired by October.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: I hit my ball to the edge of the cup. How long can I wait for it to fall in?
Golf.summary: When your ball ends up on the edge of the cup, how long do you get to wait for it to fall in? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: I hit my ball to the edge of the cup. How long can I wait for it to fall in? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. Jack hits his approach to the very edge of the cup, while his playing partners all miss the putting surface. He checks on his ball but doesn’t mark it until the others are on the green, hoping it will fall in during the extended wait. Is this allowed? – Daryl Laumann, via email

By “very edge of the cup,” presumably you mean the ball is overhanging the edge. In this case, Jack gets a reasonable time to reach the ball, from however far away that might be, and then 10 seconds maximum to see if it will fall in — whether the other players have reached the green or not. (Clarification 13.3a/1 highlights the meaning of “reasonable time.”)

Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi on 13 October, he said LIV's emergence also affected TGL, their joint venture through TMRW Sports with the PGA Tour, whose rules generally require players to be PGA Tour members in good standing.

McIlroy said LIV wasted significant capital and could have used it more strategically, including by partnering with golf's governing bodies. He said he would now vote to allow former LIV golfers back onto the PGA Tour and DP World Tour, arguing their return could increase revenue and strengthen the tours' product. Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy has explained why he and Tiger Woods became two of the strongest opponents of LIV Golf when the breakaway league emerged in 2022. Their resistance involved more than protecting the PGA Tour's established structure. McIlroy says both men had personal and professional interests that could suffer as golf fractured into competing circuits.

Their joint venture, TGL, was among the projects caught in that conflict. Now, as LIV faces bankruptcy proceedings and uncertainty over its future, McIlroy's latest comments offer fresh insight into the rivalry. His position has also softened as several LIV players reconsider their careers.

Golf.title: 2 huge reasons golfers have early extension — and how to fix them
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Brian Mogg explains two reasons he sees golfers early extend — and shares how to fix them. The post 2 huge reasons golfers have early extension — and how to fix them appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
One of the most common swing problems I see among recreational golfers is early extension. You’ve probably heard the term before. It occurs when your hips and pelvis move toward the golf ball during the downswing, leaving less room for your arms and club to move freely through impact. The result? Your chest rises, your posture changes, and making consistent contact becomes much more difficult.

But here’s something I’ve learned after decades of teaching golfers around the world: Early extension is often the result of another swing flaw, not the original problem. That’s why simply telling a golfer to keep their hips back doesn’t always work. To make a lasting improvement, you need to understand what’s causing your hips to move toward the ball in the first place.

No LPGA Tour or LIV Golf winners have used one in 2026.
Golf.copy:
Broomstick putters continue to be used on the professional circuits, with the idea behind them to help create a more fluid stroke to eliminate the dreaded yips. They've been around since roughly the 1980s and, during that time, have earned many big wins, including The Masters in 2013, when Adam Scott used his Scotty Cameron to claim a Green Jacket.

However, just a few years after Scott's victory, golf's governing bodies introduced a rule change that impacted the broomstick putter, as players were now no longer allowed to anchor it in the stroke.

Golf.title: This Is Easily My Favourite Golfing Island In The Caribbean
Golf.summary: Rob Smith returns to one of his very favourite golfing destinations, the Dominican Republic – set in the beautiful, glittering Caribbean Sea...
bullets: A Golf Monthly contributing editor names the Dominican Republic as one of the finest golf destinations in the world, having played in around 50 countries. His first visit was to Playa Dorada, a Robert Trent Jones course opened in 1976 at Puerto Plata. He later returned to cover the Latin America Amateur Championship at Teeth of the Dog, part of the Casa de Campo resort.

Teeth of the Dog, a Pete Dye design built in 1971, features seven oceanside holes and has recently received a full upgrade. Casa de Campo also has To Dye Fore and The Links, while Corales, designed by Tom Fazio, hosts the Puntacana Championship on the PGA Tour. He also recommends Punta Espada, a 2006 Jack Nicklaus design, as well as La Cana and PGA Ocean's 4.
Golf.copy:
The first time I was lucky enough to visit the Caribbean was a lifetime ago, way before I worked in golf. My first wife and a couple of our best friends decided to push the boat out – not literally, as that would have taken too long – and spend a fortnight in the Dominican Republic. We stayed on the north coast at Puerto Plata and played Playa Dorada, a Robert Trent Jones course that opened in 1976.

Expecting to get a couple of rounds in, I think we played seven or eight times and a love affair with golf in the Caribbean was born. I've not been back to Playa Dorada, but I remember it with great affection.

Golf.title: As legal battle rages on, President Trump sets new date to renovate beloved D.C. muni
