bullets: President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that his planned renovation of East Potomac Golf Links in Washington, D.C. would begin on 15 November and close the course for 15 months. He said he and architect Tom Fazio had developed a plan to allow it to host major championships, Ryder Cups and Presidents Cups, and posted a rendering of a single 18-hole course that removes Ohio Drive, a grove of cherry trees and the miniature golf course.

The announcement comes as a legal challenge continues, with Judge Ana C. Reyes ordering two administration officials to testify on Monday after the Interior Department removed over 400 trees at the site. She also barred further tree removal until 26 October. Opponents say the overhaul would raise greens fees and cut tee-time availability at a course that hosted 124,500 rounds in 2025, the busiest in the area.
Golf.copy:
The legal battle over the future of East Potomac Golf Links is set to continue Monday. But President Donald Trump added a new wrinkle on Sunday, announcing on Truth Social that his planned renovation of the historic muni would begin Nov. 15, closing the course for 15 months. Trump said he and architect Tom Fazio had “developed a plan” that would allow the course to host major championships, Ryder Cups and Presidents Cups.

Trump also posted a rendering of the proposed changes, which bears little resemblance to the existing course. The design shows a dramatically remade Hains Point, the peninsula where East Potomac sits, with a single 18-hole golf course stretching from shoreline to shoreline. It also differs substantially from the more modest proposal that was put forth earlier this year, eliminating Ohio Drive, a century-old grove of cherry trees and a renowned miniature golf course. The changes would reshape a public recreational space used by golfers, walkers,, cyclists, bird watchers and others.

Golf.title: Ruoning Yin defends Shanghai title, earns 7th LPGA win
Golf.summary: Ruoning Yin wins the 2026 Buick LPGA Shanghai, defending her title and earning back-to-back LPGA Tour victories. The post Ruoning Yin defends Shanghai title, earns 7th LPGA win appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Ruoning Yin successfully defended her Buick LPGA Shanghai title on Sunday, securing her second consecutive LPGA Tour win after the FM Championship and her seventh overall. The 23-year-old played her final 36 holes nine under, closing with five birdies and one bogey, including two birdies in her last three holes.

Yin led the field with 55 greens in regulation from 72 and hit 14 of 14 fairways in the final round. She became the second player to win the event twice, after Danielle Kang in 2018 and 2019, and is the only player from China to win it. She has passed $3 million in season earnings and moved to fifth in the Race to the CME Globe with three tournaments left.
Golf.copy:
Ruoning Yin is on a roll. The 23-year-old won the Buick LPGA Shanghai on Sunday, successfully defending her title and earning her second consecutive LPGA Tour victory after winning the FM Championship in her previous start.

Playing in front of a home crowd, Yin bounced back from a two-over-par second round by playing her final 36 holes nine under. She closed with five birdies and one bogey Sunday, making two birdies in her final three holes to secure her seventh LPGA Tour win.

Golf.title: Butterfield Bermuda Championship Field Confirmed As PGA Tour Winners Feature But Notable Names Miss Out
Golf.summary: Adam Schenk defends his title as former champions, other PGA Tour winners and top US amateurs compete
bullets: The Butterfield Bermuda Championship, part of the FedExCup Fall, is being held at Port Royal Golf Course. None of the world's top 50 are playing, with Corey Conners the highest-ranked entrant at World No.60, followed by Austin Smotherman in 66th and Eric Cole in 82nd. Lucas Glover, Taylor Moore and Seamus Power are among those working to finish inside the top 100 in the FedEx Cup standings after the RSM Classic.

Former champions in the field include Power (2022), Camilo Villegas (2023), Rafael Campos (2024), Adam Schenk, who won last year, and Brendon Todd (2019). Amateurs include Miles Russell, Kihei Akina, Jay Leng Jr and 2025 US Amateur champion Mason Howell. Absentees include Marco Penge, 10 places outside the top-100 cut-off, Rasmus Hojgaard, 113th, and Billy Horschel, 90th.
Golf.copy:
The FedExCup Fall phase of the PGA Tour season continues with the Butterfield Bermuda Championship, which will be held at Port Royal Golf Course. With each passing event, the pressure grows on players still battling to secure their PGA Tour cards for the following season.

As a result, the field includes several players with work to do to ensure they finish inside the top 100 in the FedEx Cup standings following the season-ending RSM Classic. Notable names among those are PGA Tour winners Lucas Glover, Taylor Moore and Seamus Power.

Golf.title: As LIV Golf fades away, Eugenio Chacarra might be the biggest winner of golf's civil war
Golf.summary: Just about everyone in pro golf benefitted from the the PGA Tour-LIV battle. But perhaps no one was a bigger winner than Eugenio Chacarra. The post As LIV Golf fades away, Eugenio Chacarra might be the biggest winner of golf’s civil war appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Eugenio Chacarra, 26, took the Race to Dubai lead by winning the DP World India Championship with rounds of 67-67-63-70, beating Daniel Hillier by two for his third title of the season. The Spaniard left LIV Golf after the 2024 season having earned $16 million in 34 starts, and has since won the Hero Indian Open, KLM Open and DS Automobiles 83° Open d'Italia.

Chacarra said he wanted major starts, Ryder Cups and DP World Tour wins, and that LIV had given him a financial base and a strong team. He improved his nutrition and recovery in 2026 and played through a fractured toe, finishing T3 at the French Open and T2 at the Spanish Open. His results have all but secured his 2027 PGA Tour spot, while LIV is in bankruptcy court.
Golf.copy:
If you ask Rory McIlroy, Justin Rose, or any number of top pros, almost everyone benefited from the years-long battle between the PGA Tour, the DP World Tour, and LIV Golf. If you stuck with the established tours, LIV’s emergence forced them to make needed changes; purses increased and stagnation ended. If you defected to the then-Saudi-backed league, you secured riches that were exponentially greater than what pro golfers had thought possible. Some, like Bryson DeChambeau, increased their popularity. Some, like Lee Westwood and Ian Poulter, got a nice payday as their careers reached the final stage. Others, like Brooks Koepka and Patrick Reed, got in early and left before the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund (PIF) withdrew funding, sending LIV into a tailspin that has landed the league in bankruptcy court, where it is sinking as players exit. Time will tell how much the defection cost players like Jon Rahm and Cameron Smith when it comes to major opportunities and overall legacy, but they still benefited greatly from the move and will likely get to return to the tour whose shores they once torched in due time.

But while most of pro golf’s many stakeholders finished the civil war in the green, perhaps no one was a bigger winner than Eugenio Chacarra. The young Spaniard was one of the first to leave for LIV Golf. He was the No. 2-ranked amateur in the world while at Oklahoma State and elected to take a signing bonus to join Sergio Garcia’s Fireballs GC team in 2022 instead of pursuing his initial dream: the PGA Tour. Chacarra, a ball-striking star, won early on LIV but then struggled with injuries. His contract wasn’t renewed after the 2024 season, and he chose not to try to earn his spot back on the rebel tour via LIV Q School. Instead, Chacarra aired his grievances about how things were done on LIV. He said it was about “only money” and he wanted more. After earning $16 million in 34 starts on LIV, Chacarra wanted to chase his original dreams and believed his game could get him there in due time.

Golf.title: 'How would he know?': Rory McIlroy dismisses Kevin Kisner's cash-grab claim
Golf.summary: At the DP World India Championship, Rory McIlroy dismissed Kevin Kisner's suggestion that he had made the trip just for the money. The post ‘How would he know?’: Rory McIlroy dismisses Kevin Kisner’s cash-grab claim appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Rory McIlroy responded to Kevin Kisner's claim that he played the DP World India Championship in New Delhi purely for money, asking "How would he know that?" McIlroy, who was in the event for a second straight year, received an undisclosed appearance fee, as did other leading players including Tommy Fleetwood and Justin Rose.

Kisner, speaking on the Fore Play podcast, said many players are paid to appear and doubted that the aim was to expand golf in India. McIlroy said both could be true, noting that players can be paid while genuinely trying to bring the sport to a developing country where the middle class exceeds the population of the United States. He finished T42, 17 shots behind winner Eugenio Chacarra.
Golf.copy:
Just because Rory McIlroy is growing his bank account doesn’t mean he isn’t also trying to grow the game. So the Northern Irishman said in response to criticism from Kevin Kisner, who questioned McIlroy’s stated motivations for playing in this week’s DP World India Championship in New Delhi.

In case you missed it, here’s the context. McIlroy was in the tournament for the second straight year and, like several other marquee players in the field, including Tommy Fleetwood and Justin Rose, he received an undisclosed appearance fee.

Golf.title: How the PGA Tour's best putter warms up before every round
Golf.summary: Get an in-depth look at Jacob Bridgeman's practice putting routine and steal his keys to boost your performance on the green. The post How the PGA Tour’s best putter warms up before every round appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Jacob Bridgeman led the PGA Tour this season with 63.585 total Strokes Gained: Putting, more than 23 strokes clear of the next-best player on 40.43. He keeps his approach simple, avoiding tinkering with his stroke and concentrating on start line, distance control and building consistency from close range.

In a video with TaylorMade, he explained that his warm-up begins with a start-line drill, using tees as a gate over a four- to six-foot, slightly uphill putt. He then works around the hole from four to six feet, before moving to seven-and-a-half and nine feet and varying pace with three balls. He finishes with 15 minutes of realistic scenarios, saying: "The less I do, the less can go wrong."
Golf.copy:
Jacob Bridgeman is on a roll with his putter, and the numbers are pretty wild. This season, he led the field with 63.585 total Strokes Gained: Putting, more than 23 strokes ahead of the next-best player at 40.43. In other words, his putter gives him a serious advantage over his competitors.

So, what’s the secret to his success on the greens? Surprisingly, Bridgeman keeps things pretty simple. He doesn’t tinker with his stroke or get caught up in the mechanics. Instead, he focuses on his start line, distance control and building his consistency from close range.

Golf.title: What these former NHL stars think about their golf games | Subpar
Golf.summary: On GOLF's Subpar podcast, former NHLers Brenden Morror and Mike Commodore talked hockey fights, golf matches and more. The post What these former NHL stars think about their golf games | Subpar appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
If there’s anything better than being a professional athlete, it’s being a retired professional athlete who’s really good at golf. You get to extend your competitive career, only now the stakes are a little lower and the equipment is a lot different.

Brenden Morrow has taken that route, competing on The Pro Tour, an invitation-only circuit for retired professional athletes. His fellow former NHLer, Mike Commodore, can get around a golf course, too, though he’s not quite convinced his game is ready for The Pro Tour.

Golf.title: Japanese Pro Secures Masters And Open Spots With Victory At National Championship
Golf.summary: Yusaku Hosono's second victory of the season has earned him invitations to two of golf's biggest events
bullets: Yusaku Hosono won the Japan Open Golf Championship at Tarao Country Club by two shots over Yusuke Sakamoto, earning places at the 2027 Masters and Open Championship. He shot rounds of 65, 64, 68 and 70, and it was his second win of the season after the Japan PGA Championship Senko Group Cup in May.

Invitations come through an alignment between Augusta National and The R&A that began in 2025 and was confirmed in September to continue. Hosono is the third player to qualify for both Majors this way, after Tom Kim via the Genesis Scottish Open and Grant Forrest via the Open de Espana. Winners of the Hong Kong Open, Australian Open and South African Open will also receive invitations. The 2027 Open is at the Old Course, St Andrews.
Golf.copy:
Yusaku Hosono has booked his place at next year's Masters and Open Championship after securing a two-shot victory at the Japan Open Golf Championship in his homeland. Hosono’s win at Tarao Country Club was his second of an impressive season after victory at the Japan PGA Championship Senko Group Cup in May.

However, with invitations to two of golf's biggest events also secured, his win in his home open is the more significant of the two. In September, Augusta National Golf Club and The R&A confirmed that an alignment that began in 2025, which would see invites to The Masters and The Open given to winners of select opens, would continue.

Golf.title: Chacarra wins in India to take Race to Dubai lead
Golf.summary: Eugenio Chacarra wins the DP World India Championship by two strokes to move top of the Race to Dubai standings ahead of Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy.
bullets: Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship at Delhi Golf Club by two strokes, finishing on 21 under to move top of the Race to Dubai standings ahead of Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy. After rounds of 67 and 67, bad light halted his third round on Saturday; he completed a nine-under 63 on Sunday for a five-shot lead, then shot 70 to hold off New Zealand's Daniel Hillier, who birdied the last.

It was the 26-year-old Spaniard's third win of the season, and he aims to become the third Spaniard to top the standings after Jon Rahm and Seve Ballesteros. Reed, who had led since March, finished eight under in a tie for 23rd, while McIlroy shot 74 in the final round to share 42nd. Three events remain before the winner is crowned next month.
Golf.copy:
Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship by two strokes to move top of the Race to Dubai standings ahead of Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy. Spain's Chacarra finished on 21 under, with American Reed and world number two McIlroy well off the pace by the final round of this event.

After opening with successive scores of 67 in his first two rounds at Delhi Golf Club, bad light halted play with Chacarra still on the 11th hole of his third round on Saturday.

Golf.title: 'How Would He Know That?'
Golf.summary: The six-time Major winner has responded to Kisner's suggestion that his main motivation for playing in the DP World India Championship was his appearance fee
bullets: Rory McIlroy has rejected Kevin Kisner's claim that he played the DP World India Championship only for a large appearance fee. Kisner told the Fore Play podcast that McIlroy "wants to get his $10m and go play in India". McIlroy, who finished tied for 42nd at Delhi Golf Club, replied: "How would he know that?"

McIlroy said two things can be true at once: players can be paid to appear while also having a genuine interest in growing golf in India, where the middle class is larger than the whole US population. He called India an important market for golf. He is third in the Race to Dubai behind Eugenio Chacarra and Patrick Reed, and said Chacarra's form makes his bid for an eighth title harder with two events left.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy has responded to Kevin Kisner’s claim that he only played in the DP World India Championship because he received a large appearance fee. Kisner gave his opinion on McIlroy’s reason for playing at the Delhi Golf Club event to the Fore Play podcast.

He poured scorn on the six-time Major winner's supposed motivation for playing, which he suggested was to help grow the game globally. He said: "That is such a dog s*** comment. But I guess for the right price we could all say that.

Golf.title: Eugenio Chacarra Wins DP World India Championship To Move Top Of Race To Dubai Rankings
Golf.summary: Eugenio Chacarra claimed his fourth DP World Tour title with a two-shot victory in Delhi
bullets: Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship at Delhi Golf Club by two shots from Daniel Hillier, claiming his fourth DP World Tour title in 19 months. After play was suspended on Saturday, he completed his third round with a 63, including an eagle at the 18th, then closed with three pars. Adrian Meronk and Angel Hidalgo tied for third on 15 under.

It was Chacarra's third win of the season and moves him above Patrick Reed to the top of the Race to Dubai, with Rory McIlroy third. It is also set to take him to the top of the European Ryder Cup rankings ahead of the match at Adare Manor in Ireland next September. He said he wants to qualify through one of the six automatic spots rather than as a pick.
Golf.copy:
Eugenio Chacarra has claimed his fourth DP World Tour title in 19 months, beating Daniel Hillier at the DP World India Championship. When darkness forced the suspension of play on Saturday evening at Delhi Golf Club, Chacarra led by two, but, like much of the field, he still had to complete his third round.

That led to an early start on Sunday, when the former LIV Golfer carded a 63, helped by an eagle at the 18th, to take control of proceedings. At that stage, he led Hillier by five shots, with defending champion Tommy Fleetwood 10 back.

Golf.title: Former LIV Golf recruit sends Ryder Cup message with victory in India
Golf.summary: Former LIV Golf recruit sends Ryder Cup message with victory in India Golfmagic
bullets: Eugenio Chacarra, a former LIV Golf recruit, won the DP World India Championship at Delhi Golf Club, his third victory of the season after the KLM Open and the Italian Open. Torrential rain and lightning on the opening day of the $5m event forced him to play 25 holes on Sunday. He shot a bogey-free nine-under-par 63 in the third round and a 2-under-par 70 in the afternoon, winning by two shots from New Zealand's Daniel Hillier.

The win moves the Spaniard above Patrick Reed at the top of the Race to Dubai, with the two season-ending DP World Tour play-offs in the Middle East still to come. Chacarra said he wants to qualify for Europe's 2027 Ryder Cup team in County Limerick through one of the six automatic spots, not as a captain's pick. He will play in Korea next week to extend his lead over Reed.
Golf.copy:
Former LIV Golf recruit Eugenio Chacarra was overcome with emotion after claiming his third victory of the season at the weather-disrupted DP World India Championship. Torrential rain and lightning on the opening day of the $5m event at Delhi Golf Club left tournament officials scrambling to make up for lost time.

Chacarra was consequently forced to play 25 holes on Sunday, first putting the finishing touches to a superb bogey-free nine-under-par 63 in his third round before completing the job in the afternoon with a 2-under-par 70 to win by two shots from New Zealand's Daniel Hillier.

Golf.title: LPGA Tour Hands Out Slow Play Penalties To Two Players At Buick LPGA Shanghai
Golf.summary: Carlota Ciganda and Yealimi Noh were handed slow play penalties during the Buick LPGA Shanghai, with both going over their allotted time in accordance with the LPGA Tour’s Pace of Play Policy
Golf.copy:
Professional circuits are starting to crack down on slow play and, at the Buick LPGA Shanghai, two players were handed penalties for just that on Saturday. The two players in question were Carlota Ciganda and Yealimi Noh, who were both playing the back nine when the penalties were enforced, due to the fact that they both went over their allotted time in accordance with the LPGA Tour’s Pace of Play Policy.

Reaching out to the LPGA Tour, a statement was sent to Golf Monthly from the circuit, with it being confirmed that both Solheim Cup players had received the penalty during their third rounds.

Golf.title: As LIV Golf 'experiment' ends, Justin Rose ready to welcome defectors back
Golf.summary: With LIV Golf struggling to survive in bankruptcy court, Justin Rose is ready to welcome Jon Rahm and others back. "No bad blood," he said. The post As LIV Golf ‘experiment’ ends, Justin Rose ready to welcome defectors back appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Justin Rose, who won this year's Farmers Insurance Open, said he is ready to welcome LIV Golf defectors back to the established tours. He turned down LIV's offer in 2022, saying his career goals were only attainable on the European Tour and the PGA Tour. LIV is now in bankruptcy court as it tries to reinvent itself as "LIV 2.0" without Saudi backing, and Jon Rahm is among several players to have left.

Speaking to The Mirror at the DP World India Championship, Rose called LIV "an experiment; a whirlwind four or five years" and said there were no hard feelings. He said the disruption forced the PGA Tour and DP World Tour to become better versions of themselves. Rahm and others plan to play the DP World Tour in 2027, while Rory McIlroy has also said he has no problem with their return.
Golf.copy:
Justin Rose was a prime target for LIV Golf when the then-Saudi-backed league burst onto the scene in 2022. He was a former major champion and former World No. 1 whose game had dipped as the twilight of his career appeared to beckon. LIV was paying for names and resumes, hoping that big names would help drive interest. But while Phil Mickelson, Dustin Johnson, Sergio Garcia, and others left, Rose turned down LIV’s offer, choosing instead to dig it out of the dirt and rediscover his world-class game.

“My career goals have always only been attainable by staying on the European Tour and the PGA Tour because access to them is not, you know, not possible the other way,” Rose said on Sunday after winning this year’s Farmers Insurance Open about his decision to reject LIV and the ripple effects of it.

Golf.title: Top teacher shares 2 ways to hit it flop shot
Golf.summary: Want to master the flop shot? GOLF Top 100 Teacher Debbie Doniger shares two techniques that will make these tricky shots easier to execute. The post Top teacher shares 2 ways to hit it flop shot appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
When you’re short-sided around the green with an obstacle between you and the flag, a high, open-faced flop shot can be your best chance to save par. The problem? Executing it. For many amateurs, inconsistent contact can turn a potential up-and-down into a costly mistake.

However, GOLF Top 100 Teacher Debbie Doniger has two methods that can make this tricky shot more manageable. In the video below, Doniger breaks down a beginner-friendly option and a high-launching shot for more experienced players.

Golf.title: Slow play in Shanghai: LPGA hands out multiple two-stroke penalties
Golf.summary: Carlota Ciganda was one of two players assessed a two-stroke penalty for slow play during the third round of the Buick LPGA Shanghai. The post Slow play in Shanghai: LPGA hands out multiple two-stroke penalties appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Carlota Ciganda was given a two-stroke slow-play penalty after the par-4 13th hole at Sheshan Golf Club in the third round of the Buick LPGA Shanghai, turning a par into a double bogey. She responded with birdies on the next two holes and finished with a 1-under 71, leaving her tied fourth going into Sunday's final round. Yealimi Noh was also reportedly penalised for slow play.

Under the LPGA's Pace of Play Policy, updated in 2025, officials usually warn a group that falls out of position before timing players, with exceptions for groups significantly out of position and for the final three holes. A timed player has about 40 seconds per shot. A first timing violation generally brings a warning, a subsequent one can bring a one-stroke penalty, and further breaches can lead to two strokes.
Golf.copy:
A slow-play penalty turned an otherwise routine hole into a costly moment for Carlota Ciganda during the third round of the Buick LPGA Shanghai. On Saturday, Sky Sports golf commentator Richard Kaufman reported that Ciganda was assessed a two-stroke penalty after finishing the par-4 13th hole at Sheshan Golf Club. The penalty transformed her par into a devastating double bogey, knocking her down the leaderboard.

Two players have been penalised for slow play @LPGA today in China. Carlota Ciganda given a 2 shot penalty when in contention and responded with 2 immediate birdies. Yealimi Noh also penalised. Not the 1st time for either player.

Golf.title: Patrick Reed isn't the only obstacle Rory McIlroy faces in chase for his next big goal
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy is chasing his next career goal. Patrick Reed is in his way but he's not the only obstacle the six-time major winner faces. The post Patrick Reed isn’t the only obstacle Rory McIlroy faces in chase for his next big goal appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Rory McIlroy is chasing a record-tying eighth Race to Dubai title, having won seven overall and the last four in a row, but Patrick Reed has led the standings since winning in Dubai and Qatar earlier this year. Reed left LIV Golf in January and is serving a one-year PGA Tour suspension. A top-10 finish in the standings secures him a 2027 PGA Tour card.

Eugenio Chacarra, who entered the DP World India Championship second in the standings after jumping McIlroy at the Spanish Open, led at 14 under after two and a half rounds at Delhi Golf Club. He is 166 points behind Reed and has won the KLM Open and the Open d'Italia this season. Reed sits eight shots back and McIlroy ten, with play suspended on Saturday due to darkness.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy has been hunting his next big goal ever since the major championship season came to a close. It’s in his sights, but a former rival stands in his way. “Once major season was over, that’s what I turned my attention to,” McIlroy said on The Locker Room, the DP World Tour’s preview show, ahead of this week’s DP World India Championship about chasing his record-tying eighth Race to Dubai title.

McIlroy has won four Race to Dubai titles in a row and has seven overall. An eighth would tie Colin Montgomerie’s record, a mark that McIlroy covets. McIlroy exited the major season and set his sights on Patrick Reed, who won in Dubai and Qatar earlier this year and has been atop the Race to Dubai standings ever since.

Golf.title: 'No lawsuits anymore': Patrick Reed has earned Rory McIlroy's 'respect' post-LIV exit
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy and Patrick Reed have had a frosty relationship over the last few years. But things are thawing after Reed's LIV Golf exit. The post ‘No lawsuits anymore’: Patrick Reed has earned Rory McIlroy’s ‘respect’ post-LIV exit appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Rory McIlroy said Patrick Reed has earned his respect since leaving LIV Golf in January, joking "there's no lawsuits anymore" after his first round at the DP World India Championship. Reed accepted a one-year PGA Tour suspension and has played the DP World Tour, winning in Dubai and Qatar and leading the Race to Dubai standings. McIlroy said the route Reed took meant a lot to the tour and his peers.

The relationship soured when Reed's lawyer served McIlroy a subpoena on Christmas Eve, and Reed flicked a tee at him at the Dubai Desert Classic in January 2023. Reed told The Mirror the relationship was improving and that he hoped to play more with McIlroy on weekends. Eugenio Chacarra led the event after two and a half rounds and is second in the standings.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy and Patrick Reed have been rivals for over a decade, both on and off the golf course. The emergence of LIV Golf, Reed’s decision to defect to the rebel league, and the subsequent litigation only heightened the tension between the six-time major champion and Reed.

But those tensions seem to be thawing. Reed left LIV Golf in January, accepted a one-year PGA Tour suspension and worked to play his way back to the American circuit by finishing in the top 10 in the DP World Tour’s Race to Dubai standings. Reed won in Dubai and Qatar earlier this year, all but securing his return to the PGA Tour in 2027. Reed’s willingness to take his punishment and trust himself to shoot the scores needed to return to the PGA Tour has earned respect from McIlroy.

Golf.title: 'Wants his $10 million': Kevin Kisner rips Rory McIlroy for 'grow the game' contradiction in India
Golf.summary: On The Fore Play Podcast, Kevin Kisner criticized Rory McIlroy for saying he wanted to grow the game in India while receiving an appearance fee. The post ‘Wants his $10 million’: Kevin Kisner rips Rory McIlroy for ‘grow the game’ contradiction in India appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Kevin Kisner criticised Rory McIlroy on the Fore Play podcast, suggesting McIlroy is playing the DP World India Championship for an appearance fee rather than to grow the game. Kisner claimed McIlroy "wants to get his $10 million bucks", though the amount is not publicly disclosed. McIlroy is playing the event for a second straight year, and Justin Rose and Tommy Fleetwood are also being paid to appear.

The comments followed McIlroy's appearance at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, where he said he hoped taking part would increase access to golf in India. Kisner also noted McIlroy is unlikely to use his driver on the course. Fellow host Riggs echoed the scepticism about portraying such appearances as efforts to grow the game, and the players were required to carry out promotional duties including a "Diwali with the Stars" dinner.
Golf.copy:

Golf.copy:
Everyone has accidentally butchered someone’s name at one point or another. But normally that name isn’t “Gary,” and normally that person isn’t a professional athlete. But on the latest episode of GOLF’s Subpar Podcast, former NHL star Brenden Morrow recalled playing a round at TPC Craig Ranch with Subpar co-host Colt Knost and Gary Woodland, and spending the entire day calling Woodland “Jerry.”

“I can read [his bag],” Morrow told Knost and Drew Stoltz as he started to recall the story. “I thought his name was Gary. I’m going to death that I heard one of you jack—-s call him Jerry. So I’m like, ‘Who am I?’ It’s written right on his bag, ‘Gary.’ But whatever, maybe his parents just did it. So I started calling him Jerry the entire round. He should’ve probably corrected me. He didn’t. Then, he got in my car. I drove him to North Park Mall. His now-wife, girlfriend at the time, Gabby, [was there], dropped him off. ‘Hey Jerry, had a hell of a time. I’ll catch you later.’ Still, nobody corrected me the entire day. So he’s forever known as Jerry Woodland.”

Golf.title: All the players who have left LIV Golf (so far)
Golf.summary: All the players who have left LIV Golf (so far) Golf Digest
bullets: LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September. Brooks Koepka left on 23 December 2025 and Patrick Reed made his exit official on 28 January 2026. Sergio Garcia's contract was terminated at a New Jersey hearing on 6 October.

Jon Rahm's lawyer told the judge on 7 October that his client had "no interest" in LIV 2.0, and David Puig said he does not see himself playing in it. Abraham Ancer, Charles Howell III and Thomas Pieters are reported to be heading to the DP World Tour, and Adrian Meronk is reported to have no intention of extending his contract. Cameron Smith is among players seeking a release similar to Garcia's, and LIV has asked for an extra week to review his request.
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf 1.0 is gone. The pomp, pageantry and hot-air-balloon contracts of the LIV’s first iteration went up in smoke when the league filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September. Now the future of LIV Golf hinges on financing efforts for its next chapter, colloquially referred to as LIV Golf 2.0. According to recent reports, the league must obtain key stakeholder and court approval to complete the transaction with its angel investor, BC Partners.

Key to the future of LIV Golf, however, is the status of its top pros, who will operate as equity owners of the league and its respective teams under the plan laid out by CEO Scott O’Neil. Without those players and their literal and figurative buy-in, LIV Golf may not survive to see its second chapter. So where does that leave the floundering tour as the clock continues to tick? Which players have indicated their intention of leaving (or have formally asked the court to be released from their 1.0 contract), which haven’t and which are still sitting on the fence? Let’s take a look.

Visit Myrtle Beach will continue as sole title sponsor, and there will be no change to the $4m purse.

ONEflight had put up half of the $4m purse and helped bring celebrities to the Wednesday Pro-Am. New tournament director Steve Mays, announced on Thursday, said the event would proceed as the Myrtle Beach Classic with Visit Myrtle Beach as title sponsor and would focus on the fan experience. Visit Myrtle Beach president Stuart Butler confirmed continued sponsorship. Brandt Snedeker is the defending champion after winning this year's event.
Golf.copy:
The 2027 Myrtle Beach Classic will take place as scheduled despite the PGA Tour severing ties with joint title sponsor ONEflight International. The PGA Tour has parted ways with the Colorado-based luxury travel company which is facing a number of federal fraud lawsuits after suddenly ceasing operations in September.

But although ONEflight has been dropped, the other co-main sponsor Visit Myrtle Beach will continue to support the event and there'll be no change to tournament prize money next year.

Golf.title: 2 more LIV players head for exit, eye DP World Tour futures
Golf.summary: New reports on Thursday added two LIV Golf pros to the growing list of pros fleeing the league: Thomas Pieters and Charles Howell III. The post 2 more LIV players head for exit, eye DP World Tour futures appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Thomas Pieters and Charles Howell III are reported to be leaving LIV Golf and seeking DP World Tour starts in 2027, according to reports from Flushing It Golf and Sports Business Journal's Josh A. Carpenter. They join Jon Rahm, David Puig, Abraham Ancer and Adrian Meronk among players who have confirmed their departures. The exits have accelerated since the DP World Tour announced that LIV players would be banned from its events next year.

Pieters won six DP World Tour titles before joining LIV ahead of 2023, most recently the 2022 Abu Dhabi HSBC Championship, and played in the 2016 European Ryder Cup team. Howell, ranked 510th in the world, has barely played on the DP World Tour and would need an invite, which prompted criticism from DP World Tour regular Joost Luiten. In a bankruptcy court filing on Wednesday, LIV's lawyers said a decision on LIV 2.0 or a wind-down is expected by the end of the month. LIV also rejected the contracts of 19 players, including Bryson DeChambeau.
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf has taken blow after blow in recent weeks as it races to secure its future. Since the start of its Chapter 11 bankruptcy hearings, the league has seen several pros abandon it.

After the DP World Tour announced LIV players would be banned from its events next year, the departures accelerated. Most of those players are eyeing the DP World Tour for playing time in 2027, with the PGA Tour out of reach, for now.

bullets: New Zealand's Ben Campbell has told Today's Golfer he would stay with LIV Golf next season if LIV 2.0 gets over the line. He would aim to combine 10 to 15 Asian Tour and Australasian events with 10 LIV events.

BC Partners, the London-based credit firm pledging $300m, requires a 'critical mass' of player commitments before an initial 25 October deadline. David Puig, Thomas Pieters and Charles Howell III are set to follow Jon Rahm out. The proposed relaunch would have 10 events with purses of $5.5m to $9m, compared with the $30m previously paid at each event. The DP World Tour will refuse memberships to players who sign for LIV 2.0, and those with status must apply for cards before 16 November. Bryson DeChambeau's original contract has been rejected, and he has not said what he will do.
Golf.copy:
TG has spoken to a LIV player who says he wants to continue with the league next season. It seems there’s a theme among those committing to 2.0… With a deadline looming and futures at stake, we’re about to learn what a “critical mass of players sufficient to operate a bona fide professional golf league” really looks like.

That’s the latest requirement laid out in bankruptcy court documents by BC Partners, the London-based credit firm pledging $300 million to rescue LIV on the basis the league can secure a “requisite” number of player commitments before an initial October 25 deadline.

Golf.title: Recent Tour Winner Among Three First-Round Withdrawals From DP World India Championship
Golf.summary: Open de España winner Grant Forrest was one of three players to pull out of the DP World Tour event at Delhi Golf Club prior to the second round beginning
bullets: Recent Open de España winner Grant Forrest is one of three players to withdraw from the DP World India Championship before round two. A Tour spokesperson confirmed his withdrawal was due to injury, after he shot a six-over 78 on Thursday. It is the second time since August that he has pulled out of an event. His Madrid win ended a run of nine missed cuts in 12 starts and earned him places at the 2027 Masters and Open Championship.

England's Andy Sullivan, a four-time Tour winner, withdrew through illness after a seven-over 79. Australia's Anthony Quayle also withdrew through injury, having missed 16 cuts in 25 starts and sitting just inside the Race to Dubai top 150, with only the top 100 retaining full status. Niklas Norgaard of Denmark leads after a 66 (-6), in a round disrupted by storms that cost around five hours of play.
Golf.copy:
Recent Open de España champion Grant Forrest is one of three players to have withdrawn from this week's DP World India Championship prior to round two. Forrest completed a memorable victory in Madrid just days ago, bringing an end to a woeful run of form in 2026 which saw him miss nine of his previous 12 cuts before lifting the trophy.

As a result of his success, he earned spots at The Masters and The Open Championship in 2027 while securing his future at the top level for at least a couple more seasons. However, for the second time since August, Forrest ended up pulling out of a tour event.

bullets: Charles Howell III has reportedly decided to leave LIV Golf ahead of the 2027 season, according to Sports Business Journal. The 47-year-old American joined in the first wave in 2022 and played in Bryson DeChambeau's Crushers team for four seasons. His contract expired this season and he is not interested in committing to LIV 2.0. His best LIV result was the individual title at Mayakoba, Mexico, in February 2023, when he shot a final-round 63 to finish three shots clear of Peter Uihlein.

Existing players have a soft deadline of 25 October to confirm whether they will continue. LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September, and London-based credit firm BC Partners is willing to inject $300m. The Financial Times reported that LIV hopes to run 17 events in 2027, with fields of at least 75 players. Jon Rahm, Adrian Meronk, David Puig, Abraham Ancer and Thomas Pieters have also signalled they will leave. Only Richard Bland, Victor Perez and Cameron Tringale have publicly said they will stay. Golf.copy:
Charles Howell III has become the latest player to decide to part ways with LIV Golf ahead of the 2027 season, according to a report. The American was among the first wave of players recruited by the breakaway tour in 2022 and has spent the past four seasons competing alongside Bryson DeChambeau in the Crushers quartet.

But the three-time PGA Tour winner reportedly has no interest in extending his stay with LIV Golf, according to Sports Business Journal. The publication reported on Thursday that Howell's contract expired this season and he wasn't interested in committing to LIV 2.0.

Golf.title: Will Man City FFP saga revive Super League talk? LIV Golf used as warning as Danny Mills explains why superstar players will favour ‘knighthoods’ over money
Golf.summary: Will Man City FFP saga revive Super League talk? LIV Golf used as warning as Danny Mills explains why superstar players will favour ‘knighthoods’ over money Goal.com
Golf.copy:
- Super League plans faced fierce backlash from fans Back in the spring of 2021, it was revealed that 12 heavyweight outfits had agreed to form their own competition - with the plan being to welcome 20 teams into that pack. Premier League giants City, Liverpool, Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham were all involved. The so-called ‘Big Six’ faced serious backlash from supporters, with the proposals eventually being ripped up. The shadow of a Super League has, however, continued to loom large - with the likes of Real Madrid and Juventus refusing to scrap the plans entirely. Part of the problem for those considering a severing of ties with UEFA and FIFA is that any player on their books would no longer be eligible to represent their respective countries in international tournaments - which would make it difficult for transfers to be agreed. There would, however, be greater freedom when it comes to recruitment, with FFP and PSR regulations being removed. That would allow the likes of City, and other teams with super wealthy owners, to splash the cash as they see fit. Those at the Etihad Stadium are currently locked in an FFP battle that sees 114 charges hanging over the blue half of Manchester and the harshest of punishments being mooted. If City decided that they no longer wanted to dance to the Premier League’s tune, and that of the Football Association, could they be tempted to enter back into Super League construction discussions?

- Getty Why players would be against a European Super League When that question was put to Mills, the former City defender - who was speaking in association with Gambling.com, the guide to the best online casinos - told GOAL: “It's very, very difficult. “I've had this discussion many, many times. To play international football, FIFA have to ratify your competition. So if FIFA don't ratify your Super League, none of those players can play in international competition. “Now, as much as we think players favour club over country, when it comes to World Cups, European Championships, you win the Premier League, you win the Champions League, you're a legend at your football club, a legend in your city. You win the World Cup, you win the Euros, you're a legend of your country, you get knighthoods, it's there forever. “If I said to you now, who won the Champions League in 2017? You probably don't know without looking it up. There's a limit to the impact that has. But if I said name all those countries who won the World Cups, you can pretty much list them. You know who they are. “So I don't think the Super League will ever have legs in that way. Saudi have kind of tried it, it hasn't really worked. China tried it before, that didn't really work. You're always going to need competition. And the best players will still always want to play international football.”
Golf.skip_reason: Football/Man City FFP piece; not sports business, sponsored opinion

Golf.title: 'Tightest golf course I've ever played': Pros face suffocating test this week
Golf.summary: The field at this week’s DP World India Championship are battling a different kind of test in the Lodhi Course at Delhi Golf Club. The post ‘Tightest golf course I’ve ever played’: Pros face suffocating test this week appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Patrick Reed, Rory McIlroy, Thomas Detry and Tommy Fleetwood are among the players facing the Lodhi Course at Delhi Golf Club, host of this week's DP World India Championship. The course measures only 6,912 yards but has doglegs, pinched landing zones, thick rough and fairways lined by jungle and Mughal-era ruins. Detry swapped his driver for a 3-iron and shot a five-under 67 in the rain-shortened first round, one behind Niklas Norgaard. Only about half the field finished the round.

McIlroy also left his driver out of the bag, saying his best chance of winning lay in keeping it there. Fleetwood, who won the inaugural event last year at 22 under for his eighth DP World Tour title, shot a two-under 70 on Thursday. He said the rough is more penal this year and compared it to a U.S. Open. Reed said the narrow fairways mean a missed fairway is effectively a reload, and that the course feels like an irons-only test.
Golf.copy:
Patrick Reed has made 448 starts in his professional golf career, from California to Qatar to Kawagoe (that’s in Japan) — and everywhere in between. But even for the well-traveled Masters champ, this week’s stop is a new one.

“Never come around a golf course like this before,” he said Wednesday. “It’s one of those that it’s completely different than I would expect.” Reed was referencing the Lodhi Course at Delhi Golf Club, site of this week’s DP World India Championship. The course plays just 6,912 yards all stretched out, but is tighter than a 15-handicapper playing Augusta National with Tiger Woods. Doglegs. Pinched landing zones. Ball-gobbling rough. Fairways lined by jungle and Mughal-era ruins. You name it, DGC throws it at all comers.

Golf.title: Getting your kid into golf? Here are 3 things every parent should know
Golf.summary: GOLF Teacher to Watch James Hong has three key pieces of advice for any parent of a child who is getting into golf. The post Getting your kid into golf? Here are 3 things every parent should know appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Your child just attended a junior golf camp this past summer, and now they’re hooked. Registration for local fall junior programs has opened, and you want to take advantage. Pretty soon, it’ll be the holidays, and it looks like junior clubs are on the wish list. Or maybe it’s been a couple of years since your child first picked up the game, and now they want to take it more seriously, perhaps even competing in tournaments.

So, what should you do now? What’s the next step? I get bombarded with these types of questions from parents all the time. What clubs should we get? What kind of program should we look into? Or simply, what’s next? Here are some answers to help point you in the right direction.

Golf.title: This year, my golf holiday wish list is all about the little things
Golf.summary: The holidays are coming up and the golfer in your life probably doesn't need another hat. Instead, grab them the things they need but hate buying. The post This year, my golf holiday wish list is all about the little things appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
For a guy who loves golf, but works in golf, the holidays can be tough on my family. They want to buy me fun, big, cool gear, but I’ve already got it all. Half the time, they’ve also got it themselves as I pass on the collection of items I am so lucky to collect in this role. However, there’s one thing we’ve started to agree on for the holidays: Buy me the stuff I hate buying myself.

Tees, gloves, golf balls, spikes, ball makers, repair tools and club brushes all make the list. Could I get these things for myself through the job? Sure. But that doesn’t mean I can get them quickly, and it never means that I have enough. A stockpile of these items, no matter how large it gets, is always going to hold a high value for me. Here’s a look at the small essentials I can’t get enough of, plus a few bonus items, because who doesn’t want to throw some nice things on a holiday wish list?

Golf.title: As Jon Rahm splits with LIV, what happens to his massive deal?
Golf.summary: Jon Rahm was reportedly owed more than $100 million from LIV Golf. Now that he's leaving the league, what happens to that deal? The post As Jon Rahm splits with LIV, what happens to his massive deal? appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Jon Rahm has reached a separation agreement with LIV Golf, which takes effect if Judge Michael B. Kaplan of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court of New Jersey approves it on 5 November. Rahm will then be free to play anywhere, and LIV will no longer have its largest unsecured creditor. The money still owed to him will be written off. That included $7.5m from a single period and reportedly more than $100m in current and future payments.

Rahm regains the rights to his name, image and likeness, including his "Rahmbo" logo and the Legion XIII logo, though he cannot use the Legion XIII mark in another golf league such as TGL. He gives up any equity in the Legion XIII team and any further claim against LIV. LIV is in Chapter 11 after Saudi PIF withdrew funding, and its lawyers expect to know by the end of the month whether to press on with "LIV 2.0" for 2027 or wind down. Rahm is expected to play the Abu Dhabi Championship that week and finish his season at the DP World Tour Championship.
Golf.copy:
The former World No. 1 reached a separation agreement with the breakaway league on Wednesday, marking a near-official end to his tenure less than three years after his high-profile signing. If and when the separation agreement is approved by Judge Michael B. Kaplan of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court of New Jersey on Nov. 5, Rahm will be free to play anywhere he can get a spot, while LIV will be free of its largest unsecured creditor.

The hundred-million-dollar question, then: what happens to the massive sums of money still owed to Rahm? LIV’s Chapter 11 bankruptcy filings revealed Rahm was owed $7.5 million just from a single period, a small percentage of what was reportedly more than $100 million in current and future payments left on his deal.

Golf.title: Scottie Scheffler's quiet act of kindness at his home club
Golf.summary: On GOLF's Subpar podcast, co-host Colt Knost relayed a story that reveals everything you need to know about Scottie Scheffer. The post Scottie Scheffler’s quiet act of kindness at his home club appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Scottie Scheffler surprised a junior club champion at Royal Oaks Country Club in Dallas, according to Colt Knost on GOLF's Subpar podcast. Knost played a friendly match there with the World No. 1, who gave him five shots. The match ended in a tie when Knost birdied the par-5 18th.

Before the 18th tee, Scheffler spotted a group of juniors on the driving range and asked whether one of them was the junior club champion. He gave the boy a high five and a hug and told him he was pleased to hear he had won. Knost said the gesture made the child's day. He added that it reflects Scheffler's off-course personality, which he said matches the one fans see on television.
Golf.copy:
Scottie Scheffler has made a habit of winning golf tournaments. He’s also pretty good at making someone’s day. On a recent episode of GOLF’s Subpar podcast, co-host Colt Knost provided a case in point. Knost was in Dallas recently, mostly for work but also for fun. That fun included a round with Scheffler at fabled Royal Oaks Country Club, where both grew up playing.

Knost can golf his ball but not like Scheffler, so it was only fitting that the World No. 1 gave his opponent five shots in a friendly match. Their amiable battle went back and forth, and ended in a tie when Knost birdied the par-5 18th.

Golf.title: She didn't grow up with golf. But now the game is her future
Golf.summary: The USGA's Pathways Launch internship program is designed to widen the pipeline of golf's next-generation workforce — and it's working. The post She didn’t grow up with golf. But now the game is her future appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Anna La, a 21-year-old University of Georgia senior who did not grow up playing golf, spent last summer on a three-month social-media internship with Callaway in Carlsbad, California. She got it through the USGA's Pathways Launch, which has just completed its first year. The programme placed 24 participants in summer roles at 10 organisations, including the LPGA, PGA of America, PGA Tour, Dick's Sporting Goods/Golf Galaxy, Golf Pride, Pebble Beach Company and Pinehurst Resort & Country Club.

The paid internships are jointly funded by the USGA and the host organisations. They aim to widen golf's workforce pipeline to people from underrepresented backgrounds. Of the first cohort, one participant was hired full-time by their host organisation, another received a similar offer, and two found jobs through programme connections. The USGA said more than 90 per cent of participants were encouraged to pursue a golf career. Applications for the 2027 programme are open, and La has won the Golf Writers Association of America scholarship for 2026-27.
Golf.copy:
Twenty-one-year-old Anna La grew up in Georgia without meaningful exposure to golf. Today, the University of Georgia senior is plotting a career in the game. La has blazed her unlikely trail thanks in large part to a three-month social-media internship with Callaway last summer — an opportunity fostered by the USGA’s Pathways Launch, a program that offers 24 participants summer gigs at 10 organizations across the golf industry.

Pathways Launch, which just completed its first year, is designed for graduate and undergraduate students seeking to work in golf or sports. The paid internships are funded jointly by both the USGA and the participating organizations, which include the LPGA, PGA of America and PGA Tour, Dick’s Sporting Goods/Golf Galaxy, Golf Pride, Pebble Beach Company and Pinehurst Resort & Country Club. Each organization offers positions that emphasize the development of on-the-job skills, mentorship and leadership training.

Golf.title: 7 Unwritten Women’s Golf Rules That Need To Disappear
Golf.summary: Why outdated traditions and poor pathways are driving beginners away, and how forward-thinking golf clubs can build retention
bullets: A Golf Monthly feature sets out seven unwritten rules at golf clubs that it argues hinder women who want to progress after trying the game. It says beginners are often steered towards full or five-day membership after only a few lessons, when a clear pathway to suit differing lifestyles is lacking.

The piece also calls for club professionals to teach etiquette in lessons so golfers do not learn by trial and error, and for an end to midweek-only ladies' days and male-dominated Saturday morning tee times. It argues for mixed play and open competitions across weekdays and weekends, noting that England Golf's 2026 workshops identify time, accessibility and value for money as major barriers.
Golf.copy:
When I speak to female non-golfers, there is still a huge amount of obvious stigma attached to the game that stops them from giving it a go. The usual excuses come up: “It takes all day,” “I can’t play golf until I’m retired,” and “It’s too expensive.”

For me, those are just standard excuses from anyone who isn’t yet interested in taking up the game. The real issues start once someone has tried golf, fallen in love with it, and wants to progress.

Golf.title: McKibbin one off lead in Delhi with McIlroy in contention
Golf.summary: Tom McKibbin is one shot off the lead and Rory McIlroy three further back after a weather-disrupted opening day of the DP World India Championship.

Golf.title: 'It's Actually Criminal'
Golf.summary: Seniors from the PGA Tour Champions have reacted angrily to news the $8m pension fund from the PGA Tour has been shut down
bullets: PGA Tour Champions is scrapping its $8m pension fund, president Miller Brady told players at a meeting, saying the senior tour will try to stand on its own financially. The pot had been $10m before being cut to $8m last year. The tour has $69m in prize money on offer this season.

Billy Andrade, David Toms and Scott McCarron criticised the decision, with Andrade calling it criminal and McCarron blaming PGA Tour leadership, including Jay Monahan and Brian Rolapp. The scheme dates to 1985, when $250,000 was allocated. Golf.copy:

Golf.title: Is This The Finest Course Close To Central London? I Think So
Golf.summary: This first-class course with impeccable pedigree is less than 10 miles from the Tower of London as the raven flies
Golf.copy:
Just a few miles from the heart of the capital, Royal Wimbledon Golf Club dates back to 1865 when play began over a seven-hole course. After a few years, this was expanded to a full 18 before the club was awarded its regal title in 1882. Many of its early members were influential in the evolution of The R&A, helped to inaugurate events such as the Amateur Championship and were involved in the creation of prestigious courses such as Royal St George's.

The club moved to Warren Farm and Caesar's Camp – an iron-age hill fort that skirts the 6th hole – in 1907, with Willie Park Junior masterminding the new layout. The great Harry Colt was a member, and he redesigned the course in 1924. Despite more recent changes to the 1st, 6th and 18th holes and some excellent bunker remodelling over the last few years by Tom Mackenzie, this is still fundamentally a Colt design and fully deserving of its place on the Golf Monthly Next 100 list.

He said the tour had been 'more than accommodating' to LIV players while it works on its strategic alliance with the PGA Tour and LIV is 'in such a state of flux'. Previously, players who paid fines could play most events and stay Ryder Cup eligible.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy is back in action this week at the 2026 DP World India Championship. There, he hopes to gain ground on Patrick Reed as he eyes his record-tying eighth Race to Dubai title.

A different topic, though, is hanging over the proceedings in India this week: the DP World Tour’s newly announced ban on LIV Golf players in 2027. On Wednesday morning, just two days after the tour announced its major LIV decision, McIlroy sat down for a press conference at Delhi Golf Club. Though his Race-to-Dubai chase did not come up while fielding reporters’ questions, the DP World Tour’s new anti-LIV rule did.

Golf.title: LIV Golf back in court for key hearing
Golf.summary: LIV Golf back in court for key hearing Sports Business Journal
bullets: LIV Golf has a Chapter 11 bankruptcy hearing in New Jersey on Wednesday, beginning at 1pm ET. It will seek court approval to terminate existing player contracts so it can proceed with LIV 2.0, including proposed player compensation and ownership structure. The plans include a 10-event schedule and purses second only to the PGA Tour globally.

Approval of LIV's restructuring support agreement with lead investor BC Partners would also let the league rehire employees and sign golf course agreements for 2027. The mid-October deadline to sign players has been extended to 25 October, and BC Partners can extend or waive it. The hearing follows news that the DP World Tour will no longer allow LIV players to be members, a major blow because European Ryder Cup hopefuls must be members. LIV says it remains on track with its player plans despite Jon Rahm's decision not to play LIV 2.0.
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf has its latest Chapter 11 bankruptcy hearing later Wednesday in New Jersey, and with it comes a number of milestones for the league as it tries to launch LIV 2.0. In the hearing, which begins at 1pm ET, LIV will be seeking court approval to terminate existing contracts with players so that it can move forward with various plans as part of LIV 2.0. Among those include proposed compensation for players, as well as player ownership structure. LIV has plans for a 10-event schedule, and purse sizes that rank second only to the PGA Tour globally.

The league initially had a mid-October deadline to sign players for LIV 2.0, but that now has been extended to Oct. 25. And BC Partners, the league’s lead investor, has the right to extend or even waive that deadline. Even with Jon Rahm’s decision not to play LIV 2.0, the league has maintained that it is on track with its player plans for its next iteration.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy Is Right About The LIV Golf Failure
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy Is Right About The LIV Golf Failure Yahoo Sports
bullets: Rory McIlroy told the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi that LIV Golf "had probably half of a good idea that was executed pretty poorly". He said the league could have used its money better than enriching tour pros who were already well paid. LIV filed for bankruptcy protection in September after cancelling its season finale in Michigan, though $300m from BC Partners offers some hope.

Unpaid prize money and appearance fees totalled more than $45m at the time of filing. Jon Rahm tops the unsecured creditors with a $7.5m claim, and Cameron Smith is fourth with more than $4.8m owed. Joost Luiten said returning players should face a harder route back, and the DP World Tour is introducing a rule to ban LIV 2.0 signees from the 2027 season.
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf is collapsing because it lacked a smart plan for its massive wealth. The league filed for bankruptcy protection in September after canceling its season finale in Michigan. While some hope remains due to $300 million from BC Partners, the fundamental strategy failed to hold the golf world together.

Rory McIlroy believes the league's leadership missed the mark on how to use their funds. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, McIlroy said, "LIV had probably half of a good idea that was executed pretty poorly." The PGA Tour loyalist noted that the league had plenty of money but wasted it. According to Fox Sports, McIlroy stated, "They certainly could have done better things with it instead of just enriching tour pros that were already making a lot of money."

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy has lost friends over LIV Golf – but the next big move is dividing his rivals
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy has lost friends over LIV Golf – but the next big move is dividing his rivals Today's Golfer
bullets: Rory McIlroy said he has drifted from some players who joined LIV Golf, particularly former European Ryder Cup team-mates. Speaking at a Bloomberg conference in New Delhi before the DP World India Championship, he said a difference of opinion over golf's future was not a reason to lose friends, but they stopped seeing each other once those players were ineligible for the Ryder Cup and the majors. He described LIV as a "half good idea poorly executed" and no longer a threat as it tries to relaunch and survive bankruptcy.

The next question is how returning players are reintegrated. The PGA Tour appears set on a one-year ban, while the DP World Tour must balance star names against its current members. Eddie Pepperell said the tour must handle the return of 15 to 20 LIV players across the season carefully. Joost Luiten said it should be made harder for them to return. McIlroy acknowledged loyal members might feel hard done by, but said he would vote for the players to return because it is good for business.
Golf.copy:
The avalanche of chaos that arrived with LIV Golf strained not only on professional relationships but also personal ones. Rory McIlroy, who said long ago he “hated” the LIV product as a staunch defender of the PGA Tour, admits he has drifted from a handful players who defected to the breakaway league.

The Masters champion most notably had a fallout with Sergio Garcia and at one stage was branded “immature” by the Spaniard. The pair seem to have reconciled, but there was also a war of words recently with Lee Westwood, who claimed McIlroy’s comments about the value of LIV players were “not thought out” and “typical Rory”.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy welcomes back LIV Golf rivals as exodus continues
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy welcomes back LIV Golf rivals as exodus continues bunkered.co.uk
bullets: Rory McIlroy said he would vote to let LIV Golf players return to the DP World Tour and PGA Tour, telling Bloomberg ahead of the DP World India Championship that "a rising tide lifts all boats". He said LIV had "half of a good idea that was executed pretty poorly", with much of its capital wasted instead of being used to partner with governing bodies. LIV lost the support of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund earlier this year and filed for bankruptcy protection last month.

Players leaving LIV include its No.1 player Jon Rahm and fellow Spaniard David Puig, with Adrian Meronk, Abraham Ancer and Joaquin Niemann also reportedly following. Rahm will most likely have to spend a season on the DP World Tour before returning to the PGA Tour in 2028. McIlroy said he and Tiger Woods probably had the most to lose when LIV emerged in 2022, given their PGA Tour ties and the launch of TGL. He added that he has grown less close to some former European Ryder Cup team-mates.

Rory McIlroy has been a long-time critic of LIV Golf, but the six-time major champion is ready to welcome the league’s players back to the DP World Tour and PGA Tour.

Having lost the support of the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia (PIF) earlier this year, those at LIV – who filed for bankruptcy protection last month – are battling to keep the league alive.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy makes Tiger Woods admission with latest thoughts on LIV Golf
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy makes Tiger Woods admission with latest thoughts on LIV Golf Golfmagic
bullets: Rory McIlroy said he would support the return of players who defected to LIV Golf, telling Bloomberg in New Delhi that the league "had probably half of a good idea that was executed pretty poorly". He said LIV's capital was partly wasted on enriching tour pros who were already well paid, when it could have partnered with governing bodies. LIV is fighting to survive Chapter 11 bankruptcy after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew. It has a $300m investment from BC Partners, and players have until 25 October to commit.

McIlroy said he and Tiger Woods "had the most to lose" when LIV launched in 2022, as they were about to start TGL, which required PGA Tour membership. He said some players who went to LIV were therefore lost to TGL. He also said he had grown apart from some former European Ryder Cup team-mates, not because of their differing views but because they no longer played the same events. The DP World Tour has said players who commit to LIV's 2027 season cannot keep their membership.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy has admitted he rallied so hard against LIV Golf in the beginning because he and Tiger Woods had more to lose. The six-time major champion has now revealed he would support the return of players who defected to the Saudi-backed circuit, insisting the breakaway league no longer represents the same threat to professional golf as it did when it first launched in 2022.

McIlroy has been one of LIV Golf's most vocal opponents since its formation, but recent developments have raised further questions about the league's long-term future. LIV Golf is fighting for its future and, despite securing a $300m investment from BC Partners, continues to face uncertainty.
